desktop:c897f1edefa804911081.source: The USB track list shows each track's key before its title. Green fits the master deck. Amber fits but is detuned.

desktop:b09898033efca39d6f1f.source: SORT and COLUMN sit above the USB track list and open the native sort menu. KEY FORMAT picks Classic or Camelot keys and is saved on each USB.

desktop:1d7722b963da944a8b69.source: Changing stem rows or stem levels no longer freezes BROWSE.

desktop:bc142a749cc1aeb73be0.source: Create or edit a DJ profile on the XZ. Type the DJ name and a tagline with the encoder or by touch, pick a logo image from the USB, then save it to USB 1 or USB 2.

desktop:eb5050f64c1f80c9bc4c.source: A folder named after the DJ inside DJPROFILE, with a logo in it, now counts as a profile. Profiles without their own color use the USB's rekordbox color.

desktop:d70adc8e8c23ef48f59f.source: The MODS header shows the DJ profile from your USB with its logo and name. Tap it to switch between the profiles on both USBs. Nothing is stored on the XZ.

desktop:80ec1092581723ad8c5a.source: The XZ also plays stems prepared in the AZ MODS and RX3 formats. On four-stem tracks pad D mutes bass. Sets that do not match the track are refused and the original audio plays. Not yet tested on an XZ.

desktop:e350578d51283f9635e5.source: Every game works without the touchscreen. The encoder moves and selects, BACK steps back and REKORDBOX returns to MODS. DJ VIEW on the Beat Arcade pause screen now returns to the deck.

desktop:5e6cd1773c76ce7e6bcb.source: MODS opens on GENERAL, which lists the main features in one place. A feature that needs setup opens a short page that detects it, enables it and has you test it on a deck.

desktop:3e7d27708f6b00c8cdd2.source: Each deck shows its original key, playing key and cents in the beat countdown area. Linked decks show MASTER and SYNC. Turn KEY FEEDBACK off to get the stock countdown back.

desktop:72519394feb2cf238e20.source: SHIFT + SYNC shifts the key of a deck to match the master deck. KEY SETUP checks both tracks and the master before it turns on.

desktop:6bc4754f8a79a1df0d68.source: Pressing MASTER TEMPO while Key Sync is on returns that deck to its original key. Master Tempo stays on, and the next press works as stock.

desktop:a532f34b42d05679ec9b.source: Every MODS page has a BACK button, and the physical BACK button steps back one page.

desktop:0272f2f7a88de75f9638.source: The MODS menu has a section rail on the left and an info box that explains the selected control and shows whether your change was saved.

desktop:fa80adf626b287e6ef9c.source: MODS works without the touchscreen. The REKORDBOX key opens and closes it, the browse encoder moves between controls and a push selects. Turn REKORDBOX KEY off to get the stock key back.

desktop:3c36906283532e5dace0.source: Experimental. With rekordbox in PERFORMANCE mode on a computer, the onscreen stem buttons switch that track's stems. Showing the computer track's 3-band waveform on the XZ needs a companion program on the computer and the XZ network connection. It was seen once in a test capture and has not been confirmed by watching a deck.

desktop:5cbc74e8730f1082a13d.source: RAM TRACKS copies the playing track into memory, with its prepared stems when there is room, so it keeps playing after USB STOP. One track per deck, up to 64 MB. This is experimental. Keeping the title and waveform on screen after the USB leaves is not confirmed yet.

desktop:5d4bdd1908ce5143be80.source: RHYTHM LAB adds ten short rhythm studies by VJ OpticMystic for the jogs and pads. They are prototypes, and you can rate each one.

desktop:919df758644afb5e7ad6.source: Pulling the USB, or loading one without settings, keeps your current settings. The XZ remembers your last settings and restores them when it starts without a USB. The footer says SAVED TO USB or NOT SAVED after each change.

desktop:33405621a749aed79e3e.source: Settings saved by an older loader no longer turn your Off choices, such as KEY FEEDBACK or the 3-band waveform, back On.

desktop:0a43b2739fde6355c0c2.source: STATIC SURFER is a rhythm platformer by VJ OpticMystic. Tap to jump and tilt the jog to pass through the glyphs.

desktop:e765e716b60384a25044.source: Pick a color for drums, harmonics and vocals, or let the theme choose. Drums are now blue and harmonics red by default. Stem rows, pad lights and the STEMS waveform all follow the choice.

desktop:65eb47f12892c90f0763.source: Muting stems on both decks does less audio work per block. This targets the distortion heard when muting stems on two decks. It is not yet confirmed on an XZ.

desktop:59f298f96d3455bd2294.source: MODS › GENERAL › STEM SETTINGS › STEM ORDER

desktop:b591f22276ddd0f560dc.source: STEM ORDER sets the left to right order of drums, harmonics and vocals. The stem rows, pads A, B and C and their lights follow it. It saves to your USB.

desktop:4432f9e52822e0d58ba3.source: The STEMS button cycles five stem row layouts. Rows can be full or half height, below the waveforms or at the outer edges, or hidden. Each stem button fills left to right with its level.

desktop:12cf7bd242ae170bfd1e.source: METRICS shows CPU, RAM and chip temperature next to STEMS and MODS. It is off by default. The temperature turns yellow at 80 C and flashes red at 90 C.

desktop:c2c0a9e07120cc28b8d6.source: APPS runs XZ SDK apps from the USB, when you tap RUN or each time the USB goes in. DJ controls keep working while an app runs.

desktop:1b0a405d86a32fb410b0.source: The Wave Rider board answers the jog faster in the air, and spinning back brakes it sooner.

desktop:d5c66a359822409e6b5c.source: The jog now sets the Wave Rider board's angle. Nose down gains speed and nose up launches. You can calibrate your jog and remap the action button.

desktop:88e8a31f29bf425c8dc3.source: Wave Rider has EASY, NORMAL and HARD. EASY is the default and holds the air angle you set. Clean landings show the points they earned.

desktop:d386f4bcd3ef8707293f.source: Spin the jog in the air to flip the Wave Rider board, then land level to bank flips and crests. Three perfect landings in a row light a rocket. Three new worlds use VJ OpticMystic's artwork.

desktop:fcbf00caf0df5875f9df.source: Wave Rider is now hill surfing. The loaded track's waveform becomes the hills, and two players can ride co-op or versus on the two jogs.

desktop:a102ba97fe6d5ff7d892.source: Small jog turns now tilt the Wave Rider ship instead of spinning it, and CUE adds weight on the slopes. SPIN LIFT is an optional quick jog spin near a crest.

desktop:4c9f04ccdc6ff73b3e46.source: The loading artwork and MODS screens show xzmods.com.

desktop:bb33f897697740d3a917.source: What SYNC 3, BPM 1, LIMIT and EXT MASTER mean

desktop:d5db97f97fc727f8fe10.source: SYNC 1 to SYNC 4: SYNC is on and follows that deck. BPM 1 to BPM 4: only the tempo follows, because QUANTIZE is off, a track has no beat grid, a loop is running, or the beat position is not available. LIMIT: the master tempo is out of reach, so the deck keeps its last tempo. EXT MASTER: a LINK player is master, which decks 3 and 4 cannot follow. NO BPM: analyse the track in your DJ software.

manual:8c4a0bf0fd4a0b3a95de.source: The XZ Mods app runs on your computer. It puts XZ Mods on a USB, makes stems for your tracks, makes your DJ profile, keeps the app and your USB up to date, holds tools for your library, games and the XZ screen, and sends your reports and ideas to the maintainer. It never formats a drive and never changes your music or the library your DJ software exported.

manual:44747ca2968b85ca6fd6.source: Four decks adds two software players, DECK 3 and DECK 4, to the XDJ-XZ's own DECK 1 and DECK 2. You hear them on mixer channels CH3 and CH4. A short USB cable from the back of the player to a top USB port carries their sound into the mixer: it leaves through a top USB port and comes back in at the rear USB socket, where a computer with DJ software would connect. The physical controls switch between decks with the same presses DJ software uses on the XDJ-XZ.

manual:452cd05ad2516ee0db77.source: What XZ Mods changes on the XDJ-XZ, what you need, and your first start from a prepared USB.

manual:1ae5debbd341fb1d9a70.source: XZ Mods is software for the XDJ-XZ that starts from a USB stick. It adds a MODS menu, stems you can mute live, custom beat jump, four decks over a loopback cable, DJ profiles, themes and games. It can also replace the whole play screen with its own MODERN interface.

manual:1f91ed3d8e0e7b1b5932.source: XZ Mods runs in the player's memory. It never writes to the player's firmware, so the XDJ-XZ itself stays stock.

manual:7b68ac1ef3c13bda1c23.source: ) from the USB at start and runs XZ Mods from there.

manual:ca5690f7dffa16afd97c.source: Your music, the library your DJ software exported and your playlists stay as they are. XZ Mods adds its own folders beside them.

manual:81262aa590f19e5b4a21.source: The player's own settings are still there. Hold

manual:4da5ab19b4fda000ae3d.source: to open UTILITY, exactly as on a stock XDJ-XZ.

manual:e413605e356faa13da64.source: Settings you change in MODS are saved on the USB, so they travel with it to another XZ running XZ Mods.

manual:892128c0d95b90503308.source: There is no save button in MODS. Every change saves on its own to the settings USB, the stick you browse. The settings live in the VJ.Tools folder on that stick, so they travel with you to another XZ running XZ Mods. When you browse a stick, the player takes that stick's settings. A stick with no settings, or with damaged ones, leaves the current settings as they are.

manual:9ca4cfc91ded7d36129c.source: The XZ also remembers the last settings it applied. If you start it with no stick, it uses them.

manual:66f696237305f7717178.source: The large key in each deck's column is the key the deck plays right now. Tempo with MASTER TEMPO off, a key shift and KEY SYNC all move it. Its colour compares it with the master deck's key. Green means it mixes with the master's key: the same key, its relative major or minor, or one step away on the key wheel, tuned within 25 cents of the master. Amber means it would mix, but it is detuned by more than 25 cents. White means neither, and the master deck itself is always white. Turn KEY MATCH COLOURS off in

manual:4b45f755233eeba4c440.source: and every key is white. The cents beside it show how far it sits off the semitone, so you can match by ear. Once the playing key leaves the track's analysed key, ORIGINAL shows the analysed key below it.

manual:5cced1da3c9c850e24cc.source: on the top bar. Open it to see deck 3 and 4 audio render times and active key shifters across all four decks. P99 is the time at or below which 99% of the last 256 rendered blocks finished; MAX is the longest. Short blocks are scaled to a full block. D3+D4 MAX adds both maxima and compares them with the 5,805 microseconds available per block. New shifts use a stricter 3,483 microsecond budget, leaving time for other work. These render numbers include decoding, time stretch and key shift; they do not measure the complete output path. Use them when you suspect the player is working hard, for example with stems on both decks and four decks running.

manual:d259013f539558442cab.source: XZ Mods keeps its settings on your USB, so they travel with you from player to player. This page explains where they are kept and what happens when the USB changes, then lists every setting with its values, its default and the chapter that explains it.

manual:f90690b6ddee9b2cf712.source: . You change them in MODS, or on your computer with the

manual:82a15ebdc927c91528f5.source: . There is no save button. Every change saves on its own to the USB you are browsing, and the bottom of the MODS page says what happened for a few seconds.

manual:5968bdff290bf0f07ca2.source: The player follows the same rules as its own MY SETTINGS:

manual:5895a21bf3660ee1e80b.source: Browsing a USB in USB 1 or USB 2 loads that USB's settings. Browsing a computer or a LINK source never changes them.

manual:a77d07adf9d9cdd3ae18.source: A USB without settings, or with settings the player cannot read, leaves your current settings as they are. Nothing resets to defaults in the middle of a set.

manual:464a98682d65b72e12aa.source: The player remembers the last settings it used. Started without a USB, it uses those. A USB with its own settings takes over again once you browse it.

manual:9386791dedb022948a0a.source: The player's own MY SETTINGS, which your DJ software writes to the USB, are a separate set. XZ Mods settings never change them, and loading MY SETTINGS does not change XZ Mods settings.

manual:af68d456b1f04bb2fe86.source: MODERN's own display choices are settings too: its waveform colour, waveform position and zoom, how it writes keys, the TRACK COLOURS choice, the LAMPS AND TITLES and BYPASS BUTTON switches, and the columns of its track list. So are the 3-band colours. They are saved to the USB with everything else and come back after the player restarts.

manual:b4cbf7b4c7f2963bd169.source: Things you do during a set, such as muting a stem, BYPASS, a key shift, KEY SYNC or a RAM copy, are not settings. They start fresh every time the player starts.

manual:1a5f0ebe5bfd39cfaf54.source: There is no single button that resets every setting. Set each one back in MODS, using the Default column below. Some pages have their own way back: PAGE 1: STOCK for beat jump page 1, RESET STEM COLORS for the stem colours, and RESET 3-BAND COLOURS for the 3-band colours.

manual:f3b92a6a1f393f5d71f2.source: Deleting the settings file from the USB does not reset anything. The player keeps the settings it has, and saves them to the USB again with your next change.

manual:1ec5495f3196f2b8e8c7.source: XZ Mods keeps a short diagnostic diary in

manual:8098edcd4aeb8e55512f.source: on each mounted USB stick, including music sticks. If a problem happens during a set, keep those sticks so you can include their diaries in a later report.

manual:a82d804449cbb8d48f17.source: The diary records the XZ Mods version, settings fingerprint, USB slots, interface, deck view, state changes and fixed notice codes. It also records available CPU, memory, audio, SYNC, key-processing and USB-read measurements. It never records track titles, music paths, serial numbers or network identities. A missing measurement stays unknown.

manual:b1824ff31849e5841776.source: Each stick holds at most 4 MiB of diary files. Older segments are replaced first, and the previous session's latest segment is kept when a new session starts. Writing pauses during track loads, RAM copies and heavy USB reads. No diary is created on a read-only stick or when less than 64 MiB of free space plus a small write reserve remains. Read-only test sessions save nothing. Normal USB-loader sessions write diary entries when these conditions allow it. Long busy periods and removal can leave gaps.

manual:eeaeeea825c3d1163539.source: The diary stays on the sticks. Nothing is sent until you choose to include it in a report.

manual:543fbba26449863f42b2.source: When something goes wrong, send a report. It helps fix the problem for everyone.

manual:a445fa3667ce5747cf87.source: beside an error in the dock. Choose a topic, add words if you like, and send. Offline, the report waits on the stick for your computer. See

manual:5d46ad9c98b52a1ced23.source: at the top right and choose

manual:c1a04feeb924c7fe25e7.source: . Only one box is required, and

manual:ff78472b4e4e7ee7df50.source: Every screen, control and setting XZ Mods adds to the XDJ-XZ. Pick your interface at the top and the manual shows only what applies to you.

manual:511c2ab701d9001219c3.source: XZ Mods can draw the whole play screen: bigger waveforms, a browse sidebar and stem buttons. CLASSIC keeps the player's own screen.

manual:c46ed4f347e82816510b.source: Mute vocals, harmonics and drums live from the pads or the screen. BYPASS brings back the whole track.

manual:4393c0158f1110b22bbc.source: Decks 3 and 4 play on mixer channels CH3 and CH4, over one short USB cable from the back of the player to the top.

manual:5be1fed37911180e7193.source: Two pages of jump sizes you choose, from 1 beat to 64 bars, on all four decks.

manual:7636f897d8b3bf74546f.source: Move a deck's key a semitone at a time, or match it to the master deck with SHIFT + SYNC.

manual:36c6c195cb1a7eba99da.source: Copy a track into the player's memory, so the deck keeps playing if the music USB goes out.

manual:dccd58e99152814ca122.source: 25 themes, waveform colours, your own 3-band colours and key notation.

manual:97bf277e516d40f7890f.source: Everything XZ Mods can change, in one menu on the player. Every change saves to your USB.

manual:0e2f5512d9122f89dc80.source: Your name and logo on the player, carried on your USB.

manual:e8055eb9af619475245f.source: Prepare the USB, make stems and watch the XZ screen live on your computer.

manual:8feaf1a9b3a9f2488abc.source: XZ Mods runs in the player's memory. It never writes to the player's firmware, so the XDJ-XZ itself stays stock. Hold MENU for a second Push ROTARY SELECTOR Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Press BACK The player picks up the XZ Mods loader ( autoexec.bin ) from the USB at start and runs XZ Mods from there. Your music, the library your DJ software exported and your playlists stay as they are. XZ Mods adds its own folders beside them. The player's own settings are still there. Hold MENU to open UTILITY, exactly as on a stock XDJ-XZ. Settings you change in MODS are saved on the USB, so they travel with it to another XZ running XZ Mods.

manual:46b0596cbd52351af0d3.source: Switch the player off. Start it without the XZ Mods USB, or with a USB that has no autoexec.bin on it. The player starts stock. Plug the XZ Mods USB back in and start again to load XZ Mods. If you play from a separate music stick, that stick works on the stock player as before.

manual:fd6ef40a28fcbdda0e35.source: Item What you need Player XDJ-XZ on firmware 1.26. No other firmware version is supported Computer 64-bit Windows with WebView2, or a Mac with macOS 14 or later, to prepare the USB Stems Made on a Windows computer or an Apple silicon Mac. An Intel Mac can import stems made elsewhere USB A USB stick for the loader. It can be your music USB, or a separate loader stick Four decks A USB-B to USB-A cable. See Four decks experimental The app downloads the official firmware it needs from the manufacturer and checks it. No firmware or boot files come with the XZ Mods download. Caution XZ Mods is a preview. Test every new USB at home before you use it in a set.

manual:95c69dc8cea7f779279a.source: You prepare the USB in the XZ Mods app on your computer. It does not format the drive or touch your music. Install the XZ Mods app and open it. Plug in your USB. The app finds it and opens it. With several USBs plugged in, choose yours from the list. Choose Install XZ Mods . Follow the short guide: your DJ profile, the screen the XZ starts with, then a checklist of what it will write. Back returns to the step before. Choose Write to USB , then Eject USB . The checklist before the write. Music, playlists and prepared stems are never touched. Loader XZ Mods itself. Games Free games the app downloads and checks. Interface The screen the XZ starts with. Write to USB Writes everything in the checklist. Every step of the app is in The XZ Mods app . To add stems to your tracks, see Stems .

manual:1219da555d2d3b0da143.source: Press BROWSE Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise Press LOAD 1 Press BACK Press MENU Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to SCREEN and push it Tap CLASSIC Tap MODERN Press MENU Plug the USB into USB 1 or USB 2 on the top of the XDJ-XZ. Switch the player on. Wait for XZ Mods to start. Load a track as usual and check it plays. Press MENU on the play screen, or touch MODS at the top right, to open the MODS menu. HOME is the first page. If you use a separate loader stick, keep it in until XZ Mods has started. Keep the USB with your music and stems in while you play.

manual:ba3b20a68c74d25011dc.source: MODERN draws the whole play screen. The player's controls work as before, and the top bar adds a few buttons. The MODERN play screen with a track on each deck. MODS Opens the MODS menu, like a short press of MENU. STEMS Shows or hides the stem rows. DECKS Chooses two or four decks. Deck lanes One waveform lane per deck, with its source and key. Deck panel The track, time, tempo and BPM of each deck. The rest of the play screen is in The play screen .

manual:9d76e64d0a12e7056dda.source: CLASSIC keeps the player's own play screen and adds MODS to it. Touch MODS at the top right, or press MENU , to open the menu. A classic theme can restyle the screen. See Screen, interfaces and themes . Press the button above LINK Press the button above LINK

manual:e1873f68ef8e6b6aaad3.source: The XZ starts in the interface saved on the USB. You choose it in the app before the first start, and you can change it on the player at any time. Nothing else changes when you switch. Your settings, stems and decks stay as they are. Interface What you see MODERN XZ Mods draws the whole screen: bigger waveforms, a browse sidebar and a stems row with mute buttons. Marked Beta in the app CLASSIC The player's own play screen, with MODS added. Classic themes can restyle it A new USB starts in MODERN unless you choose the standard interface in the app. Choose the screen the XZ shows. New interface is MODERN, Standard XDJ-XZ interface is CLASSIC. New interface MODERN. Standard XDJ-XZ interface CLASSIC.

manual:40b5d8098887ca8374ad.source: There are two ways to switch. Press the button above LINK . Out of the box it switches between MODERN and CLASSIC, and the screen says which one you are in. You can give it another job in PLAY › BUTTON ABOVE LINK . Open MODS, go to SCREEN and choose CLASSIC or MODERN under INTERFACE . Press the button above LINK Press the button above LINK Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap CLASSIC Tap MODERN INTERFACE is the first choice on the SCREEN page. INTERFACE The interface the XZ shows. The change saves to the USB. CLASSIC The player's own screen with MODS. MODERN The full-screen XZ Mods layout. THEME The classic theme. See Screen, interfaces and themes. Explanation What the highlighted choice does. Save state Confirms the change is saved to the USB. Tip You can always reach MODS with the hardware alone. In CLASSIC, the button above LINK takes you to MODERN, where MENU opens MODS, and the encoder and BACK drive it.

manual:131e30bce24aa9dd62a8.source: There are two things to update, and they update separately. Press MENU Tap CONNECT Tap UPDATES Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise What How The app on your computer On Windows the app checks at launch and offers the update. On a Mac, download the new version from the release page. See App updates XZ Mods on your USB Open the USB in the app. When it says Update available , choose Update USB . The app backs up the old loader first XZ Mods over the network Send the update from the app and download it on the player. See Updates over the network experimental Caution Updating the app does not change the USB. After an app update, open the USB page and choose Update USB . Music, your exported library and your saved settings stay in place through an update. A USB built with Keep this version on the USB stays on its build and ignores network updates. See XZ Mods version . If something does not work after an update, see Messages and troubleshooting .

manual:c79c73a8217cff738cfb.source: The picture shows the XDJ-XZ from straight above, rendered from a true-scale model of the player. The XDJ-XZ from above: the browse section with the touch screen at the top centre, a deck on each side and the four-channel mixer under the screen. Touch screen Shows the play screen in the interface you chose (MODERN or CLASSIC) and the MODS menu. Every MODS control also answers touch. MENU (UTILITY) Press: opens MODS where the screen has no MENU job of its own. Hold: opens the player's own UTILITY, as on a stock XDJ-XZ. BACK Goes up one level, in MODS too. Rotary selector Turn to move the highlight in MODS, push to select. It drives every MODS page, so you never need the touch screen. SHORTCUT Opens the SHORTCUT screen as on a stock player. A short MENU on that screen opens MODS. Button above LINK The media button directly above LINK. XZ Mods lets you choose what it does, alone and with SHIFT. LINK Its stock job. It can also switch the VJ.Tools view on and off. TIME MODE and DECK QUANTIZE Stock on decks 1 and 2. While a side drives deck 3 or 4 they also reach the software decks. LOAD 1, LOAD 2 Load into the deck that side controls now: deck 1 or 3 on the left, deck 2 or 4 on the right. Left deck Controls deck 1, or deck 3 after you press SHIFT twice. Right deck Controls deck 2, or deck 4 after you press SHIFT twice. Mixer channels 3 1 2 4 Decks 3 and 4 play through CH3 and CH4 over the loopback cable.

manual:1bea4525184f9fc0091e.source: Open SOURCE ( BACK at the top of a list) Press MENU Press MENU Press INFO Press MENU Press BACK Press MENU Press SHORTCUT Press MENU Press MENU Hold MENU for a second Press BACK Key Action with XZ Mods MENU press Opens MODS on the play screen, the SOURCE screen, the INFO screen and the SHORTCUT screen experimental . Everywhere else it keeps its stock job. In MODS it closes MODS. MENU hold Opens the player's own UTILITY, in both interfaces. BACK Goes up one level. In MODS it steps from an open item to its page, then to the section rail. TURN Rotary selector, turn Moves the highlight to the next card, row or button in MODS. On a beat jump pair, after a push, it steps the jump size. PUSH Rotary selector, push Opens or changes the highlighted item in MODS. BUTTON ABOVE LINK Does what you chose in MODS > PLAY > BUTTON ABOVE LINK. The default is INTERFACE. SHIFT + BUTTON ABOVE LINK Hold SHIFT on either deck and press it. Does the second choice on the same page. The default is ITS OWN JOB. LINK Its stock job. With the screen switch key set to LINK it also switches the VJ.Tools view on and off. SHORTCUT Opens the SHORTCUT screen. In MODERN this is MODERN's own SHORTCUT screen. LOAD Loads the highlighted track into the deck that side controls: deck 1 or 3, deck 2 or 4. TIME MODE , DECK QUANTIZE Stock on decks 1 and 2. For decks 3 and 4, see Quantize and Four decks . A short press of MENU keeps the job the player's own firmware gives it wherever there is one. What a short press does in each place: Where you are Short press of MENU The MODS menu is open Closes MODS A game is on screen The game's own key The VJ.Tools view is on screen As before A menu, popup or dialog is open Works or closes the open menu A track list (browse, playlist, search, history) The sort menu or the track menu TAG LIST LIST MENU The play screen in GRID ADJUST The beat grid menu The play screen Opens MODS experimental The SOURCE screen Opens MODS experimental The track INFO screen Opens MODS experimental The SHORTCUT screen Opens MODS experimental The player's own UTILITY Closes UTILITY Any other screen The screen's own job

manual:ddab45489d92bf5858ca.source: The XDJ-XZ has a media button directly above LINK . On a stock player it opens the library of a computer or phone connected to the player. XZ Mods gives it two slots: a plain press, and a press while SHIFT is held on either deck. Set them in MODS > PLAY > BUTTON ABOVE LINK. Press the button above LINK Press the button above LINK Both slots at their defaults. A press switches the interface, and SHIFT + press keeps the button's own job. Media buttons The four media buttons in the player's order from the top, left to right: the button above LINK, highlighted, then LINK, USB 1 and USB 2. PRESS What a plain press does. The filled choice is the current one. What it does One line explaining the current PRESS choice. SHIFT + PRESS What the button does while SHIFT is held on either deck. What it does One line explaining the current SHIFT + PRESS choice. Dock Explains the highlighted choice before you pick it. Choice What the button does MODS MENU Opens and closes MODS. MODS then works with the rotary selector and BACK . ITS OWN JOB The stock job: the screen for playing a computer's or phone's library. In MODERN the player's own screen for it takes over until you are back on the play screen. INTERFACE Switches between MODERN and CLASSIC, with the same notice as MODS > SCREEN. VJ.TOOLS SCREEN Switches the VJ.Tools screen on and off. Without an enabled, connected VJ.Tools link it says so instead. STEMS Does what the STEMS button on the screen does: steps the stem buttons through their places in 2 DECKS, and shows or hides them in MODERN's 4 DECKS. DECK VIEW Steps DECK VIEW: 2 DECKS, 4 DECKS in number order 1 2 3 4, 4 DECKS in mixer order 3 1 2 4, then 2 DECKS again. It saves the choice and shows the new view in a short notice. NOTHING The button does nothing. Tip With the default INTERFACE on a plain press, you can always get back to MODS without touching the screen: press MENU on the play screen, or switch interface with the button above LINK and press MENU there.

manual:ece5610a67cfa704b7a6.source: When VJ.Tools on a computer is connected, the player's screen can show the VJ.Tools view instead of the play screen. MODS > CONNECT > VJ.TOOLS has a SCREEN SWITCH KEY with two choices: Press MENU Tap CONNECT Tap VJ.TOOLS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise Choice What switches the VJ.Tools view LINK (default) Pressing LINK . LINK also keeps its stock job. ONSCREEN A VJ.Tools button on the screen, in the corner opposite MODS. To switch the view with the button above LINK instead, set that button to VJ.TOOLS SCREEN. See Connect and DJ profiles for the connection itself.

manual:b968512a040fa660315b.source: The picture shows the left deck from above. The right deck has the same controls in the same places. Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press SYNC on the left deck Press MASTER TEMPO on the left deck Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press SYNC on the left deck Press SHIFT on the left deck twice quickly One deck from above. The pads are named A to D on the top row and E to H on the bottom row. SHIFT Press twice quickly to switch this side between its two decks. Held, it is the modifier for the combinations below. SYNC SHIFT + SYNC matches this deck's key to the master deck (KEY SYNC). SYNC alone is stock on decks 1 and 2. MASTER TEMPO While KEY SYNC holds, a press returns the deck to its own key. TEMPO slider After you switch decks, the new deck keeps its tempo until the slider reaches it. Jog wheel Stock on decks 1 and 2. Plays decks 3 and 4, and the games. Pad mode buttons HOT CUE, BEAT LOOP, SLIP LOOP, BEAT JUMP. One of them gives stem pads. With SHIFT, they mute stems. BEAT JUMP Press for beat jump page 1. SHIFT + BEAT JUMP gives page 2. Pads A to D Stem pads in the stem mode when the bank is A-D. Jump pairs A/B and C/D in BEAT JUMP mode. Pads E to H Stem pads when the bank is E-H. Jump pairs E/F and G/H in BEAT JUMP mode. CUE and PLAY/PAUSE Stock on decks 1 and 2. They play deck 3 or 4 while the side drives it. Key Action with XZ Mods SHIFT twice Switches the left side between deck 1 and deck 3, or the right side between deck 2 and deck 4. Press it twice within about half a second, without touching anything else. Decks 3 and 4 need the loopback cable; without it the screen says DECK 3 AND 4 NEED THE CH3/CH4 ROUTE. SHIFT + SYNC KEY SYNC: shifts the key of the deck this side controls to match the master deck, and turns on MASTER TEMPO. Press it again to end KEY SYNC. Works on all four decks. SYNC alone keeps its stock job on decks 1 and 2. MASTER TEMPO While KEY SYNC holds on that deck, a press ends KEY SYNC and returns the deck to its own key. Otherwise stock. SHIFT + MASTER TEMPO keeps its stock job. HOT CUE , BEAT LOOP , SLIP LOOP Choose the pad mode as on a stock player. The mode set in MODS > STEMS > STEM PADS turns four pads into stem pads. SHIFT + HOT CUE Mutes or unmutes the first stem in your STEM ORDER (vocals by default) on that deck. SHIFT + BEAT LOOP Mutes or unmutes the second stem (harmonics by default). SHIFT + SLIP LOOP Mutes or unmutes the third stem (drums by default). BEAT JUMP Beat jump mode with page 1 of your jump sizes. SHIFT + BEAT JUMP Beat jump mode with page 2 of your jump sizes. Let go of SHIFT before you press a pad. TEMPO slider After a deck switch, the deck that takes over keeps its tempo until the slider crosses its value. Then the slider moves it again. This works both ways. LOAD Loads into the deck the side controls now. Jog wheel Stock on decks 1 and 2. On decks 3 and 4 it bends, scratches in VINYL mode and moves loop edges. The jog games use it too. The three SHIFT + pad mode combinations work while the USB loader has the stem engine. They also turn stem audio on if it was off. With them, the stock SHIFT + HOT CUE (CALL) is not available on decks 1 and 2. Every other deck key keeps its stock job on decks 1 and 2. While a side drives deck 3 or 4, the transport, loop, cue and tempo keys play that software deck instead. Four decks lists what each one does there.

manual:1b9aebc57b3152907884.source: The eight pads keep their stock job in every pad mode, with two exceptions: the stem pads, and the BEAT JUMP pads. Press HOT CUE on the left deck Press BEAT LOOP on the left deck Press SLIP LOOP on the left deck Press BEAT JUMP on the left deck Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press HOT CUE on the left deck, then BEAT LOOP on the left deck, then SLIP LOOP on the left deck Pad mode Pads with XZ Mods HOT CUE Stock hot cues. Gate cue and smart cue change what a hot cue does when you turn them on; see Gate cue and smart cue . BEAT LOOP Stock beat loops. SLIP LOOP Stock slip loops. BEAT JUMP Your jump sizes. A/B, C/D, E/F and G/H are pairs: the first pad jumps back, the second forward. With a loop on, the loop moves instead. SHIFT + pad keeps its stock job on decks 1 and 2. See Beat jump . The stem mode Four pads (A to D, or E to H) mute stems instead. The other four keep their job in that mode.

manual:1b09c1189c8611232654.source: In the pad mode you choose for stems, four pads switch stems on that deck. A, B and C mute the three stems in your STEM ORDER. D is BYPASS: it plays the original track instead of the stems. On a 4-stem track, D mutes bass instead. With the E-H bank, E to H do the same. Press MENU Tap STEMS Tap STEM PADS Tap HOT CUE Tap BEAT LOOP Tap SLIP LOOP Tap BEAT JUMP Tap PADS A-D Tap PADS E-H Tap ORDER Tap STEM COLOURS Tap OFF Press HOT CUE on the left deck Press pad A on the left deck Press pad B on the left deck Press pad C on the left deck Press pad D on the left deck Press pad A on the left deck HOT CUE gives stem pads on A to D, in the default order, with stem colours on the pad lights. Pad mode The pad mode button that gives stem pads. The others keep their pads. Pad diagram What each pad does in that mode, laid out like the pads on the deck. STEMS ON Which four pads carry the stems: PADS A-D or PADS E-H. Order The order of the stems on pads A, B and C and on the play screen. Push, then turn to change it. Stem pad lights STEM COLOURS lights stem pads in their stem colours and dims muted stems. OFF leaves the pad lights to the player. Works on Stem pads work on decks 1 and 2. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems. Setting on this page Choices Default Pad mode HOT CUE, BEAT LOOP, SLIP LOOP, BEAT JUMP HOT CUE STEMS ON PADS A-D, PADS E-H PADS A-D STEM PAD LIGHTS STEM COLOURS, OFF STEM COLOURS If you choose BEAT JUMP for stems, beat jumps win its pads. Page 2 always jumps. Page 1 jumps while it uses MY SIZES, and gives stem pads only while page 1 is set to STOCK. Stems explains the stem audio itself, the order and the stem buttons on the screen.

manual:005d9f65c43efb090898.source: What you see Meaning Stem pads in stem colours, muted stems dim STEM PAD LIGHTS is STEM COLOURS, on decks 1 and 2. Warm red and amber pads in BEAT JUMP mode Beat jump page 2 is selected on that deck. Stock pad colours Every other mode, and page 1 of BEAT JUMP.

manual:d996053fae70c661b356.source: Each side of the XZ drives one of two decks: the left side deck 1 or deck 3, the right side deck 2 or deck 4. Press SHIFT twice to switch. LOAD on that side then loads into the deck it controls. Press SHIFT on the right deck twice quickly Connect the loopback cable and wait until MODS > 4 DECKS says the route is ready. Press SHIFT twice quickly on the left side. The left side now drives deck 3. Move the TEMPO slider until it reaches deck 3's tempo. Until then the slider does not change deck 3. Press SHIFT twice again to go back to deck 1. If the loopback route goes down, both sides go back to decks 1 and 2. Four decks covers setup, the deck view and every status.

manual:6e55561724a48fcce92b.source: What happens Why, and what to do MENU opens a stock menu instead of MODS That screen has its own MENU job. Press BACK to the play screen, then press MENU . MENU opens UTILITY You held it. A short press opens MODS. The button above LINK does nothing It is set to NOTHING. Change it in MODS > PLAY > BUTTON ABOVE LINK. SHIFT twice shows DECK 3 AND 4 NEED THE CH3/CH4 ROUTE Decks 3 and 4 are not connected. Open MODS > 4 DECKS. The TEMPO slider does not change the deck Pickup after a deck switch. Move the slider through the deck's tempo. A key sync press shows a message on the deck's key See Keys and KEY SYNC . A BEAT JUMP pad shows JUMP UNAVAILABLE See When a jump is refused .

manual:7baed42621c487837b69.source: The play screen is where you spend the set. XZ Mods gives you two ways to draw it. MODERN replaces the whole screen with its own layout. CLASSIC keeps the player's own screen and adds a row of buttons, the playing key and the stem rows to it. You choose between them in MODS under SCREEN (see Screen, interfaces and themes ).

manual:9f982046117c8084f49b.source: MODERN draws every deck the same way: a top bar across the screen, one waveform lane per deck with a narrow info column on its left, a row of hot-cue lamps, and a deck strip at the bottom. Two decks share the screen in halves. For four decks, see Four decks . Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 6 clicks clockwise Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 6 clicks anticlockwise Tap TIME 1 Tap TIME 1 Tap INFO HEADER Press BACK

manual:fc4834423a5deb1c4362.source: Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Tap STEMS HEADER Tap STEMS HEADER Deck 1 is the master, deck 2 plays in a 4-beat loop with KEY SYNC holding its key. SINGLE CONTINUE | PLAY MODE. The lit word is what a deck does at the end of a track: SINGLE stops, CONTINUE loads the next track in the list and plays it. Tap to switch. A. HOT CUE Lit while HOT CUE AUTO LOAD is on. Red means every track brings its hot cues, white means only the tracks marked for it in the library. Tap to step through ON, the library setting and OFF. A. CUE Lit while AUTO CUE is on, so the cue point lands where the music starts. Tap to switch it. BEAT FX The effect, its beat and time, the FX BPM and the channel it is on. It fills red while the effect is on. DECKS Shows which decks the sides drive and opens DECK VIEW. See Four decks . INFO Opens INFO for the active deck's track. STEMS Steps the stem buttons through their layouts. Lit blue while stems are on. In 4 DECKS it shows or hides them. See Stems . MODS Opens MODS. A lamp label in grey shows a mode the player does not let XZ Mods change from the screen. Change it in the player's own UTILITY instead (hold MENU ). You can hide the three lamps in MODS under SCREEN , LAMPS AND TITLES . The BEAT FX readout then takes their room. ECHO on: the readout fills red, with the beat, the time in milliseconds and the FX BPM PING PONG chosen but off: a quiet outline An effect without beats shows its name alone VINYL BRAKE with a long time and the FX BPM set by TAP The first moments after start, before the effect has been read MODE LAMPS and QUANTIZE LAMP hidden: the readout starts at the left edge The same with ECHO on

manual:9ff485f2e02353be7239.source: Each deck gets an info column and a scrolling waveform. The playhead is the red line in the middle. DECK tag Tap to make this the active deck. The blue tile marks the active deck. The dashes beside the name count the beats of the bar. Source Where the track came from: USB1 or USB2. Key The key the deck plays now. Green or amber means it mixes with the master deck's key. See Key . KEY SYNC Replaces the KEY caption while KEY SYNC holds this deck's key. Tuning How many cents the playing key sits off the nearest semitone. ORIGINAL The track's analysed key, shown once the playing key has moved away from it. Beat countdown Bars and beats to the next cue ahead of the playhead, as bars.beats. Bar number Counts bars every four bars, so you can count phrases. Loop A running loop shades the waveform and names its length. Playhead The current position. The waveform scrolls past it. ZOOM How far the waveforms are zoomed. Turn the rotary encoder to zoom in or out. Hot-cue lamps Pads A to H in their cue colours. A dark lamp is an empty pad. Turn the rotary encoder on the play screen to zoom both lanes together. There are seven zoom steps. The zoom is kept when you leave the screen, and saved to the USB with your other settings. Zoomed fully in on deck 2 Zoomed fully out WAVEFORM CURRENT POSITION set to LEFT: more of what is coming up. This choice is saved to the USB too

manual:e5786941472c1f20622d.source: The two deck strips. Deck 1 is the tempo master, deck 2 is synced to it. DECK badge The deck this strip belongs to, lit when it is the active deck. Title and artist The loaded track. Play state A triangle while the deck plays, two bars while it is paused. TRACK The track's number in the list it was loaded from. REMAIN / TIME The lit word says how the time counts: REMAIN counts down to the end, TIME counts up from the start. Tap the time to switch. QUANTIZE Red while QUANTIZE is on, with the beat value loops and cues snap to. Tempo range The tempo slider's range, for example ±10. MT MASTER TEMPO. It blinks while KEY SYNC holds the key. SYNC Lit while the deck is synced. BPM The deck's playing BPM. MASTER marks the tempo master. Cue marks Hot cues as lettered chips and memory cues as red marks above the overview. Overview The whole track. The lighter part is what has played. Minute scale Minutes to the end in REMAIN, from the start in TIME. In the last 30 seconds of a track the overview's playing address flashes slowly, and in the last 15 seconds it flashes fast, in either time mode. Deck 1 in its last 12 seconds, the end warning flashing Deck 2 with no track: Not Loaded. in its lane and strip A three-digit track number TIME MODE that you can switch by touch: the lit word is white The first frame after start, before anything has been read: dashes everywhere

manual:0a1cd56afa64922af3fb.source: The large key in each deck's column is the key the deck plays right now. Tempo with MASTER TEMPO off, a key shift and KEY SYNC all move it. Its colour compares it with the master deck's key. Green means it mixes with the master's key: the same key, its relative major or minor, or one step away on the key wheel, tuned within 25 cents of the master. Amber means it would mix, but it is detuned by more than 25 cents. White means neither, and the master deck itself is always white. Turn KEY MATCH COLOURS off in SCREEN and every key is white. The cents beside it show how far it sits off the semitone, so you can match by ear. Once the playing key leaves the track's analysed key, ORIGINAL shows the analysed key below it. Press MENU Tap PLAY Tap KEYS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY UP and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY DOWN and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to RESET and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY SYNC and push it While KEY SYNC holds a deck's key, the KEY caption becomes a blue KEY SYNC chip and the deck's MT lamp blinks, half a second lit and half a second dark. KEY SYNC holds Bbm, MT lit Half a second later, MT dark MASTER TEMPO off: +2.20 % lifts A minor by 38 cents, still Am At +6.10 % the playing key reaches Bbm Keys written as wheel numbers, with a key shift on deck 1 The whole play screen with wheel-number keys An older loader without the analysed key: the key and its key-shift step No key read on deck 1, and a key name too long for the large face on deck 2 You choose how keys are written (as on the USB, musical or wheel numbers) and whether the playing key shows at all in MODS under SCREEN . See Screen, interfaces and themes .

manual:0063d4b2152453a1e479.source: MODS under SCREEN offers four waveform colours for MODERN. They change the lanes and the overviews together. Your choice is saved to the USB. 3-BAND COLOURS , beside LAMPS AND TITLES, changes the colour of each band; see 3-band colours . Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap STOCK Tap RGB Tap 3-BAND Tap STEMS Tap LAMPS AND TITLES Tap MODE LAMPS Tap QUANTIZE LAMP Tap TITLES IN WAVEFORMS Tap DECK + WAVE Tap DECK ONLY Tap OFF Tap CLOSE Choice What you see STOCK One blue waveform with white peaks RGB Lows red, mids green, highs blue 3-BAND Lows blue, mids amber, highs white, or the colours you chose in 3-BAND COLOURS STEMS Drums, harmonics and vocals in their stem colours. A track without stems shows 3-BAND STOCK RGB 3-BAND STEMS USB COLORS (MODS, SCREEN , LAMPS AND TITLES ) lets each deck take the colours saved on the USB stick its track came from. DECK + WAVE: the deck tile takes the stick's colour and the waveform the stick's waveform colour DECK ONLY: only the deck tile takes the stick's colour OFF: every deck uses the player's own colours

manual:7714277c0627fecbcf95.source: When something you asked for does not happen, a notice appears in the middle of the screen for two and a half seconds. It says what went wrong in one line, for example DECK 1 DID NOT LOAD THE TRACK . A long notice wraps. Messages and troubleshooting explains each one. Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Tap CHOOSE TRACK Push ROTARY SELECTOR Tap TRACK ROW Tap LOAD DECK 3 A notice over the lanes A long notice The same screen once the notice has gone If a deck cannot go on, its lane turns red and names the problem, for example EMERGENCY LOOP (the deck loops until you load a track) or CANNOT READ THE TRACK with the player's error code. Tap CHOOSE TRACK on the red band to make that deck active and open BROWSE. EMERGENCY LOOP on deck 2 CANNOT READ THE TRACK with error E-8302 A deck that plays its whole track from RAM after the music USB went out is not in trouble, so its lane says so in teal instead: WHOLE TRACK IN RAM · PLAYABLE , in the waveform's place. See RAM tracks .

manual:0199e14f3330dbf64d44.source: Press SHORTCUT on the play screen to see the settings you change most during a set on one page. It has the same four groups as the player's own SHORTCUT screen: PLAYER SETTINGS, DECK STATUS, DEVICE SETTINGS and MY SETTINGS. Press BACK or tap the arrow in the top left corner to return to the play screen. Press SHORTCUT Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Press BACK The SHORTCUT screen with quantize, waveform and time settings for both decks. Highlighted row Turn the encoder to move between rows. The line under the title explains the highlighted row. Locked value A lock and READ ONLY HERE mean XZ Mods shows this value but cannot change it here. Pushing or tapping it does nothing. Choice buttons Tap a value to change it. The lit button is the current value. DECK 1 lamps QUANTIZE (or Q1), SYNC, SLIP, MASTER and the time mode for deck 1. Tap QUANTIZE to switch it, tap REMAIN or TIME to change the time mode. LINK lamp Shows whether the player is linked to other players. Jumps TRACK, PLAYLIST and SEARCH open those lists. MATCHING opens matching tracks, or hands over to the player's own browser when XZ Mods cannot list them. DEVICE SETTINGS Waveform colour, playhead position, key display format and waveform zoom. These change the MODERN screen at once. MY SETTINGS Time mode, play mode and auto cue for the decks. Which rows you can change depends on what the player lets XZ Mods write. A locked row shows its value and the reason it is read-only. A short MENU on SHORTCUT opens MODS. NEEDLE LOCK appears in PLAYER SETTINGS when the player reports it. LOCK prevents a waveform touch from searching a playing deck. Pause the deck to search, or choose UNLOCK when that setting is writable. HOT CUE AUTO LOAD has choices; QUANTIZE BEAT VALUE and AUTO CUE LEVEL are read-only in this fixture QUANTIZE BEAT VALUE as four choices, play mode and auto cue locked The waveform colour row with STEMS chosen The player's own settings shown as values while it is not accepting changes. DEVICE SETTINGS still change the MODERN screen With four decks, SHORTCUT also shows DECK SELECT. See Four decks .

manual:5f577cfac2d8aec40e0a.source: CLASSIC keeps the player's own play screen, so every stock element stays where the XDJ-XZ operating instructions put it. XZ Mods restyles it in the classic theme you chose and adds a row of buttons across the top, the playing key under each deck's key, and stem rows under the waveforms. Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen The ORIGINAL theme with stems on in the BELOW / HALF layout. Deck 1's playing key has moved from 2A to 11A. VJ.TOOLS Switches to the VJ.Tools screen when a VJ.Tools computer is connected. See Connect and DJ profiles . DECKS Shows which decks the sides drive and opens DECK VIEW. See Four decks . Metrics The player's CPU load, free memory and temperature. Tap METRICS to set it up. See Extras . STEMS Steps the stem rows through their layouts. The marks under the label show the current one. Dark in 4 DECKS, which has no stem rows. See Stems . MODS Opens MODS. Playing key Shown under the player's own key. The analysed key, an arrow, then the key the deck plays now, with its tuning in cents. Same key When the playing key has not moved, KEY and the key, with the cents. Stem rows VOCALS, DRUMS, HARMONICS and BYPASS for each deck. See Stems . This picture is the stock screen of a real player with the XZ Mods buttons and stem rows added. Everything else on it is the player's own: the deck tabs, source, key, BEAT FX, ZOOM, the deck strips with A.HOTCUE, A.CUE, QUANTIZE, TEMPO and the BPM box. The XDJ-XZ operating instructions explain those. The key line replaces the player's beat countdown under the key. You choose the key notation and whether the playing key shows in MODS under SCREEN . An earlier capture with stems in the BELOW / FULL layout, the rows taller with room for the stem level bars. Stem colours here follow an older default. Today drums are blue and harmonics red; see Stem colours .

manual:3daad9c574654b5e0f53.source: In CLASSIC, SCREEN offers three scrolling waveforms. The setting is wave_mode on the USB. Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap CLASSIC Tap 2 DECKS Tap 4 DECKS Tap 4 DECKS Tap STOCK Tap 3-BAND Tap STEMS Tap AS ON THE USB Tap MUSICAL Tap WHEEL Tap PLAYING KEY Tap KEY MATCH COLOURS Tap KEY BEFORE TITLE Tap CLOSE Choice What you see STOCK The player's own scrolling waveform 3-BAND Layered lows, mids and highs (the default). 3-BAND COLOURS chooses their colours; see 3-band colours STEMS Drums, harmonics and vocals layered in their stem colours. A track without prepared stems shows 3-BAND The overview in each deck strip stays the player's own in every choice. When a deck plays its whole track from RAM after the music USB went out, a teal card in its lane says WHOLE TRACK IN RAM · PLAYABLE where the waveform was. See RAM tracks .

manual:84a910e5032198070d10.source: Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap PLAYING KEY Tap PLAYING KEY Tap KEY MATCH COLOURS Tap KEY BEFORE TITLE Tap CLOSE You see Why What to do Dashes instead of numbers The value has not been read yet, or the deck has no track Wait a moment, or load a track A grey mode lamp that does not react The player does not let XZ Mods change that mode Change it in UTILITY (hold MENU ) NO STEM WAVE YET · 3BAND in a lane STEMS waveform chosen, but this track's stems are not loaded yet Wait, or prepare the track's stems. See Stems The key stays white on every deck No master deck, or KEY MATCH COLOURS is off Set a tempo master, or turn KEY MATCH COLOURS on in SCREEN

manual:58076368d1612a6078d6.source: Press BROWSE or TAG LIST to open that list, or hold BROWSE for SEARCH. PLAYLIST is in the BROWSE category rail and on the SHORTCUT screen. Press BACK to go up one level. At the top of a list BACK opens SOURCE, where you pick the USB to browse. Press BROWSE Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 7 clicks clockwise, then push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Press BACK Press BACK The TRACK category of USB1, sorted by title, with PREVIEW on and a row touched. Source The USB you are browsing, in its own colour. Tap to open SOURCE. Category rail ARTIST, ALBUM, TRACK, KEY, BPM, GENRE, RATING, COLOR, PLAYLIST, FOLDER, HISTORY and MATCHING. Tap one, or drag the rail to see the rest. BACK Goes up one level. PREVIEW Shows or hides the preview waveform column. INFO Opens the INFO panel for the highlighted track. Column title The arrow marks the column the list is sorted by. The number in brackets is how many items the list holds. Preview A small waveform of each track, so you can see breaks and builds before you load. Played A green note marks a track you have played. On a deck A blue number says the track is loaded on that deck. LOAD Appears on the row you touched. Tap 1 or 2 to load the track on that deck. Key colour Green or amber means the key mixes with the master deck's key. Deck strip Both decks' time, overview, tempo, key and BPM stay in view while you browse.

manual:7c71eefdfe38b411e425.source: Press BROWSE Push ROTARY SELECTOR Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 5 clicks clockwise Press BACK Control What it does Turn the encoder Moves the highlight one row Push the encoder Opens a folder. On a track, opens the track menu: LOAD TO DECK for each deck, CUE / LOOP LIST when the track has memory points and the deck can load at one, and CANCEL. The active deck is highlighted, so a second push loads it there Hold the encoder Turns letter jump on. Turning then jumps by first letter, or by page where the list has no index. Push or hold again to stop Drag or flick the list Scrolls Tap a row Highlights it and shows LOAD BACK Up one level. At the top, opens SOURCE MENU Opens the list's MENU panel: sort, columns and the track menu INFO Opens or closes the INFO panel PREVIEW off: the PREVIEW OFF tile and the full width for the columns PREVIEW on Letter jump: the letter shows large while you turn Page jump in a list with no letter index The highlight near the end of a long list Rows still on their way from the USB stay blank for a moment The PLAYLIST category: folders and playlists The category rail dragged down to HISTORY and MATCHING Long names are cut to fit their column The first moment after opening, before the list has been read BROWSE before the USB's library has been read: LIST NOT READ YET PLAYLIST before it has been read TAG LIST before it has been read SEARCH before the library has been read Deck 2 empty in the deck strip The preview column starts hidden. One tap on PREVIEW shows it, and XZ Mods remembers your choice on the USB ( browse_preview ). PREVIEW is touch only.

manual:b84a797b154280c82317.source: There are three ways to load the highlighted track: Press BROWSE Push ROTARY SELECTOR Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise Press LOAD 1 Press BACK Tap the row, then tap 1 or 2 on its LOAD chip. Push the encoder twice to load on the active deck, or push, turn to another deck and push. Press the LOAD button of the deck you want. If no track is highlighted, LOAD says SELECT A TRACK, THEN PRESS LOAD . On a screen that is not a track list it says OPEN A TRACK LIST TO LOAD . To load onto decks 3 and 4, see Four decks . The same row with deck 2 active: its 2 is highlighted Loading not available on this list: the row highlights without LOAD SELECT A TRACK, THEN PRESS LOAD

manual:793191cbd2d5ff9aa1b5.source: Press INFO or tap INFO to open a panel with the highlighted track's details beside the list. The list narrows to make room. Press INFO Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen The INFO panel: BPM, KEY, TIME, RATING, COLOR, PLAYED and ON DECK The INFO panel opened with INFO while keys are colour coded Keys coloured against deck 1's Fm

manual:43efccd65c7ee4165ccf.source: Press MENU or tap a column title. The MENU panel opens on the right with the sort order, the columns to show, and the actions for the highlighted track. Press BROWSE Push ROTARY SELECTOR Press MENU Tap CUE/LOOP LIST Tap INTRO CUE The MENU panel on a track list, with three tracks already in the tag list. TRACK Actions for the highlighted track. ADD TO TAG LIST Adds the track to the tag list. On a track already in it this reads REMOVE FROM TAG LIST. CUE/LOOP LIST Not on the player in this version. MARK PLAYED Marks the track played. A played track offers MARK UNPLAYED. SEARCH Opens SEARCH. Tag marks Tracks in the tag list carry a check mark. Close Closes the panel. MENU and BACK close it too. Sort by: one choice at a time COLUMNS: tick the columns the list shows Six columns with PREVIEW off, sorted by BPM, highest first COLOR and TIME columns Check marks on tracks in the tag list HISTORY: ADD ALL TO TAG LIST, DELETE HISTORY and DELETE ALL HISTORIES

manual:06e372f724013244927a.source: Tap FILTER to narrow the list without leaving it. The filters stay on while you move between categories, and a chip in the header says which are on. Press BROWSE Press TRACK FILTER Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise, then push it Press BACK Filter What it keeps BPM Tracks within a range of the master deck's BPM, for example MASTER ±6 MATCH MASTER KEY Tracks whose key mixes with the master deck's key AT LEAST Tracks rated at least that many stars COLOR Tracks with any of the colours you tick MY TAG Not available yet CLEAR ALL FILTERS in the panel, or a tap on the chip, turns every filter off. Filters that compare with the master deck need one. Without it you see NO MASTER DECK: BPM FILTER OFF or NO MASTER KEY: KEY FILTER OFF . TRACK FILTER with BPM, key, rating and colour filters on The filter chip in the header. Tap it to clear every filter

manual:6712973cc24ce4a6bf06.source: Hold BROWSE (SEARCH is printed above it), or tap SEARCH on the SHORTCUT screen. Type on the keyboard and the list updates as you type. SEARCH puts the keyboard away so you can scroll the results. DELETE removes a letter and CLEAR empties the field. Hold BROWSE for a second Tap A Tap B Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise Typing NEON. Eleven tracks match so far. Search field What you have typed. Count How many tracks match. SEARCH Puts the keyboard away and moves to the results. DELETE Removes the last letter. Key The key you touched is outlined. SEARCH before you type The results with the keyboard put away

manual:7abf26c1f57b856e0b6d.source: The tag list is a quick list of tracks you want to play next. It holds up to 100 tracks and shows how many it has in the header. XZ Mods keeps it on the USB in XZMODS/playlists.txt , with your playlist changes. To add a track, use ADD TO TAG LIST in the MENU panel. To add a whole folder, highlight it and use ADD ALL TO TAG LIST. Press TAG LIST Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise Press MENU Press BACK The tag list with 12 of 100 tracks, one row touched The tag list full at 100 tracks MENU in the tag list: REMOVE FROM TAG LIST, CREATE PLAYLIST and REMOVE ALL TRACKS CREATE PLAYLIST: the tag list saved as a new playlist REMOVE ALL TRACKS armed: push again to clear the tag list

manual:da13d375ad5579fa7001.source: Tap PLAYLIST in the BROWSE category rail, or on the SHORTCUT screen, to open the USB's playlists. You can also make your own and change them on the player. Press MENU in the playlist list or inside a playlist. Press BROWSE Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 6 clicks clockwise, then push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise, then push it Press BACK In the MENU panel What it does NEW PLAYLIST Makes a playlist in the folder that is open. Type its name on the keyboard RENAME Renames the highlighted playlist DELETE Deletes the highlighted playlist. Push again to confirm ADD TO PLAYLIST Adds the highlighted track to a playlist you pick REMOVE FROM PLAYLIST Takes the highlighted track out of the playlist MOVE TRACK Picks up a track. Turn the encoder to move it, push to drop it Playlists, the tag list, played marks and histories can change only on a USB that is not read-only. Changes made on the player are saved on the same USB in XZMODS/playlists.txt . They never change the library your DJ software exported, so your DJ software and the CLASSIC browse screens do not show them. A playlist you changed on the player is marked in the list. In HISTORY the MENU panel offers DELETE HISTORY and DELETE ALL HISTORIES, each after a second push. If the USB is read-only you see THIS STICK IS READ-ONLY: PLAYLISTS CANNOT CHANGE . If it is full you see THE STICK IS FULL: PLAYLIST NOT SAVED . The playlist list with its MENU panel open and DELETE highlighted. PLAYLIST Actions for the playlist list. NEW PLAYLIST Makes a playlist here. RENAME Renames the highlighted playlist. DELETE Deletes it after a second push. Sort and columns The same sort and column choices as in BROWSE. A playlist's tracks Playlist folders DELETE armed: push again to delete Naming a new playlist on the keyboard ADD TO PLAYLIST: pick the playlist A track picked up to move A playlist changed on the player, marked in the list

manual:219f04aba54d2d36dedb.source: SOURCE shows every place music can come from, one tile each. Press BACK at the top of a list, or tap the source tile at the top left of BROWSE. Open SOURCE ( BACK at the top of a list) Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise Press BACK USB1 is being browsed and plays on both decks. USB2 is still loading. BROWSING The source BROWSE shows now. Name and colour The USB's name and the colour saved on it. Status READY, LOADING, NOT CONNECTED, or DECK'S OWN SCREEN where the player's own screen handles that source. FREE Free space on the USB. Decks The decks playing a track from this source. LINK Players on LINK. Browsing LINK from MODERN is not available yet. COMPUTER DJ software on a computer linked to the player. Browsing it from MODERN is not available yet. Hint Opening a source opens its library in BROWSE. Turn the encoder to pick a tile and push to open it, or tap it. A source the player's own screen handles opens that screen. Touch cannot open it yet; push the encoder instead. The highlight on COMPUTER USB2 being browsed while it loads Nothing connected LINK handled by the player's own screen COMPUTER handled by the player's own screen Long device names cut to fit Before the sources have been read SOURCE opened before anything has been read SOURCE reached with BACK from the top of BROWSE USB2 asked for with nothing in it BROWSE on a USB that has been removed: no old rows remain

manual:cb109f648bb37285832d.source: Press INFO on the play screen, or tap the INFO icon in the top bar, to see everything about a loaded track. INFO for deck 1's track. Deck tabs Switch between the decks' tracks. Close Back to where you were. INFO and BACK close it too. Artwork The track's artwork, when the USB has it. RATING The track's stars. Linked field A field with an arrow opens BROWSE with every track that shares it. ARTIST, ALBUM, KEY, BPM and GENRE are linked. KEY and BPM Tap to open the KEY or BPM category at this value. COMMENT The comment saved with the track in your DJ software. SOURCE Where the track came from. Deck strip Both decks stay in view. Deck 2's track with a long title The highlight on KEY, ready to push The highlight on GENRE INFO for the track highlighted in a list, in its own tab A deck with no track INFO when browsing is not available: fields are not linked Long names cut to fit Before the track has been read INFO opened before anything has been read

manual:fa07657fffaa1fe941d5.source: CLASSIC keeps the player's own browse screens: the same lists, keys and menus the XDJ-XZ operating instructions describe. XZ Mods adds three things to them. The key in every row. Each track row shows up to three fields from the library exported to your USB inside the title cell. The default is the title, then the key, then the BPM. Key before title. With KEY BEFORE TITLE on, the key leads the row, so you can read keys down the list. Key match colours. With KEY MATCH COLOURS on, a leading key is green when it mixes with the master deck's key, amber when it is detuned against it, and grey otherwise. The table header names what the player's own MENU click changes: SORT over the title column and COLUMN over the right-hand column. The STEMS and MODS buttons stay at the top right. These additions only use tracks on a USB with an exported library. A track XZ Mods cannot match in the export keeps the player's own row, and a field the export does not have is left out.

manual:f49b94f9a96c13df885c.source: Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap KEY MATCH COLOURS Tap KEY BEFORE TITLE Tap CLOSE Press BROWSE Push ROTARY SELECTOR Press MENU Tap ARTIST Setting MODS What it does Default browse_preview PREVIEW tile in MODERN browse Shows the preview waveform column in MODERN browse Hidden browse_traffic SCREEN , KEY MATCH COLOURS Colours keys that mix with the master deck's key, in both interfaces On browse_key_prefix SCREEN , KEY BEFORE TITLE Puts the key first in each CLASSIC browse row On browse_1 , browse_2 , browse_3 none The three fields in each CLASSIC browse row, in order. Each is TITLE, ARTIST, KEY or BPM TITLE, KEY, BPM modern_browse_columns COLUMNS in the MODERN MENU panel The columns of the MODERN track list. TITLE always shows Automatic MODS has no control for the three CLASSIC row fields in this version. They keep the values stored on the USB. In MODERN, choose columns from the MENU panel instead.

manual:451f974c562c77a53f2e.source: Open SOURCE ( BACK at the top of a list) Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Press BROWSE Push ROTARY SELECTOR Press LOAD 1 You see What to do USB1 IS NOT CONNECTED or USB2 IS NOT CONNECTED Insert the USB, or pick another source USB SOURCE CHANGED: SELECT TRACK AGAIN The USB changed while you chose. Highlight the track again LOAD FROM THIS LIST IS OFF Load from a track list instead LINK BROWSING IS NOT AVAILABLE YET or COMPUTER BROWSING IS NOT AVAILABLE YET Switch to CLASSIC to browse that source TOUCH CANNOT OPEN THIS YET: PUSH THE ENCODER Highlight the tile and push the encoder PLAYLIST CHANGE NOT APPLIED Try again. If the USB is read-only or full, the notice says so

manual:d05c7865a169b5cd4494.source: Stems split a track into its parts so you can mute them live. XZ Mods plays three stems per track: VOCALS , HARMONICS (everything melodic that is not a voice) and DRUMS . You mute them from the pads or from buttons on the screen, change their levels by sliding, and switch back to the whole track with BYPASS . Stems work on decks 1 and 2. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems. Note MODERN labels the harmonics stem INST and the vocals stem VOCAL on its stem buttons. They are the same stems.

manual:3e8836116b64ae5e0fc0.source: The player cannot split a track itself. You prepare stems on your computer, once per track, and they travel on the USB beside your music. Prepare the stems in the XZ Mods app on your computer, or in OverCue Desktop. See The XZ Mods app . Keep the stems on the same USB as the music. Your original files and the library your DJ software exported stay unchanged. On the player, load the original track through the normal browser and wait a moment for its stems to load. A track without prepared stems plays as normal. Its stem buttons say why, and the button at their end tells you what to do (see Stem readiness ).

manual:1dab51c2c6d9e449b4d7.source: Open MODS, choose STEMS on the section rail, and turn USB STEMS on. It is on by default. With it off, every pad keeps its normal job and the stem buttons say STEMS ARE OFF or STEMS OFF . Press MENU Tap STEMS Tap USB STEMS Tap USB STEMS Tap CLOSE The STEMS page with USB stems on. USB STEMS Plays prepared stems from the USB. Off gives every pad its normal job back. Without the stem engine on the USB it reads SET UP USB STEMS and starts the setup. STEMS IN DJ SOFTWARE Sets up stem control for DJ software on a computer. See Stems in DJ software . STEM PADS Which pad mode gives stem pads, the stem order and the pad lights. See Stem pads . Stem buttons on screen Where the stem buttons sit on the play screen. The outlined tile is the current layout. STEM COLOURS The colour of each stem. See Stem colours . WORKS ON The decks this page applies to. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems.

manual:2ea63d933ff4eb12917d.source: Each deck gets three stem buttons and BYPASS . Tap a stem button to mute that stem, and tap it again to bring it back. A muted stem goes dark and keeps its level in its label. Tap STEMS HEADER Tap STEMS HEADER Tap STEMS HEADER Tap STEMS HEADER Tap STEMS HEADER Tap STEMS HEADER

manual:13e7db6ad942b389834b.source: Tap DRUMS Tap BYPASS Tap BYPASS BELOW / FULL rows. Deck 1 plays its stems with INST muted. Deck 2 is bypassed and plays the whole track. STEMS Lit blue while stems are on. Tap to step to the next layout. The marks under the label show which one is current. In 4 DECKS it shows or hides the stem buttons. DRUMS Tap to mute. Slide sideways to set the level. The fill and the percentage show it. VOCAL The vocals stem. INST Muted. It goes dark and keeps its level in the label. BYPASS Grey while the stems play. BYPASS lit Lit white, the deck plays the original track and every stem button goes dark. Tap again to hear the stems as you left them. On full-height rows each stem button is also a fader. Put a finger on it and slide right to raise the level or left to lower it. One button's width covers the whole range. A tap without a slide toggles the mute. Half-height rows and the small buttons beside the hot cues mute only. In 2 DECKS, STEMS in the top bar steps through six layouts in this order: beside the hot cues, below each deck at full height, below at half height, at the outer edges at full height, at the outer edges at half height, and hidden. You can also pick one in MODS under STEMS . MODERN keeps its own layout ( modern_stems ), so switching to CLASSIC and back does not change it. The default is the small buttons beside the hot cues. BY THE CUES: small buttons beside the hot-cue lamps (the default) BELOW / FULL: a full row under each deck's waveform BELOW / HALF: half-height rows, more room for the waveforms OUTER / FULL: above deck 1 and below deck 2 OUTER / HALF HIDDEN: full-height waveforms, stems still play The marks under STEMS follow the same order, so the lit mark tells you the layout without looking at the decks. First mark: BY THE CUES Second mark: BELOW / FULL Third mark: BELOW / HALF Fourth mark: OUTER / FULL Fifth mark: OUTER / HALF Sixth mark: HIDDEN BYPASS BUTTON in MODS under STEMS shows or hides the BYPASS button. Hidden, the stem buttons take its room and the pads still bypass. BYPASS beside the hot cues, deck 2 bypassed An older loader that does not report the layout: small buttons with BYPASS BYPASS on half rows BYPASS at the outer edges BYPASS at the outer edges, half height BYPASS BUTTON hidden: three wider stem buttons Sliding deck 1's DRUMS down to 35 % Deck 2 with DRUMS and VOCAL muted beside deck 1 playing all three Stems on with the stem buttons beside the hot cues STEMS waveform with stems muted on both decks VOCAL muted on deck 2 Two stems muted on deck 2, with stem colours of the DJ's own choice A track without stems: only the hot-cue lamps If stems are off when you tap STEMS , the layout still changes, and a notice says STEM ROWS SHOW ONCE STEMS ARE ON IN MODS .

manual:912f6d12a09875aec48f.source: In a 4 DECKS view the lanes are too short for the layouts, so STEMS is a switch there. One tap hides the stem buttons on every deck, and the screen says STEM BUTTONS HIDDEN . The next tap brings them back and says STEM BUTTONS SHOWN . STEMS is lit while they show and has no layout marks. Your 2 DECKS layout does not change, and XZ Mods saves the 4 DECKS choice on the USB separately. Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Tap STEMS HEADER Tap STEMS HEADER A deck whose track has no prepared stems shows no stem buttons in 4 DECKS, and its waveform keeps the whole lane. The buttons appear when you load a track with stems. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems, so they never show stem buttons. Four decks has pictures.

manual:98875ef5cf012b8ab711.source: In CLASSIC the stem rows sit inside the player's own waveform area, one row per deck. Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen Two full rows. Deck 1 plays HARMONICS at 70 % with DRUMS muted. VOCALS Tap to mute. Slide sideways to set the level. Level The fill and the percentage show the stem's level. Muted A muted stem goes dark and reads MUTE with the level it returns to. BYPASS D1 OFF means deck 1 plays its stems. Tap to play the original track. In 2 DECKS, the STEMS button in the top right corner of the play screen steps the rows through five layouts: BELOW / FULL, BELOW / HALF, OUTER / FULL, OUTER / HALF and HIDDEN, then back to BELOW / FULL. Its five marks show the current one. Half rows give each waveform more height. HIDDEN gives the player's waveforms their full size back while the stems keep playing. CLASSIC keeps its own layout ( stems_overlay ). While four decks show in CLASSIC, no stem rows are drawn, and STEMS stays dark. A tap changes nothing and says STEM BUTTONS SHOW IN 2 DECKS VIEW . The layout comes back when you return to two decks.

manual:fe6f3a8b424ec35fb3db.source: The pads mute stems too, without looking at the screen. Open STEM PADS on the STEMS page. Press HOT CUE on the left deck Press pad A on the left deck Press pad B on the left deck Press pad C on the left deck Press pad D on the left deck Press pad A on the left deck HOT CUE gives stem pads on A to D, in the order VOCALS, HARMONICS, DRUMS. Pad mode button Pick the pad mode that gives stem pads: HOT CUE, BEAT LOOP, SLIP LOOP or BEAT JUMP. The other modes keep their normal pads. Stem pads Pads A, B and C mute the three stems in the order below. BYPASS pad Pad D plays the original track while lit. Other pads Pads E to H keep their normal job. STEMS ON Put the stems on pads A to D or on pads E to H. Order The stem order on the pads and on the screen. Push, then turn to change it. Pad lights STEM COLOURS lights the stem pads in their stem colours and dims a muted one. OFF leaves the lights to the player. SHIFT shortcut SHIFT + HOT CUE, BEAT LOOP or SLIP LOOP always gives stem pads, whatever mode you picked. Mute and bypass are performance state. They are not saved, and every track starts with all stems playing.

manual:4fd43b5800c0660c491c.source: The order puts the stems where your fingers expect them. It changes the pads and the stem buttons on the screen together. There are six orders. Press MENU Tap STEMS Tap USB STEMS Tap BY THE CUES Tap BELOW / FULL Tap BELOW / HALF Tap OUTER / FULL Tap OUTER / HALF Tap HIDDEN Tap BYPASS BUTTON Order Pads A, B, C VOCALS / HARMONICS / DRUMS The default VOCALS / DRUMS / HARMONICS HARMONICS / VOCALS / DRUMS HARMONICS / DRUMS / VOCALS DRUMS / VOCALS / HARMONICS DRUMS / HARMONICS / VOCALS The layered STEMS waveform and the stem row for DJ software keep their own order.

manual:cb944f55cc99f38234f4.source: Each stem has a colour on the pads, the stem buttons and the STEMS waveform. In the ORIGINAL theme drums are blue, harmonics red and vocals green. Every theme has its own shades. Press MENU Tap STEMS Tap STEM COLOURS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise All three stems follow the theme. Stem DRUMS, HARMONICS and VOCALS each have their own column. THEME Follows the theme you chose. The outlined tile is the current choice. Bass A four-stem track's bass always follows the theme. Preview The three colours as the STEMS waveform draws them. RESET STEM COLORS Puts all three back to THEME. The choices are THEME, BLUE, RED, GREEN, AMBER, PURPLE, CYAN, PINK and WHITE. A fixed colour stays when you change theme. Amber drums, cyan harmonics and pink vocals on half rows The STEMS waveform zoomed out The STEMS waveform zoomed in The STEMS waveform at full zoom on the play screen Deck 2's stems not loaded yet: it draws 3-BAND and says NO STEM WAVE YET

manual:b67f944a15a38f9b1d68.source: Each deck's stem buttons tell you whether its stems can play. When they cannot, the stem buttons go dark and the last button names the reason. Where you can fix it from the player, that button does it. Press MENU Tap STEMS Tap SET UP USB STEMS Tap CHECK STEM ENGINE Tap TURN ON USB STEMS / DECKS 1 + 2 Tap CHECK THIS DECK AGAIN Tap CHECK THIS DECK AGAIN Tap STEMS READY / BACK TO PLAY On the stem row What it means What to do STEMS READY The stems play Nothing NO STEM ENGINE, with SET UP The USB loader has no stem engine Update the USB loader with XZ Mods on your computer, then restart the player STEMS OFF, with TURN ON USB STEMS is off Tap TURN ON, or turn USB STEMS on in MODS NO TRACK LOADED The deck is empty Load a track from USB on this deck NOT PREPARED, with HOW TO FIX This track has no prepared stems Prepare it in XZ Mods on your computer, then load it again LOADING STEMS The stems are loading from USB Wait a moment PLAY TO ALIGN The stems are loaded and wait for the track Press PLAY. The stems lock to the track a few seconds in STEM SET ERROR, with HOW TO FIX A stem file is missing or damaged Verify the track in XZ Mods on your computer STEMS READY on deck 1 NO STEM ENGINE on both decks STEMS OFF on both decks NO TRACK LOADED on deck 1 NOT PREPARED on deck 1, with HOW TO FIX LOADING STEMS on deck 1 PLAY TO ALIGN on deck 1 STEM SET ERROR on deck 1 USB STEMS off and no deck ready: TURN ON for all decks In MODERN the stem buttons on a deck that cannot play stems read STEMS ARE OFF or NO STEMS ON THIS TRACK , and only the hot-cue lamps stay in the pad row. In 4 DECKS such a deck shows no stem buttons, and its waveform keeps the whole lane.

manual:54b605c30e896b23bd3a.source: Tap SET UP or HOW TO FIX on a stem row, or SET UP USB STEMS in MODS, to open USB STEMS setup. It checks one deck at a time and walks you through the three steps: check the engine, turn stems on, load a prepared track. Deck 1 has found its OverCue stems and waits for PLAY. DECK 1 / DECK 2 The deck this setup checks. Steps Check the engine, turn stems on, load a prepared track. Deck status Where this deck stands now. FOUND The stem format found for this track. Next step What to do next, in one line. Action Does the next step, or checks the deck again. STEMS READY: STEMS READY / BACK TO PLAY NO STEM ENGINE STEMS OFF NO TRACK LOADED NOT PREPARED LOADING STEMS STEM SET ERROR, with the missing file named The setup page reached from MODS

manual:a7895a7832a52c377b54.source: When the XZ plays from DJ software on a computer over USB, the stem buttons can switch the software's stems instead. Open STEMS IN DJ SOFTWARE on the STEMS page and follow its four steps for each deck: DETECT , MAP STEMS , LIVE TEST and CONFIRM . Press MENU Tap STEMS Tap STEMS IN DJ SOFTWARE Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise Experimental Stem switching works after the live test. Levels and BYPASS for DJ software need more checking, and the software has no stem bypass over USB. Deck 1 before setup, with no computer deck found yet. Deck The deck this setup checks.
