Status The deck's source, the link to the computer and whether stem switching has been tested. Steps DETECT, MAP STEMS, LIVE TEST and CONFIRM. DETECT PC Checks that this deck plays from the computer. Connect the XZ to the computer by USB and open your DJ software in Performance mode before you start. A deck playing from the computer then shows a stem row for the software, with three or four stems. Four software stems ready on deck 1, the XZ's own stems on deck 2 Four stems with the software's on and off state shown A switch sent, waiting for the software to confirm A stem button held down Not tested yet: SET UP PC LINK LOST: nothing is sent Source not confirmed yet Three software stems ready Three stems with feedback Three stems, a switch pending Three stems, a button held Three stems, not tested yet Three stems, PC link lost Three stems, source not confirmed Setup, four stems, before the live test Setup done, four stems Four stems with feedback Four stems, a switch pending Four stems, link lost Four stems, source not confirmed Setup, three stems, before the live test Setup done, three stems Three stems with feedback Three stems, a switch pending Three stems, link lost Three stems, source not confirmed

manual:0b77ba02422bd649880c.source: You see What to do No stem buttons at all in MODERN Tap STEMS in the top bar until the layout you want shows. HIDDEN shows none. In 4 DECKS, tap STEMS once. A deck whose track has no stems shows none STEMS ARE OFF Turn USB STEMS on in MODS under STEMS NO STEMS ON THIS TRACK or NOT PREPARED Prepare the track in the XZ Mods app, copy it to the USB, then load it again PLAY TO ALIGN does not go away Let the track play for a few seconds. If it stays, check the track in the XZ Mods app Stems on decks 3 and 4 Not available. Stems work on decks 1 and 2 only

manual:d77c3bc002c57814ba70.source: Open MODS and choose PLAY in the section rail. Press MENU Tap PLAY Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise Press BACK The PLAY page with the default settings: gate cue and smart cue off, the default jump sizes, and the button above LINK on INTERFACE. BEAT JUMP PADS Opens the beat jump editor. The numbers are your page 1 and page 2 sizes in beats. GATE CUE Hot cues play only while you hold the pad. Off by default. SMART CUE A hot cue press also moves the CUE point there. Off by default. KEYS Opens the key page: key shift and KEY SYNC for all four decks. RAM TRACKS Opens RAM TRACKS: copy a deck's track into memory. BUTTON ABOVE LINK What the button above LINK does, alone and with SHIFT. See Controls on the player. Dock Explains the highlighted row in plain words. Works on The decks the highlighted feature works on, in mixer order 3 1 2 4. A dim number is a deck it does not work on, with the reason below. If the cue engine has not reported on this USB loader, GATE CUE and SMART CUE show as SET UP GATE CUE and SET UP SMART CUE instead of switches. See Feature setup .

manual:3713fb46803dc63f0c57.source: In BEAT JUMP mode the eight pads form four pairs: A/B, C/D, E/F and G/H. The first pad of a pair jumps back, the second jumps forward, by the same number of beats. With a loop on, the loop moves by that amount instead. Press MENU Tap PLAY Tap BEAT JUMP PADS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise Press BEAT JUMP on the left deck Press pad A on the left deck Press pad B on the left deck Press pad C on the left deck Press pad D on the left deck Press pad E on the left deck Press pad F on the left deck Press pad G on the left deck Press pad H on the left deck Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press BEAT JUMP on the left deck Press pad A on the left deck Press pad B on the left deck Press pad C on the left deck Press pad D on the left deck Press pad E on the left deck Press pad F on the left deck Press pad G on the left deck Press pad H on the left deck You get two pages of sizes: Page How you select it Default sizes A/B, C/D, E/F, G/H Page 1 Press BEAT JUMP 1, 2, 4, 8 beats Page 2 Hold SHIFT , press BEAT JUMP , let go of SHIFT 16, 32, 64, 128 beats (4, 8, 16, 32 bars) Page 1 Press BEAT JUMP . With the default sizes the pairs A/B, C/D, E/F and G/H jump 1, 2, 4 and 8 beats. The first pad of a pair jumps back, the second forward. Page 2 Hold SHIFT , press BEAT JUMP , let go of SHIFT . The pairs jump 16, 32, 64 and 128 beats, and the pads light warm red and amber. With a loop on With a loop on, the loop moves by the jump instead. Press BEAT JUMP for page 1, or SHIFT + BEAT JUMP for page 2. Let go of SHIFT . Press a pad. The first pad of a pair jumps back, the second forward. Each deck remembers its own page. Choosing another pad mode and coming back with BEAT JUMP gives page 1 again. On page 2 the pads light warm red and amber, so you can see which page you are on. SHIFT + pad keeps its stock job on decks 1 and 2.

manual:85ad9cb238f9c9e36b41.source: Open MODS > PLAY > BEAT JUMP PADS. The editor shows the pads as they sit on the deck: A to D on top, E to H below. Press MENU Tap PLAY Tap BEAT JUMP PADS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to PAGE 2 and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to PAGE 1 and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to PAGE 1: MY SIZES and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to PAGE 2 and push it Editing page 2. Pads A and B are selected and jump 16 beats. PAGE 1 Edit the sizes BEAT JUMP gives. PAGE 2 Edit the sizes SHIFT + BEAT JUMP gives. The filled tab is the page you are editing. PAGE 1: STOCK or MY SIZES STOCK keeps the player's own 1, 2, 4 and 8 beats on page 1. MY SIZES uses yours. Page 2 always uses yours. Pad pair Two pads with one size. The left pad jumps back, the right pad forward. The selected pair has a light outline. Beats The size in beats. Bars The same size in bars. 4 beats make 1 bar. Readout The selected pair and its size. Sizes Tap a size to give it to the selected pair. The filled size is the current one. Dock What the highlighted control does. Works on Beat jump works on all four decks. Choose PAGE 1 or PAGE 2. For page 1, choose PAGE 1: MY SIZES. With STOCK, page 1 keeps the player's own sizes. Tap a pad in the pair you want to change. Tap a size in the row along the bottom. Without the touch screen, turn the rotary selector to a pair, push it, then turn to step the size. It stops at the smallest and largest size. Push or press BACK when you are done. Sizes you can choose Beats 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 Bars 1/4, 1/2, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 The sizes apply to every deck. UTILITY's own beat jump setting is separate and does not change them. Setting Choices Default PAGE 1 STOCK, MY SIZES MY SIZES Page 1 A/B, C/D, E/F, G/H 1 to 256 beats 1, 2, 4, 8 beats Page 2 A/B, C/D, E/F, G/H 1 to 256 beats 16, 32, 64, 128 beats

manual:830f25a42ed930bbd3c5.source: A jump the deck cannot make does nothing else. XZ Mods never silently shortens the selected distance. The screen shows why: Press BEAT JUMP on the left deck Press pad A on the left deck Notice Deck What it means JUMP UNAVAILABLE: TRACK EDGE, BUFFER OR DECK STATE 1 or 2 The player refused the jump. It would pass the start or end of the track, or the deck cannot jump right now. JUMP UNAVAILABLE: BEFORE TRACK START 3 or 4 The jump would land before the start of the track. JUMP UNAVAILABLE: AFTER TRACK END 3 or 4 The jump would land after the end of the track. JUMP UNAVAILABLE: LOOP MOVE OUT OF TRACK 3 or 4 Moving the loop would push it past the start or end. JUMP UNAVAILABLE: NO BEAT GRID OR BPM 3 or 4 The track's beat grid is damaged, so beats can't be counted. Analyse it again in your DJ software.

manual:aeaa63ab20aee5835fc3.source: Both change what a hot cue pad does in HOT CUE mode. Turn them on in MODS > PLAY. Both are off by default, and each works on its own. Press MENU Tap PLAY Tap GATE CUE Tap SMART CUE Tap CLOSE Press HOT CUE on the left deck Press pad A on the left deck Feature What a hot cue pad does GATE CUE The track plays from the hot cue only while you hold the pad. Let go and it jumps back to the hot cue and pauses. Use it to stab hot cues like samples. Press PLAY/PAUSE while you hold the pad to keep playing after you let go. SMART CUE Calling a hot cue also moves the CUE point there, so CUE takes you back to the last hot cue you used. Recording a new hot cue does not move it. Gate cue and smart cue work on all four decks. On decks 1 and 2 they need the cue engine; see below.

manual:8231e1ef5d9b2141a68a.source: When the cue engine has not reported on a deck, MODS shows a short setup instead of the switch. It checks the feature on a loaded USB track in four steps: detect, choose deck, enable and test. Press MENU Tap PLAY Tap SET UP GATE CUE Tap DETECT FEATURE Tap DETECT FEATURE Tap USE SELECTED DECK Tap ENABLE FEATURE Tap I TESTED IT / DONE The setup page at its first step, checking gate cue. For smart cue it reads SMART CUE. Feature The feature this setup checks. Steps The four steps. The button at the bottom always runs the next one. Deck Choose deck 1 or deck 2. What to do The instruction for the current step. Track The track loaded on the chosen deck. Status FEATURE DETECTED, or what to do when it is missing. Next step Runs the step. Missing support keeps its reason on the screen. Load a track from USB on deck 1 or deck 2. Press DETECT FEATURE. Choose the deck, then enable the feature. Close MODS and test it: hold and release a hot cue for gate cue, or call a hot cue and check that the cue point follows for smart cue. Reopen the setup and confirm. If the status still asks you to load a USB track while one is loaded, prepare the USB again with the current XZ Mods app .

manual:13c8352d10cbee0ccc94.source: XZ Mods can move the key of any deck a semitone at a time, and match a deck's key to the master deck with KEY SYNC. The master can be any deck, 1 to 4. The key display then shows the key the track plays in now. Press MENU Tap PLAY Tap KEYS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press SYNC on the left deck

manual:45e0a7c1eedd7d0e240e.source: Load tracks with analysed keys, and make the deck you want to match to the tempo master. Hold SHIFT and press SYNC on the deck you want to move. On a side that drives deck 3 or 4, this moves that deck. The deck shifts to a key that fits the master deck and MASTER TEMPO turns on. A notice shows the new key and the master deck, with RELATIVE KEY when it matches the relative major or minor. To end KEY SYNC, press SHIFT + SYNC again, or press MASTER TEMPO . Both return the deck to its own key and put MASTER TEMPO back the way it was. After that, MASTER TEMPO works as on a stock player. KEY SYNC changes the key only. The tempo, SYNC and the master deck stay as they were. All four decks can hold key shifts and KEY SYNC together. Before starting a new shift on deck 3 or 4, the player checks its measured audio workload. If there is too little headroom, it shows KEY SHIFT REFUSED: AUDIO LOAD TOO HIGH and leaves the current keys unchanged. Shifts already in use keep running. SYSTEM READOUT shows render times and the number of active key shifters. If KEY SYNC cannot work, a notice or the deck's key display shows why for a few seconds: Message What to do KEY ENGINE OFF: SET UP KEYS This USB loader has no key engine. Open MODS > PLAY > KEYS and press SET UP KEYS, or prepare the USB again with the current XZ Mods app. DECK 1 TRACK HAS NO KEY (or another deck) The track on this deck has no analysed key. Analyse it in your DJ software. LOAD AN ANALYZED TRACK / SET UP KEYS The deck has no track with an analysed key. Load one. LOAD A KEYED TRACK ON DECK 2 (or another deck) The master deck has no track with an analysed key. THIS DECK IS MASTER, MAKE DECK 2 MASTER FIRST The deck you pressed is the master, so there is nothing to match. Make another deck the master. On the KEYS page the master deck has no KEY SYNC button and says it is the master. SELECT ONE LOCAL MASTER / SET UP KEYS No deck on this player is the tempo master. Press MASTER on the deck to match to. VERIFY MASTER PLAYING KEY / SET UP KEYS The master deck's playing key is not known yet. Let it play a moment, then try again. MASTER CHANGED / RETRY KEY SYNC, TRACK CHANGED / RETRY KEY CONTROL The master or the track changed before the key moved. Press again. KEY SHIFT REFUSED: AUDIO LOAD TOO HIGH Measured audio work leaves too little headroom for a new shift. Existing shifts keep running. Check SYSTEM READOUT and retry when the load falls. SHIFT OUT OF RANGE, KEY RANGE IS -12 TO +12 SEMITONES The key that fits is further away than the deck can shift. EMERGENCY LOOP / LOAD NEXT TRACK The deck lost its track and loops. Load another track first.

manual:92151a2c998e307e4054.source: MODS > PLAY > KEYS does the same from the screen, and adds key shift by semitones. On the play screen, tapping a deck's key opens the same controls for that deck. Press MENU Tap PLAY Tap KEYS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY UP and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY DOWN and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to RESET and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY SYNC and push it The KEYS page for deck 1 with the key engine ready. The deck is in its own key. Deck Choose deck 1, 2, 3 or 4. Where there is room, a tab adds USB DECK for decks 1 and 2 and SOFTWARE for decks 3 and 4. KEY DOWN Lowers the deck's key one semitone. RESET Shows the current shift. Press it to return the deck to its own key. KEY UP Raises the deck's key one semitone. KEY SYNC Shifts the deck to a key that fits the master deck, as SHIFT + SYNC does. Deck keys Each deck's own key, the key it plays in now, the cents and SYNC or MASTER. The rows are empty in this picture. Works on Key shift and KEY SYNC work on all four decks. With MASTER TEMPO on, the key holds while the tempo moves. Without it, the tempo changes the key too, and the key display shows that. When the key engine has not reported, the buttons show an amber dot, the dock says NOT READY and SET UP KEYS appears. It opens a short setup that checks the key engine and the chosen deck's track, and ends with a live test: The KEYS page before the key engine reports, with SET UP KEYS The KEYS page before the key engine reports, with SET UP KEYS

manual:224a882e067c762010a0.source: In MODERN each deck's panel beside its waveform shows its key. With PLAYING KEY on, the big key is the key the track plays in now, after tempo and key shift. Deck 2 holds KEY SYNC: it plays Bb minor, moved up from its own A minor, 12 cents sharp. Key panel KEY SYNC, the key the deck plays in now, the cents left over and the track's own key. Deck in its own key Deck 1 plays in its own key, so the panel shows only KEY and the key. MT MASTER TEMPO. It blinks while KEY SYNC holds on that deck. Part of the key panel Meaning KEY SYNC KEY SYNC holds on this deck. The big key The key the deck plays in now. Green or amber compares it with the master deck's key; see Key and KEY SYNC . +12¢ Cents between the playing key and the nearest semitone. ORIGINAL The track's own key, shown when the playing key differs. ▲1 The key shift in semitones, on older USB loaders that do not report the analysed key. KEY SYNC with the MT lamp in the dark half of its blink With MASTER TEMPO off, +2.20 % tempo lifts A minor by 38 cents With MASTER TEMPO off and +6.10 % tempo, the track plays in Bb minor Keys in WHEEL notation, deck 1 shifted down two semitones An older USB loader shows the key and its shift step only No key on deck 1, and a key name too long for the panel The top bar lamps and QUANTIZE lamps hidden The same, with BEAT FX on

manual:a9094599b281c7c46f89.source: In CLASSIC, XZ Mods draws the playing key where the player shows its beat countdown, under the key: What you see Meaning KEY and a key The track plays in its own key. TRACK KEY Deck 3 or 4 shows the track's own key until it reports the key it plays in. Own key ▸ playing key The tempo or a key shift moved the key. SYNC KEY SYNC holds on this deck. The tile turns green while the key matches the master. MASTER This deck is the master that KEY SYNC matches to. +12c in amber Cents between the playing key and the nearest semitone. Green or amber key The playing key compared with the master deck's key, as KEY MATCH COLOURS sets it. A message in red KEY SYNC could not work; see the table above.

manual:8679816e8c4cea00a59b.source: PLAYING KEY is on by default. Turn it off in MODS > SCREEN to show the track's own key instead. In CLASSIC, off brings the beat countdown back. Key notation (AS ON THE USB, MUSICAL or WHEEL) is set on the same page; see Screen, interfaces and themes . Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap PLAYING KEY Tap PLAYING KEY Tap KEY MATCH COLOURS Tap KEY BEFORE TITLE Tap CLOSE Decks 3 and 4 show their playing key too, after tempo and key shift. Until a software deck reports it, the deck shows the track's own key.

manual:f775c9c4d068f91b0a63.source: RAM TRACKS copies the track on a deck into the player's memory. The deck then plays from memory, so it keeps playing if the music USB goes out. It works on all four decks. Decks 3 and 4 need the loopback cable connected to start a copy. Press MENU Tap PLAY Tap RAM TRACKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to LOAD TRACK INTO RAM and push it Deck 1 on a USB loader without the RAM engine. Deck Choose deck 1, 2, 3 or 4. State The deck and the state of its RAM copy. Source The track loaded on that deck, or what to do next. Progress How much of the track is copied, in MiB. Memory How much of the 128 MiB the copies use, prepared stems apart, then each deck's copy and state. Action The one next step for this state: set up, choose a track, load, cancel, retry or release. Scope What RAM holds for this deck. COPIES AUDIO / STEMS STAY ON USB means only the original audio goes into RAM. Reason Why the feature is not available. Here the RAM engine is missing. Load a track from USB on the deck. Open MODS > PLAY > RAM TRACKS and choose that deck. Press LOAD TRACK INTO RAM. Keep the USB connected while it copies. Wait for ORIGINAL AUDIO IN RAM. A track that plays is also copied on its own when there is room. CANCEL COPY or RELEASE RAM COPY stops that for the loaded track. State Button What it means RAM ENGINE NOT DETECTED SET UP RAM TRACKS This USB loader has no RAM engine, or it has not reported yet. The setup checks the engine. If it stays, prepare the USB again with the current XZ Mods app. LOOPBACK CABLE NOT CONNECTED SET UP FOUR DECKS Deck 3 or 4 is chosen and decks 3 and 4 are not running. The button opens 4 DECKS. NOT IN RAM LOAD TRACK INTO RAM The deck plays from USB. COPYING TO RAM CANCEL COPY The copy is running. Cancel leaves the track playing from USB. ORIGINAL AUDIO IN RAM RELEASE RAM COPY The deck plays from memory. Release frees the memory and needs the USB still connected. COPY FAILED RETRY LOAD INTO RAM The track keeps playing from USB. Retry; if it fails again, load the track again from USB. USB OUT / RAM COPY ONLY BACK TO PLAY The USB is out and the deck plays from memory. The play screen says so in the deck's lane; see below . Load another track to release the copy. When a copy does not fit, the page says why and offers the next step: Message What to do This file exceeds the 64 MiB RAM limit. Press CHOOSE ANOTHER TRACK. Other RAM tracks leave too little space for this file. Press MANAGE RAM TRACKS, choose a deck with a copy and release it. Free RAM cannot keep the 64 MiB safety reserve. Release another copy the same way. One track per deck. Each file can be up to 64 MiB, and all four decks together up to 128 MiB. The player always keeps 64 MiB of its memory free. RAM TRACKS copies the original audio. On decks 1 and 2, the line under the action button says what else is held; see the table below. On decks 3 and 4 the waveform, beat grid and cues already loaded stay with the copy when the USB goes out. Cues you change then are kept for the session and not written to a USB. If the loopback cable goes out, decks 3 and 4 keep their copies and pause, as they do without RAM. They do not start again on their own when the cable returns. Loading another track on the deck drops its RAM copy.

manual:83409e3bde25ba13362c.source: Press BROWSE Push ROTARY SELECTOR Press LOAD 1 NOT IN RAM The deck plays from USB. COPYING TO RAM Press LOAD TRACK INTO RAM. Keep the USB connected while it copies. ORIGINAL AUDIO IN RAM The deck plays from memory. USB OUT / RAM COPY ONLY The music USB goes out and the deck plays on from memory. A teal card, WHOLE TRACK IN RAM · PLAYABLE, takes the waveform's place and says how to get it back. A deck with its whole track in RAM keeps playing when the music USB goes out. The waveform was read from the USB, so the deck's lane cannot draw it any more. A teal card takes its place: WHOLE TRACK IN RAM · PLAYABLE , and under it how to get the waveform back. Everything else about the deck stays on screen: title and artist, time and remain, BPM, tempo, key, the lamps, the hot cues and the playhead. 2 DECKS: deck 1 plays from RAM. Deck 2 is unchanged Both decks play from RAM 4 DECKS: decks 2 and 4 play from RAM MIXER order: the card stays with its deck Deck 1 plays from RAM after the USB went out. The stem rows, the deck column and the deck strip stay as the player shows them. RAM card The deck plays its whole track from RAM. The second line says how to get the waveform back. To get the waveform back, reinsert the same USB or insert another, then load a track from it. The card goes as soon as the deck has a waveform to draw again. Loading a track also ends the deck's RAM copy, as it always does. On decks 3 and 4 the waveform loaded before the USB went out stays, so the card shows there only if the waveform had not loaded yet. Line under the button, decks 1 and 2 What it means COPIES AUDIO / STEMS STAY ON USB No copy yet. RAM TRACKS copies the audio, not the stems. AUDIO IN RAM / STEMS NEED USB The audio is in RAM. The stems still read the USB. AUDIO + STEMS IN RAM / WAVES KEPT The deck's prepared stems are held in RAM as well, and the loaded waveforms stay. Experimental Playing on from RAM after the USB goes out has not been confirmed on a player yet. Keep the USB in during a set.

manual:9606d9d95cce42f97769.source: On decks 1 and 2, quantize is the player's own: DECK QUANTIZE and UTILITY work as on a stock player. In MODERN each deck shows its QUANTIZE lamp and beat value above its time. You can hide them in MODS > SCREEN > LAMPS AND TITLES. Press DECK QUANTIZE Press DECK QUANTIZE While a side drives deck 3 or 4: Key Action DECK QUANTIZE Switches quantize for every deck. Decks 1 and 2 switch through the player as before. SHIFT + DECK QUANTIZE Switches quantize only for the deck of that side. With quantize on, decks 3 and 4 put cue points, loop in and out, hot cues and beat and slip loops on the beat grid, at a one-beat value. SYNC then also locks the deck to the master's beat. Four decks has the rest of what decks 3 and 4 do.

manual:18ef05b1a88bbaedd7c3.source: Four decks adds two software players, DECK 3 and DECK 4, to the XDJ-XZ's own DECK 1 and DECK 2. You hear them on mixer channels CH3 and CH4. A short USB cable from the back of the player to a top USB port carries their sound into the mixer: it leaves through a top USB port and comes back in at the rear USB socket, where a computer with DJ software would connect. The physical controls switch between decks with the same presses DJ software uses on the XDJ-XZ. Decks 3 and 4 Decks 3 and 4 are software players. They run inside the player, beside decks 1 and 2. Top USB Their sound leaves the player through the top USB port the cable is in, USB 1 or USB 2. Loopback cable The loopback cable carries it over the back edge of the player. Rear USB It comes back in at the rear USB socket, where a computer with DJ software would connect. CH3 and CH4 With their input switches on USB, mixer channels CH3 and CH4 play decks 3 and 4. Experimental Four decks is experimental in this version. Test it with your own tracks before a set, keep the music stick connected, and keep a two-deck plan ready.

manual:c2df73871e97d61e9c94.source: The loopback cable : a USB cable with a USB-B plug on one end and a USB-A plug on the other, the kind a printer uses. For tracks, a music stick in the other top USB port, or music sticks on one USB 2.0 hub in that port. Decks 3 and 4 can start before you insert any music. Decks 1 and 2 stopped or paused while decks 3 and 4 start. Once they run, you can play all four decks. CH3 and CH4 on the mixer set to USB so you hear decks 3 and 4. The cable goes directly from the rear USB socket to either USB 1 or USB 2 on top. Put music in the other top port. The picture uses USB 1 as an example; both arrangements work. One USB-B to USB-A cable runs from the rear USB socket over the back edge into a top USB port; the picture shows USB 1. No computer is involved.

manual:2897fa118e907664e0da.source: Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Tap RESCAN Stop or pause decks 1 and 2. Choose either top USB port for the loopback cable. Leave the other port for music. Plug the USB-B end of the loopback cable into the rear USB socket . Plug the USB-A end directly into your chosen top port, USB 1 or USB 2 . Set the CH3 and CH4 input switches to USB . Tap DECKS at the top of the play screen and choose one of the 4 DECKS pictures, or open MODS and choose 4 DECKS . Wait for DECKS 3 AND 4 ARE READY . The card in the lanes of decks 3 and 4 tells you each step it is waiting for. Press SHIFT twice on the left side to play deck 3, or on the right side to play deck 4. Decks 3 and 4 start as soon as the cable is in, even when decks 1 and 2 have no tracks loaded. You can leave the cable connected before starting the USB loader. No RESCAN is needed. Decks 1 and 2 must be stopped or paused while the route starts. RESCAN checks at once if you want to check again. After a disconnection, plug the cable back into either top port. Decks 3 and 4 come back once decks 1 and 2 are stopped or paused; the card says when it is waiting for that. No restart of the USB loader is needed, also when you move the cable to the other port. Note The XZ Mods app shows steps 2 to 5 with an animation of the cable while it writes your USB and when it is done. You set four decks up at the player, not in the app. Tip You can choose a four-deck view before you plug in the cable. Decks 3 and 4 then show a card with the cable steps and their current state, and decks 1 and 2 keep playing as usual.

manual:d83684b9ca0435a401d2.source: Once the USB loader is running, you can bring up decks 3 and 4 with only the loopback cable connected. Insert music later in the other top port. Starting the audio route does not load a track. To connect several music sticks, put one high-speed USB 2.0 hub in the top port opposite the loopback cable. Stop or pause decks 1 and 2 while a newly connected hub starts. Connect the sticks to that hub and choose the sources the player makes available. The hub does not add more decks or source buttons. Connect the loopback cable directly to the player, never through the music hub. Do not connect a second hub behind the first. Check that your hub and drives have enough power; use the hub's own power supply if it has one. Keep any drive that holds a playing track connected.

manual:015d329133a9c1c4c765.source: MODS > 4 DECKS shows the cable's state, lets you choose the deck view, and lists what works on each deck. Press MENU Tap 4 DECKS Tap 4 DECKS Tap 4 DECKS Tap 2 DECKS The 4 DECKS page before the cable is plugged in. In this picture the key and RAM engines have not reported yet, so KEY SYNC has no tick on decks 1 and 2 and RAM TRACKS none on any deck. Cable picture Shows USB 1 as an example; USB 2 works too. The picture explains the connections, not which port is currently occupied. State Where four decks stand now, with one sentence on what happens next. The states are listed under The card in every state . RESCAN Checks the cable and the audio route now. Reads TRY AGAIN after a failed start and SCANNING while a check runs. DECK VIEW 2 DECKS, 4 DECKS in number order (1 2 3 4) or 4 DECKS in mixer order (3 1 2 4). The highlighted box is the saved view. Deck columns One column per deck, in mixer order 3 1 2 4, the same on both halves of the grid. Feature row A tick means the feature works on that deck. A dash means it does not. Turn the encoder onto a row and the dock says why. Dock Explains the highlighted control or row. Save state Confirms that your deck view is saved to the USB. The HOME page shows the same state on the 4 DECKS card. When four decks need you (no cable found, a failed start, a lost connection, or no four-deck engine on the USB loader) HOME also shows SET UP FOUR DECKS , which opens this page. If the USB loader has no four-deck engine, the page says so and offers CHECK INSTALLED ENGINE . Rebuild the USB loader in the XZ Mods app , restart the player with it, then press CHECK INSTALLED ENGINE . HOME status line What it means Not connected No loopback cable found yet. Looking for the cable A check is running now. Starting decks 3 and 4 The cable is found and the software players are starting, or they wait for decks 1 and 2 to stop. Ready, 2 decks shown Decks 3 and 4 run. The play screen shows two decks. Ready, 4 decks shown Decks 3 and 4 run. The play screen shows four decks. Could not start The start failed. The 4 DECKS page says why. Disconnected The cable was unplugged or lost power. Not available on this player The software players are not running in this build.

manual:53c04b18dbe7eadfe618.source: While decks 3 and 4 are not running, a four-deck view puts a card in their lanes. The card shows the cable steps, the state, and the buttons you need. Decks 1 and 2 stay live above it. In number order the card fills the lanes of decks 3 and 4 under decks 1 and 2. In mixer order it splits into a strip above deck 1 and a strip below deck 2. Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Four decks in number order before the cable is plugged in. CLASSIC draws the same card in its own colours, with shorter sentences. Cable picture USB 1 is the illustrated example; USB 2 works too. The picture moves for a minute after the card appears or your last input, then rests. Steps The two things to do: connect the cable, and set the CH3 and CH4 input switches to USB. State The state's title and what happens next. RESCAN Checks for the cable now. TWO DECKS Goes back to the two-deck view. Decks 3 and 4 keep trying in the background. Deck 3 tag NOT CONNECTED while deck 3 is not running. Deck 3 channel The bottom channel of deck 3 waits for the loopback cable. DECKS button Shows the current view. The small amber dot means decks 3 and 4 are not connected. You can drive the card with the encoder. While the card shows, push the encoder to highlight RESCAN , turn it to move between the card's buttons and the DECKS button, and push again to press. BACK , or six seconds without input, gives the encoder back to the player. Card title What it means What to do NO CABLE FOUND The XZ does not see the loopback cable. Connect the cable directly to either top port. Music goes in the other port and is optional for startup. Press RESCAN to check at once. LOOKING FOR THE CABLE... A check runs now. The button reads SCANNING . Wait a moment. STARTING DECKS 3 AND 4 The cable is found and the audio input is starting. Wait a few seconds. The card's sentence says which step is running. STOP DECKS 1 AND 2 Decks 3 and 4 or a newly connected music hub wait for decks 1 and 2 to stop. Stop or pause decks 1 and 2. The card changes by itself. COULD NOT START DECKS 3 AND 4 The start failed. The picture marks the type of connection that needs attention: top USB, cable, rear socket or CH3/CH4 switches. The drawn port is an example. Read the sentence, fix that part, then press TRY AGAIN . It tries the start again, and restarts the four-deck helper if it had stopped. DECKS 3 AND 4 DISCONNECTED The cable was unplugged or lost power while decks 3 and 4 ran. Plug the cable back into either top port. Press RESCAN to check at once. FOUR DECKS ARE NOT AVAILABLE The software players are not running in this build. Decks 1 and 2 play as usual. Press TWO DECKS . DECKS 3 AND 4 ARE READY The route came up. The card turns green, then wipes away. Press SHIFT twice on a side to play deck 3 or 4. LOOKING FOR THE CABLE. A check is running, so the button reads SCANNING STARTING DECKS 3 AND 4. The cable is found and the audio input is starting STOP DECKS 1 AND 2, in mixer order. The card splits into two strips COULD NOT START. The failed part is marked in red and the button reads TRY AGAIN DECKS 3 AND 4 DISCONNECTED. The cable went away while decks 3 and 4 ran FOUR DECKS ARE NOT AVAILABLE. Only TWO DECKS is offered NO CABLE FOUND in mixer order The encoder on the card. RESCAN is highlighted DECKS 3 AND 4 ARE READY. The card turns green The card wipes away and decks 3 and 4 appear When the route comes up, a banner says DECKS 3 AND 4 ARE READY for a few seconds. If the play screen shows two decks at that moment, the banner says DECKS 3 AND 4 ARE READY. TAP DECKS AT THE TOP FOR FOUR DECKS. The view does not change by itself.

manual:96e2487b0a57718419e0.source: The player sees the loopback cable as a USB hub. When you plug it in, the player raises its own warning E-8307: HUBS ARE NOT SUPPORTED and would keep it up while the cable stays in. That is not an error. XZ Mods removes the warning window as soon as the player draws it, so it does not stay on screen in MODERN, MODS or CLASSIC, whether four decks are on or not. A music hub the player refuses raises the same warning, and XZ Mods removes it too. If the sticks on a music hub do not appear, stop or pause decks 1 and 2 with the loopback cable connected and let the music hub finish connecting. A hub in the loopback port, a second hub behind the first, or a hub that does not support high-speed USB 2.0 is not supported. Remove that hub or connect the music stick directly.

manual:59f910eeda9a22e72c29.source: DECK VIEW chooses what the play screen shows. It changes neither the sound, the mixer channels, nor which deck a side controls. Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Tap DECKS Press BACK DECK VIEW Waveform lanes, top to bottom Bottom channels 2 DECKS (the default) The two decks the sides control The same two decks 4 DECKS, number order 1 2 3 4 1, 2, 3, 4 3, 1, 2, 4 4 DECKS, mixer order 3 1 2 4 3, 1, 2, 4 3, 1, 2, 4 The bottom channels always follow the mixer, left to right: CH3, CH1, CH2, CH4. Mixer order puts the lanes in the same order, top to bottom. Each lane and each channel carries its deck's number in a badge, so you can always tell which deck is which. Decks 1 and 2 have a white number on grey. Decks 3 and 4 have a black number on white, as on the jog displays. DECK VIEW is saved to the USB with your other settings. You can change it in five places, and they all change the same setting: the DECKS button at the top of the play screen; TWO DECKS on the card; MODS > SCREEN > DECK VIEW ; MODS > 4 DECKS > DECK VIEW ; the button above LINK , when you set it to DECK VIEW in MODS > PLAY > BUTTON ABOVE LINK . Each press then steps 2 DECKS, 4 DECKS in number order, 4 DECKS in mixer order.

manual:31d146b7cd44b61de7b1.source: The DECKS button is always at the top of the play screen in both interfaces. It names the decks on screen: DECKS 1 2 , DECKS 1234 , DECKS 3124 , or the pair the sides control in 2 DECKS, such as DECKS 3 2 . In MODERN it sits left of the INFO button. In CLASSIC it sits in the black space between VJ.TOOLS and the METRICS readout. Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Tap DECKS to open the picker. Tap a picture to choose it. DECKS button Opens and closes the picker. It shows the view now on screen. 2 DECKS The two decks the sides control, like the player itself. 4 DECKS, number order All four decks, lanes 1 2 3 4. 4 DECKS, mixer order All four decks, lanes 3 1 2 4, matching the mixer channels. Status LIKE THE PLAYER ITSELF for two decks. DECKS 3 AND 4 READY in green, or 3 AND 4 NOT CONNECTED in amber. A tap outside the picker, BACK , or six seconds without input closes it. The encoder also turns and pushes inside the open picker. 2 DECKS. The player's own two-deck screen with the DECKS button at the top 4 DECKS in number order with decks 3 and 4 ready 4 DECKS in mixer order. Lanes 3 1 2 4 over channels 3 1 2 4 2 DECKS with the left side on deck 3. The screen shows decks 3 and 2 2 DECKS when decks 3 and 4 come up. The banner says how to show four

manual:f61d639b92295cd2b955.source: The left controls play DECK 1 or DECK 3. The right controls play DECK 2 or DECK 4. Decks 3 and 4 must be ready. Press SHIFT on the left deck twice quickly Press SHIFT on the right deck twice quickly Press SHIFT twice quickly on a side to switch it. The left SHIFT switches between decks 1 and 3, the right SHIFT between decks 2 and 4. These are the presses the XDJ-XZ uses for DJ software. Or press SHORTCUT and tap the deck under DECK SELECT modern . After a switch the tempo fader does not jump. The deck you switched to keeps its tempo until you move the fader across that deck's value. The same holds when you switch back. In 2 DECKS the screen follows the sides. A side on deck 3 or 4 shows that deck's waveform, tag and channel, and the screen says where the side went for two seconds, for example LEFT: DECK 3 . In a four-deck view the lanes stay where they are, and a pale blue tag marks the decks the sides control. If decks 3 and 4 are not running, SHIFT pressed twice does not switch. The screen says DECK 3 AND 4 NEED THE CH3/CH4 ROUTE . If the route is lost while a side plays deck 3 or 4, both sides go back to decks 1 and 2 and the screen says DECK 3/4 ROUTE LOST . SHORTCUT with the left side on deck 3. DECK SELECT Each deck row has its switch. Tap 1 or 3 for the left side, 2 or 4 for the right side. CONTROL In the bottom strip, the decks the sides control carry CONTROL with an arrow. SHORTCUT with four decks before the software players report. No DECK SELECT yet DECK SELECT with both sides on decks 1 and 2 DECK SELECT with both sides on decks 3 and 4 The play screen with the left side on deck 3. Its tag and channel read CONTROL

manual:f9cde9e968c5d8791103.source: Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Tap LANE 3 Tap the screen Tap LANE 3 Tap STEMS HEADER Tap STEMS HEADER All four decks loaded and playing. DECKS button Shows DECKS 1234 or DECKS 3124. Tap it to change the view. Lane tag The deck's badge, source stick and the key it plays in now, in the key match colours. VINYL Whether VINYL is on for deck 3 or 4. Bottom channels The four decks in mixer order 3 1 2 4: time, tempo, range, BPM, hot cues and the whole-track overview. MASTER The tempo master. A software master reads 3/4 MASTER. SYNC What SYNC is doing. SYNC 3 means synced to deck 3, BPM 3 deck 3's tempo only, LIMIT a tempo out of reach. See SYNC on decks 3 and 4 . Tap a lane of deck 3 or 4 to open its detail panel. It shows the full pad bank, the deck's modes, what SYNC is doing and a whole-track overview you can touch to search. Tap the lane again, or CLOSE , to close it. Deck 3 is the deck the encoder and screen act on Decks 3 and 4 with no track loaded Deck 4 is the tempo master and plays a loop A software deck as master. Deck 3 reads 3/4 MASTER and deck 4 reads SYNC 3 SYNC states. Deck 3 reads BPM 1 and follows deck 1's tempo only. Deck 4 reads SYNC 3 and follows deck 3 Mixer order 3 1 2 4 ON AIR marks and NEEDLE LOCK, with the playhead on the left Long titles are cut short to fit A read error on deck 3. CANNOT READ THE TRACK, with CHOOSE TRACK GRID ADJUST on deck 4 GRID ADJUST on deck 4 with stem rows on decks 1 and 2 Stem buttons show in a half row under a deck's waveform, only for decks 1 and 2 and only while the deck's track has prepared stems. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems. A deck without stems shows no stem buttons and its waveform keeps the whole lane. STEMS in the top bar shows or hides the stem buttons on all four lanes: one tap hides them, the next shows them. The screen says STEM BUTTONS HIDDEN or STEM BUTTONS SHOWN , and STEMS is lit while they show. Your 2 DECKS stem layout does not apply here and does not change. See Stems . Stem buttons on decks 1 and 2. STEMS is lit One tap of STEMS: the stem buttons are hidden and every waveform has its whole lane Deck 2's track has no prepared stems: no stem buttons, the whole lane BYPASS on deck 2

manual:60e83df13bcea8e3c3ea.source: CLASSIC keeps the player's own look and adds what four decks need. Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen Waveforms. The waveform area holds four narrower lanes, one per deck, in the order DECK VIEW chooses. Decks 3 and 4 draw the same 3-band waveform with beat ticks, hot cue flags A to H, the cue point, loops and the playhead. Side column. The left column has one tag per lane. The tag of a deck a side controls is pale blue with LEFT or RIGHT. Decks 1 and 2 show the analysed key, the playing key and its cents. Decks 3 and 4 show their playing key and its cents the same way, TRACK KEY until they report it, or NOT CONNECTED and SEE THE CARD while they are not running. Bottom panel. Four channels in mixer order 3 1 2 4. Each shows the deck's title, time, QUANTIZE, tempo and range, AUTO CUE and MT, what SYNC follows, what the pads do, the BPM (orange with MASTER for the master deck) and the whole-track overview. A deck that is not connected shows a dim band with NOT CONNECTED and DECK n WAITS FOR THE LOOPBACK CABLE. Stem rows are not drawn while four decks show, because there is no room, and STEMS stays dark. Your stem layout comes back when you return to two decks. Pressing STEMS meanwhile changes nothing and says STEM BUTTONS SHOW IN 2 DECKS VIEW . 2 DECKS shows the decks the sides control. A side on deck 3 or 4 gets a whole half in the player's own style: its waveform, its side tag and its bottom panel. Tap a lane, side tag or channel title of deck 3 or 4 to open its detail panel. Touch the overview in the bottom channel to search the track. NEEDLE LOCK refuses a search while the deck plays.

manual:7f017d29991e0a3ea09a.source: LOAD on a side loads the highlighted track into the deck that side controls, deck 3 or deck 4 included. In CLASSIC this goes through the player's own browser. In MODERN, tap a track to see a LOAD chip with one cell per deck, then tap the deck number. See Browsing and loading for the rest. Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Press BROWSE Push ROTARY SELECTOR Tap TRACK ROW Tap LOAD DECK 3 A tapped track with its LOAD cells. LOAD Tap a deck number to load the track there. LOAD returns to the play screen. Target deck The blue cell is the deck the screen acts on now. Bottom strip The four decks in mixer order while you browse. Browsing with four decks. The bottom strip shows all four decks Browsing while the sides control decks 3 and 2 Deck 4 with no track. Not Loaded in the strip The play screen after a load After LOAD on the left side. The track went to the left side's deck After LOAD on the right side. The track went to the right side's deck Decks 3 and 4 cannot load a track at a memory point from the CUE/LOOP LIST. The screen says DECK 3 AND 4 CANNOT LOAD AT A MEMORY POINT .

manual:8b982a16bcc04e478658.source: INFO has a tab for each deck. SOURCE shows which decks use each stick. UTILITY and the other full screens keep a compact strip of all four decks at the bottom. Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Press INFO Tap the screen Tap the screen Press BACK Open SOURCE ( BACK at the top of a list) Press BACK Hold MENU for a second Press BACK INFO with tabs DECK 1 to DECK 4 SOURCE. Decks 1 and 2 on USB 1, decks 3 and 4 on USB 2 UTILITY with the four-deck strip at the bottom INFO tabs named PLAYER 3 and PLAYER 4 are other players on the LINK network, not decks 3 and 4 A LINK player with no track loaded

manual:15f3c6b94985a080c78d.source: Decks 3 and 4 are software players. They follow the player's own controls on the side that controls them. MODS > 4 DECKS shows the current answer for each feature. Tap DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Press PLAY/PAUSE on the left deck Press CUE on the left deck Press PLAY/PAUSE on the left deck Press SYNC on the left deck Press DECK QUANTIZE on the left deck Press SYNC on the left deck Press MASTER on the left deck Press SYNC on the left deck Press PLAY/PAUSE on the left deck Press IN/CUE on the left deck Press OUT on the left deck Press RELOOP/EXIT on the left deck Feature Decks 1 and 2 Decks 3 and 4 Beat jump pads with your own sizes Yes Yes, the same sizes and both pages Gate cue and smart cue Yes Yes Waveform colours, key notation, titles Yes Yes Playing key Yes Yes Key sync and key shift Yes Yes. Both can shift together; new shifts check measured audio headroom. Stems Yes, with USB stems set up No. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems. RAM tracks Yes Yes, while the loopback cable is connected. See RAM tracks . On a side that controls deck 3 or 4, these controls work on that deck experimental : Control What it does on deck 3 or 4 PLAY/PAUSE , CUE Play and pause, back cue and cue audition. With VINYL on, pause brakes to a stop at the VINYL SPEED ADJUST rate. HOT CUE , BEAT LOOP , SLIP LOOP , BEAT JUMP Set the pad mode of the software deck. The native deck keeps its own mode. Pads Hot cues, beat loops, slip loops and beat jumps, as on decks 1 and 2. IN/CUE , OUT , RELOOP/EXIT Manual loops, loop adjustment with the jog, reloop and exit. SLIP , DIRECTION REV , VINYL Slip, reverse and vinyl mode. TEMPO RANGE , TEMPO RESET , MASTER TEMPO Tempo range up to WIDE, original speed, and key lock while the tempo moves. SYNC , MASTER Follow the master deck's tempo, and with QUANTIZE its beat. Make this deck the master. See SYNC on decks 3 and 4 . SHIFT + SYNC , MASTER TEMPO KEY SYNC to the master deck, and back to the deck's own key. See Keys and KEY SYNC . DECK QUANTIZE Cue, loop and hot cue points land on the beat. DECK QUANTIZE switches every deck. SHIFT + DECK QUANTIZE switches only this side's deck. MEMORY , DELETE , CUE/LOOP CALL Store, delete and call memory points. TRACK SEARCH , SEARCH Previous and next track, and fine search. With AUTO CUE on, the new track waits at its cue. Previous and next follow the list the track was loaded from in MODERN. After a CLASSIC load the deck shows NO SAVED TRACK ORDER, and TRACK SEARCH back returns to the cue. On decks 3 and 4, TRACK SEARCH respects AUTO CUE. With AUTO CUE on, a newly loaded track waits at its cue point. With AUTO CUE off, a deck that was playing continues with the new track; a paused deck stays paused. Hot cues and memory points you set on decks 3 and 4 are saved on the music stick for those decks only. Decks 1 and 2 and your DJ software do not see them, and the exported library stays unchanged.

manual:1384ad70e2788f6eb5ea.source: Press SYNC and the deck takes the master deck's BPM at once. The SYNC button stays lit for as long as SYNC is on. With QUANTIZE on and a beat grid on both tracks, the deck also locks to the master's beat. Press SYNC again to turn it off. Master Deck 1 is the tempo master. Deck 3 plays at its own tempo, with SYNC off. SYNC Press SYNC on deck 3. It takes the master's BPM at once and reads SYNC 1. With QUANTIZE on and a beat grid on both tracks, it also locks to the master's beat. Tempo only With QUANTIZE off, only the tempo follows, and deck 3 reads BPM 1. If the beats drift apart, press SYNC off and on again. With QUANTIZE on, every engage snaps to the nearest position at the selected beat value, even for a small drift. The beat value can be 1, 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 beat. With QUANTIZE off, only the tempo follows. The tempo follows even when the master or the synced deck is paused. If the beat position is available, the paused deck aligns once. If it is unavailable, alignment happens as soon as it can be read. Continuous beat lock resumes when both decks play. A pause, a jump, a loop or a new master never turns SYNC off. The deck follows again on its own, with no second press. Nudge the jog from the side to move the deck a little off the master's beat. SYNC stays on and the tempo stays matched. The deck keeps the new alignment, also when the master's tempo changes, and the SYNC button flashes. Nudge the master's jog from the side to move only the master. It stays master, and the synced decks keep their tempo and the new alignment. To line the beats up again, press SYNC off and on. The deck snaps to the nearest beat and the button lights steadily. Scratching on the platter top takes control of the deck. When you let go, QUANTIZE snaps it back to the beat. Press SYNC off and the deck keeps its position and the synced tempo. The tempo fader takes over once you move it to that tempo. The tempo fader does not move the deck while SYNC is on. The bottom channel, the lane and the detail panel say what SYNC is doing: Shown What it means SYNC 1 to SYNC 4 SYNC is on and follows that deck. BPM 1 to BPM 4 Only the tempo can follow that deck: QUANTIZE is off, a track has no beat grid, a loop is running, or the master's beat position is not available. MASTER This deck is the tempo master. 3/4 MASTER This deck is the master for decks 3 and 4 only. LIMIT The master's tempo is out of this deck's reach. The deck keeps its last tempo. EXT MASTER The master is another player on the LINK network, which decks 3 and 4 cannot follow. NO BPM The track has no BPM to sync with. Analyse it in your DJ software. The detail panel adds a line about the reason, for example: Detail panel What it means SYNC ON / FOLLOWING DECK 1 The deck follows deck 1. SYNC ON / TEMPO MATCHED, PAUSED / TEMPO MATCHED The tempo matches. The beat locks once both decks play. BPM SYNC / MASTER PAUSED, BPM SYNC / DECK PAUSED One of the two decks is paused. The tempo follows, and the beat locks once both play. BPM SYNC / NO BEAT GRID A track has no beat grid, so only the tempo follows. BPM SYNC / LOOP ACTIVE A loop is running, so only the tempo follows until it ends. BPM SYNC / BEAT POSITION UNAVAILABLE The master's beat position cannot be read, so only the tempo follows. BPM SYNC / QUANTIZE OFF QUANTIZE is off, so only the tempo follows. SYNC ON / JOG CONTROL You are nudging or scratching. SYNC picks up again when you let go. After a side nudge it keeps the new alignment. NO MASTER / TEMPO UNCHANGED No deck is master. The deck keeps its tempo and follows as soon as there is one. MASTER CLOCK UNAVAILABLE / LAST TEMPO RETAINED The master's tempo cannot be read right now. The deck keeps the last tempo. SYNC TEMPO LIMIT / LAST TEMPO RETAINED The master's tempo is out of reach. EXTERNAL MASTER / SYNC SOURCE UNAVAILABLE A LINK player is master. TRACK BPM UNAVAILABLE / SYNC ON The track has no BPM.

manual:4e181b80eec396c1a242.source: Decks 1 and 2 must be stopped or paused while decks 3 and 4 start. Keep the music stick connected while you play. Decks 3 and 4 read from it all the time. Decks 3 and 4 play WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3 and Ogg Vorbis files. AAC and M4A files do not play on decks 3 and 4. A deck 3 or 4 master reads MASTER when decks 1 and 2 can follow it too, and 3/4 MASTER when it drives decks 3 and 4 only. Press MASTER on a playing deck 3 or 4 and it is master at once. The MASTER buttons show the change. When you pause the master, MASTER passes at once to the next playing deck. A deck with SYNC on comes first. Otherwise after deck 3 comes deck 4, then decks 1 and 2. After deck 4 come decks 1 and 2, then deck 3. In VINYL mode MASTER passes when you press pause, while the deck slows down. When you pause a deck 1 or 2 master, a playing deck 3 or 4 takes MASTER at once. If the other of decks 1 and 2 is playing, MASTER goes to that deck instead, as with two decks. In VINYL mode, hold the master's platter top and MASTER passes to the other synced, playing deck after a moment. Load a new track on the master and MASTER passes to the other playing deck. The loading deck keeps SYNC on and plays its new track at the tempo the decks shared. A handover never changes the tempo. A master set by another player over LINK is never taken. Some lamps on the player do not yet light as they do for decks 1 and 2. The beat loop and slip loop pad colours are provisional. Four decks, the handover of MASTER between native and software decks, and scratching on decks 3 and 4 are experimental in this version. If something goes wrong, the card or the 4 DECKS page names the state. Messages and troubleshooting lists every notice.

manual:05f75481682cb0860f33.source: Press MENU on the play screen. A short press opens MODS wherever the player's own firmware has no job for MENU , and leaves the stock job alone everywhere else. Hold MENU to open the player's own UTILITY, exactly as on a stock XDJ-XZ. Press MENU Press MENU Press MENU Tap CLOSE Where you are Short press of MENU The MODS menu is open Closes MODS A game is on screen The game's own key The VJ.Tools view is on screen As before A menu, popup or dialog is open Works or closes the open menu A track list (browse, playlist, search, history) The sort menu or the track menu TAG LIST LIST MENU The play screen in GRID ADJUST The beat grid menu The play screen Opens MODS experimental The SOURCE screen Opens MODS experimental The track INFO screen Opens MODS experimental The SHORTCUT screen Opens MODS experimental The player's own UTILITY Closes UTILITY Any other screen The screen's own job Note Rows marked experimental follow the XDJ-XZ operating instructions but have not been checked on every firmware version yet. If a press does something different on your player, report it github.com/OpticMystic/XZ-Mods/issues . To leave MODS, press MENU again, tap CLOSE in the top right corner, or press BACK until you are back on the play screen. You can also open MODS from the MODS button at the top of the MODERN play screen, or from the button above LINK when you set it to MODS MENU in PLAY .

manual:a1da1285b6b396bb2e42.source: You can drive the whole menu with the rotary encoder, with touch, or with both. Press MENU Push ROTARY SELECTOR to choose PLAY Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to GATE CUE and push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to SMART CUE and push it Press BACK Control What it does in MODS Turn the encoder Moves the highlight to the next card, row or button Push the encoder Opens or changes the highlighted item BACK Goes up one level: from an open item to its page, then from a page to the section rail Tap Opens or changes whatever you tap The hints in the bottom right corner ( TURN MOVE · PUSH SELECT · BACK UP ) always show what the encoder and BACK will do next. Every page has the same frame. The section rail on the left lists HOME, PLAY, STEMS, SCREEN, 4 DECKS, CONNECT and EXTRAS. The dock along the bottom explains whatever is highlighted. On the right of the dock, WORKS ON shows which decks the highlighted feature works on, in mixer order 3 1 2 4. A dimmed number means the feature does not work on that deck, and a short amber line says why.

manual:78023cf6810b7fbd8b39.source: HOME is the first page. It shows one card for each section, with a one-line summary of what the section does and the current state of its most important setting, so you can see at a glance whether stems are ready or four decks are connected. Press MENU Tap HOME Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise Press BACK The HOME page with stems ready and four decks not connected yet. BACK Goes up one level. On HOME it closes MODS. Section rail Every section of MODS, top to bottom. Tap one, or turn the encoder while the rail is highlighted. Section card Opens that section. The highlighted card has a light outline. Status line The state of the section's main setting. Green means ready, amber means it needs you. Setup button Appears when a feature needs setting up, and starts a short guide for it. Dock Explains the highlighted item in plain words before you open it. Save state Confirms your changes are saved to the USB, or says why they cannot be. Encoder hints What turning, pushing and BACK will do right now. CLOSE Closes MODS and returns to where you were. Card Its status line shows PLAY Your beat jump sizes, page 1 then page 2 STEMS Not set up, Off, or On with the state of deck 1 and deck 2 SCREEN The interface, the waveform colours and the key notation 4 DECKS Not connected, Looking for the cable, Starting decks 3 and 4, Ready with the deck view, Could not start, Disconnected, or Not available on this player CONNECT Your DJ profile and its USB, and whether VJ.Tools is connected EXTRAS The games and how many USB apps are on the stick Two setup buttons can appear on HOME. SET UP USB STEMS opens the USB stems guide when the stem engine is not ready. SET UP FOUR DECKS opens 4 DECKS when no cable is found, a start failed, the cable was lost, or the USB loader has no four-deck engine.

manual:2dd82dab7ebf50c3afd8.source: PLAY changes what the pads and buttons do while you perform. Press MENU Tap PLAY Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise Press BACK BEAT JUMP PADS Your own beat jump distances for both pad pages. The row shows the sizes now in use. GATE CUE and SMART CUE Switch each cue trick on or off. A feature the player has not reported yet shows a SET UP button instead. KEYS and RAM TRACKS Open their own pages. BUTTON ABOVE LINK What the button above LINK does on a press, and with SHIFT. WORKS ON The decks the highlighted feature works on. Beat jump and performance features explains every item on this page.

manual:4ba8cc9ea7fd54980833.source: STEMS mutes vocals, harmonics and drums from the pads or the screen. Press MENU Tap STEMS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise Press BACK USB STEMS Switches stems from the USB on or off. Reads SET UP USB STEMS until the stem engine is ready. STEM PADS Which pad mode and pad bank the stems use. Stem buttons on screen Where the stem buttons sit on the play screen. Each picture is one layout. STEM COLOURS The colours of drums, harmonics and vocals. WORKS ON Only decks 1 and 2 are lit. The amber line under it says decks 3 and 4 have no stems. STEMS IN DJ SOFTWARE sets up stems for a computer playing through the player. MODERN adds a BYPASS BUTTON switch beside STEM COLOURS. Stems explains every item on this page.

manual:7dfd896506c76ee108f5.source: SCREEN sets how the play screen looks. Press MENU Tap SCREEN Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise Press BACK INTERFACE CLASSIC or MODERN. The picture shows each one. DECK VIEW 2 DECKS, 4 DECKS in number order, or 4 DECKS in mixer order. THEME The CLASSIC theme. In MODERN this place holds LAMPS AND TITLES instead. 3-BAND COLOURS A colour for the lows, mids and highs of the 3-BAND waveform. The squares show the colours in use. WAVEFORM COLOURS STOCK, 3-BAND or STEMS. MODERN adds RGB. KEY NOTATION AS ON THE USB, MUSICAL or WHEEL, each with an example key. Keys and the track list PLAYING KEY, KEY MATCH COLOURS, KEY BEFORE TITLE and TRACK LIST COLUMNS. SYSTEM READOUT CPU, memory and temperature on the top bar, on its own row at the bottom of the page. Screen, interfaces and themes explains every item on this page. DECK VIEW is explained in Four decks .

manual:fa6ef007b6166f0b3ff3.source: 4 DECKS plays decks 3 and 4 over the loopback cable experimental . Press MENU Tap 4 DECKS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise Press BACK Cable state Where four decks stand, and what happens next. RESCAN Checks the cable now. Reads TRY AGAIN after a failed start. DECK VIEW How many decks the play screen shows, and in what order. What works on each deck A tick for every deck a feature works on. Four decks explains the cable, every state and what decks 3 and 4 can do.

manual:d677319a46c96c8206bd.source: CONNECT links the player to you and to computers. Press MENU Tap CONNECT Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise Press BACK DJ PROFILE Your DJ name and logo from the USB, for VJ screens. VJ.TOOLS Lets VJ.Tools on a computer connect, and shows its picture instead of the play screen. NETWORK The network adapter and address, applied for this start of the player. UPDATES Signed updates over the network. An update becomes active at the next start. Connect and DJ profiles explains every page here.

manual:25b5cfe8739b91290fb1.source: Press MENU Tap EXTRAS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise Press BACK GAMES Doom, Chex Quest, Beat Arcade, Wave Rider, Rhythm Lab and Static Surfer. The music keeps playing. USB APPS Apps for the XZ from the USB. REPORT AN ISSUE Sends a problem, a question or an idea, in three presses. ABOUT XZ MODS Credits, links and support. Extras explains every page here.

manual:b8f013ad4fd5b209c224.source: MENU held opens the player's own UTILITY: quantize, auto cue, play mode, the display and the other stock settings. Hold MENU for a second Push ROTARY SELECTOR Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it Press BACK In CLASSIC you see the player's own UTILITY screen, unchanged. In MODERN, XZ Mods draws UTILITY in the MODERN look. It is the same list of stock settings, in the stock order. In MODERN, MODS also has a UTILITY cell at the bottom of the section rail. It closes MODS and opens UTILITY. Until MODERN has read the player's settings, it reads NOT READY.

manual:37331479a07776c6f262.source: Press SHORTCUT Tap the screen Tap the screen UTILITY in MODERN, open on its first setting. UTILITY STOCK The player's own settings. On the player, the rail lists the MODS sections below it, and each one opens MODS on that section. Group DJ SETTING, DISPLAY (LCD), MIXER, SYSTEM and INFO, as on the player. Lock XZ Mods shows this setting but cannot change it here. The help says why. Current value A locked setting shows its value without choice buttons. Writable settings open a list of choices. Help What the setting does and why it is read-only here, or what a writable choice means. Version The player's firmware version. Deck strip Decks 1 and 2 stay in view while you change settings. Turn the encoder to move through the settings. On a writable row, push to open its choices, turn to pick one and push to set it. A locked row stays in the list and shows a read-only value and explanation. BACK goes back to the list. MENU or X closes UTILITY. A lock next to a setting comes with one of these notes: Note What it means PLAYER CONTROLLED The player sets this itself. XZ Mods only shows it. FIRMWARE LIMIT XZ Mods cannot read or set it on this firmware version. READ-ONLY BUILD A RAM trial shows settings but changes none. Start from the USB loader to change them. READ ONLY HERE XZ Mods shows this setting but cannot change it here. Pushing a locked setting does nothing. A setting highlighted in the list The choices open. Turn and push to set one A setting XZ Mods can change, its choices open A locked setting further down. Its help says it is read only here The end of the list. MIXER, SYSTEM and VERSION No. Before the version is read. TIME MODE first, then the display settings UTILITY on its DJ SETTING and DISPLAY (LCD) groups Before the decks report. The deck strip shows dashes SETTINGS NOT AVAILABLE HERE when the settings cannot be read UTILITY with four decks. A compact strip of all four decks

manual:f71f9594ae32d097deca.source: MY SETTINGS shows the player settings saved on a USB stick, and the DJ profiles on it. In MODERN, open the stick in browse, highlight the category rail on the left, and press MENU . Press BROWSE Press MENU Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen Tap the screen MY SETTINGS for USB 1 while deck 1 plays. MY SETTINGS The panel for the stick you browse. X closes it. Stick The stick whose settings these are: USB 1, USB 2, or a LINK player's USB. LOAD TO DECK Applies the settings saved on the stick to the active deck. Reads PAUSE DECK 1 TO LOAD while that deck plays. SAVE TO USB 1 Saves the player's current settings to the stick, replacing the ones there. Push once to arm it, then again to save. DJ PROFILE The DJ profiles on the stick. Push one to make it active and apply its settings and look. ACTIVE marks the one in use. DAMAGED A profile whose files cannot be read. SAVE SETTINGS TO Saves the current settings into the active DJ's profile. Push twice. Help What the highlighted row does. Further down, WAVEFORM sets COLOR, POSITION, ZOOM, USB COLORS and the stem row layout. SAVED ON USB 1 lists the settings stored on the stick, which you can change there. PUSH AGAIN TO SAVE. The save is armed The DJ PROFILE rows The WAVEFORM rows SAVED ON USB 1. The settings on the stick, with help for the highlighted one A locked stick with nothing saved. Only the WAVEFORM rows remain A LINK player's USB while deck 1 plays After a load. How many settings applied and how many do not exist on this deck

manual:dfe7f22d7cef0dbf9691.source: There is no save button in MODS. Every change saves on its own to the settings USB, the stick you browse. The settings live in the VJ.Tools folder on that stick, so they travel with you to another XZ running XZ Mods. When you browse a stick, the player takes that stick's settings. A stick with no settings, or with damaged ones, leaves the current settings as they are. Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap CLASSIC Tap MODERN Press MENU The XZ also remembers the last settings it applied. If you start it with no stick, it uses them. The save state at the right of the dock says what happened to your last change: Save state What it means SAVING... The change is being written. SAVED TO USB 1 (or USB 2) The change is on the stick. SAVED ON THIS XZ / NO USB No stick is in. The change is kept on this XZ. SAVED ON THIS XZ / USB CHANGED The settings stick changed. The change is kept on this XZ. SAVED ON THIS XZ / USB PROFILE KEPT The stick is locked. The change is kept on this XZ and the stick is left as it was. USB REMOVED: SETTINGS KEPT You pulled the settings stick. Nothing resets. NOT SAVED TO USB 1: CHECK USB Writing failed. Check that the stick is in and not locked. NOT SAVED: USB PROFILE KEPT The stick is locked and the XZ could not keep the change either. NO SETTINGS USB: CHANGES LAST UNTIL POWER OFF. Nothing can be saved. Your change works until you switch the player off. NOT SAVED: CHANGES LAST UNTIL POWER OFF. This build does not save settings. Changes work until you switch the player off. Lines that say NOT SAVED or NO SETTINGS USB show in amber. DJ profiles are not settings. They stay on the DJ's stick and never on the XZ. See Connect and DJ profiles .

manual:d3562812aab649b7ca05.source: Earlier versions had GENERAL, CONTROLS, THEMES and SETTINGS pages in MODS. They are gone. Anything that pointed at them now opens the page that replaced them: Old page Opens GENERAL HOME CONTROLS STEM PADS, in STEMS THEMES SCREEN SETTINGS PLAY

manual:bb6fc88735ce095c3179.source: SCREEN is the MODS section for how the player looks. Here you choose between the MODERN and CLASSIC interfaces, pick a theme, set the waveform colours and the 3-band colours, and decide how keys are written. Nothing on this page changes how a track sounds. Open MODS with MENU , then choose SCREEN in the section rail.

manual:40b3f8f1c0c10d29efd7.source: Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap 2 DECKS Tap 4 DECKS Tap 4 DECKS Tap STOCK Tap RGB Tap 3-BAND Tap STEMS Tap AS ON THE USB Tap MUSICAL Tap WHEEL Tap PLAYING KEY Tap KEY MATCH COLOURS Tap KEY BEFORE TITLE The SCREEN page with CLASSIC chosen. Under MODERN, the THEME row reads LAMPS AND TITLES, 3-BAND COLOURS sits beside it, and WAVEFORM COLOURS offers four choices. INTERFACE MODERN or CLASSIC. The framed picture is the one in use. DECK VIEW How many decks the play screen shows and in what order. See Four decks . THEME Opens CLASSIC THEMES. The value is the theme in use. Under MODERN this row is LAMPS AND TITLES. 3-BAND COLOURS Opens the 3-BAND COLOURS page. The three squares are the colours of the lows, mids and highs now. WAVEFORM COLOURS How the scrolling waveforms are coloured. KEY NOTATION How keys are written everywhere MODS draws them. PLAYING KEY Shows the key a track plays in after tempo and key shift. KEY MATCH COLOURS Colours keys by how well they mix with the master deck. KEY BEFORE TITLE Shows the key in front of each title in the track list. TRACK LIST COLUMNS Tells you where to change the columns of the track list. SYSTEM READOUT CPU, memory and temperature on the top bar. Reads SET UP until you have run its setup. WORKS ON The decks the highlighted control applies to, in mixer order 3 1 2 4. Control Choices What it changes INTERFACE CLASSIC, MODERN Who draws the play screen. See MODERN and CLASSIC DECK VIEW 2 DECKS, 4 DECKS in number order, 4 DECKS in mixer order Which decks the play screen shows. Sound and controls do not change. Hidden on a player that cannot run decks 3 and 4 THEME (CLASSIC) 24 classic themes The look of the player's own screen and of MODS LAMPS AND TITLES (MODERN) A page of switches Which parts of the MODERN play screen you see 3-BAND COLOURS A page of colours The colours of the lows, mids and highs in every 3-BAND waveform. See 3-band colours WAVEFORM COLOURS STOCK, 3-BAND, STEMS (MODERN adds RGB) The colours of the scrolling waveforms KEY NOTATION AS ON THE USB, MUSICAL, WHEEL How keys are written PLAYING KEY ON, OFF The key a track plays in now, or its original key KEY MATCH COLOURS ON, OFF Green or amber keys on the play screen and in the track list KEY BEFORE TITLE ON, OFF The key in front of each title in the track list TRACK LIST COLUMNS Information only Tap a column title in the track list, or press MENU there, to choose its columns and sort SYSTEM READOUT Opens its setup CPU, RAM and temperature on the top bar. It has the last row of the page to itself The HOME card for SCREEN sums the page up in one line, for example Classic | 3-band | Am keys .

manual:c53308a1dc0a7e31831c.source: XZ Mods gives the player two interfaces. You choose one with INTERFACE on the SCREEN page, or when you prepare the USB in the XZ Mods app. MODERN is the default. Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap CLASSIC Tap MODERN Press the button above LINK Press the button above LINK MODERN is a full-screen layout drawn by XZ Mods, with bigger waveforms and a browse sidebar. CLASSIC keeps the player's own play screen and adds MODS to it. The classic themes restyle that screen. MODERN CLASSIC Play screen Drawn by XZ Mods, full screen The XDJ-XZ's own layout, restyled Themes One look, STANDARD. MODS is drawn in FLAGSHIP 24 themes. MODS is drawn in the theme you pick Waveform colours STOCK, RGB, 3-BAND, STEMS STOCK, 3-BAND, STEMS Lamps and titles Each part can be shown or hidden Not available Playing key Shown as the big key in each deck's column Shown where the beat countdown sits Stem buttons Six places, including small buttons beside the hot cues Five places Browse The XZ Mods browser with a sidebar. See Browsing and loading The player's own browser Each interface keeps its own theme. If you switch from CLASSIC to MODERN and back, your classic theme comes back with you. To switch without opening MODS, press the button above LINK . Out of the box it switches between MODERN and CLASSIC. You can give it another job in PLAY › BUTTON ABOVE LINK . See Controls on the player . The MODERN play screen with two decks, 3-BAND waveforms and the playing key shown. Mode lamps SINGLE or CONTINUE, A. HOT CUE and A. CUE. Hide them in LAMPS AND TITLES. QUANTIZE lamp Red while QUANTIZE is on, with its beat value. Hide it in LAMPS AND TITLES. Playing key The key the track plays in now. ORIGINAL below it is the key it was analysed in. Scrolling waveform Coloured by WAVEFORM COLOURS. STEMS and MODS STEMS steps the stem buttons through their places, or shows and hides them in 4 DECKS. MODS opens the MODS menu.

manual:1781ad9aee9d5a5523d5.source: A classic theme restyles the player's own play screen and the MODS menu: artwork, text, waveforms, cue marks and dialogs. Track positions, numbers and touch areas stay where the player puts them, so a theme never moves a control under your finger. Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap CLASSIC Tap THEME Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise, then push it Choose THEME on the SCREEN page to open CLASSIC THEMES . Tap a theme, or turn the encoder to it and push. Close MODS to see the play screen in the new theme. Every classic theme on one page. ORIGINAL is in use. Theme in use Framed, with SELECTED under its name. Colour dots The theme's main colours, so you can compare themes before you pick one. Dock Says what a theme restyles before you choose it. WORKS ON Themes apply to decks 1 to 4. The gallery shows the HOME page of MODS in every theme. Original White Cyberpunk Neon Mocha Aurora Sandstone Game Boy Super Nintendo Windows 95 Game Boy Color Aqua / Itunes Game Boy Dark Super Nintendo Dark Windows 95 Dark Game Boy Color Dark Aqua / Itunes Dark Game Boy Dmg Game Boy Dmg Dark Liquid Glass Liquid Glass Dark Lcars Matrix Analog Flagship

manual:8c5c431af1d3b73a6309.source: Tap the screen Tap the screen Family Themes What to expect Modern palettes ORIGINAL, WHITE, CYBERPUNK, NEON, MOCHA, AURORA, SANDSTONE Colour schemes on the player's own artwork. ORIGINAL is the player as it ships Game Boy GAME BOY, GAME BOY DARK, GAME BOY COLOR, GAME BOY COLOR DARK, GAME BOY DMG, GAME BOY DMG DARK Handheld palettes, with their own player artwork and title treatment Super Nintendo SUPER NINTENDO, SUPER NINTENDO DARK Console colours with their own player artwork Windows 95 WINDOWS 95, WINDOWS 95 DARK Grey bevelled windows and title bars Aqua AQUA / ITUNES, AQUA / ITUNES DARK Glossy rounded panels Liquid Glass LIQUID GLASS, LIQUID GLASS DARK Translucent rounded panels LCARS LCARS Amber and violet swept panels and capsules. Its own MODS layout with a sidebar Matrix MATRIX A green terminal with inverse selections and pixel lettering Analog ANALOG A brushed metal faceplate with lamp keys and switches. Its needle shows the VJ.Tools frame rate, not audio level Most families come in a light and a DARK version. Pick the dark one for dim booths. Note Themes change the screen only. The pad and button lights on the player keep their own colours.

manual:055c8579673e79a636fc.source: MODERN has one look, STANDARD , so it has no theme list. The MODS menu is drawn in FLAGSHIP: black pages, a grey section rail and blue selections. More MODERN looks are planned. Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap LAMPS AND TITLES Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise Instead of THEME, the SCREEN page offers LAMPS AND TITLES . Its row shows ALL SHOWN , or how many parts you have hidden. Group Switch or choice Shown Hidden TOP BAR MODE LAMPS The SINGLE / CONTINUE, A. HOT CUE and A. CUE lamps light while their mode is on The lamps leave the screen. The modes keep working TOP BAR QUANTIZE LAMP Each deck's QUANTIZE lamp and beat value above its time The QUANTIZE button's own light still shows it WAVEFORMS TITLES IN WAVEFORMS Track titles inside the waveform lanes The waveforms use that space. Titles at the bottom stay TRACK COLOURS DECK + WAVE The colours set for the USB in your DJ software show on the deck tag and its waveform TRACK COLOURS DECK ONLY Those colours show on the deck tag only TRACK COLOURS OFF USB colours are not shown A hidden lamp also stops answering touch. Your LAMPS AND TITLES choices, TRACK COLOURS and the BYPASS BUTTON switch are saved to the USB with your other settings, so they come back after the player restarts. So are MODERN's waveform colour, its waveform position and zoom, and how it writes keys. Every lamp shown MODE LAMPS and QUANTIZE LAMP hidden TRACK COLOURS DECK + WAVE. Deck 1 comes from a yellow USB set to RGB waveforms, deck 2 from a pink USB TRACK COLOURS DECK ONLY TRACK COLOURS OFF The BYPASS BUTTON switch for MODERN sits with the stem buttons in STEMS . See Stems .

manual:b524eab0c5264fc97e01.source: WAVEFORM COLOURS sets how the scrolling waveforms are coloured. The setting itself is explained with the rest of the play screen in The play screen . Choice What you see STOCK The player's own waveform colours RGB The full-colour waveform. MODERN only 3-BAND Lows, mids and highs as layers: lows outside, mids around them, highs at the core. Blue, amber and white unless you choose your own 3-band colours STEMS Drums outside, harmonics around them, vocals at the core, in your stem colours The preview strip on the 3-BAND COLOURS page draws the three layers in the colours in use: lows outside, mids around them, highs at the core. 3-BAND and STEMS read the track analysis your DJ software and the XZ Mods stem builder already put on the USB. You do not prepare anything extra. A track without stems shows 3-BAND under STEMS. A track with four stems also shows 3-BAND, because its stems carry no waveform data yet. Stem colours are set in STEMS › STEM COLOURS . See Stems . In MODERN, UTILITY's WAVEFORM COLOR is the same setting. Your choice is saved to the USB and comes back after a restart.

manual:29c380688efce7004e12.source: 3-BAND COLOURS chooses the colour of each band in the 3-BAND waveform: the lows, the mids and the highs. On the SCREEN page it sits beside THEME in CLASSIC and beside LAMPS AND TITLES in MODERN. Its row shows the three colours in use. Press MENU Tap SCREEN Tap 3-BAND COLOURS Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise Every band on STANDARD, the interface's own colours. LOWS The colour of the lows, the outer layer of the waveform. MIDS The colour of the mids, the middle layer. HIGHS The colour of the highs, at the core. STANDARD Keeps the interface's own colour for that band. The highlighted choice in each band is the colour in use. Colour choices BLUE, RED, GREEN, AMBER, PURPLE, CYAN, PINK and WHITE. Tap one to give it to that band. Preview A strip drawn the way the 3-BAND waveform stacks the bands, in the colours you chose. RESET 3-BAND COLOURS Puts all three bands back to STANDARD. WORKS ON 3-band colours apply on all four decks. Open MODS > SCREEN > 3-BAND COLOURS . Tap a colour under LOWS , MIDS or HIGHS . Without the touch screen, turn the encoder to a colour and push. Close MODS to see the play screen in the new colours. Band Choices Default LOWS STANDARD, BLUE, RED, GREEN, AMBER, PURPLE, CYAN, PINK, WHITE STANDARD MIDS The same nine STANDARD HIGHS The same nine STANDARD The colours apply to every 3-BAND waveform: the MODERN lanes and overviews, the CLASSIC scrolling waveform, decks 3 and 4, and the browse preview. STANDARD is not one fixed colour. It is the colour the interface itself uses for that band, so MODERN and CLASSIC can differ a little. The 3-BAND pictures under WAVEFORM COLOURS on the SCREEN page are drawn in your colours too. Stem colours are separate. Set them in STEMS › STEM COLOURS . The colours are saved to the USB with your other settings.

manual:73c1748a722262d43a61.source: KEY NOTATION sets how keys are written everywhere MODS draws them: on the play screen, in the track list and in MODS. Choice Example When to use it AS ON THE USB as set in your library Keys look the way your DJ software writes them MUSICAL Am You think in note names WHEEL 8A You mix by key wheel numbers MUSICAL. Deck 2 plays Bbm, analysed in Am WHEEL. Deck 2 plays 3A, analysed in 8A

manual:32da8470b88b6ad1d090.source: With PLAYING KEY on, each deck shows the key the track plays in now, after tempo changes and key shifts. The original key and the offset in cents sit beside it. In MODERN the playing key is the big key in each deck's column. Off shows the track's original key there. In CLASSIC the playing key sits where the beat countdown is. Off brings the countdown back. Decks 3 and 4 show their playing key too. Until a software deck reports it, the deck shows the track's own key, marked TRACK KEY in CLASSIC. Deck 2 sped up with MT off. It still plays in Am, 38 cents sharp Faster still.
