While decks 3 and 4 are not running, a four-deck view puts a card in their lanes. The card shows the cable steps, the state, and the buttons you need. Decks 1 and 2 stay live above it. In number order the card fills the lanes of decks 3 and 4 under decks 1 and 2. In mixer order it splits into a strip above deck 1 and a strip below deck 2.

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it

You can drive the card with the encoder. While the card shows, push the encoder to highlight RESCAN, turn it to move between the card's buttons and the DECKS button, and push again to press. BACK, or six seconds without input, gives the encoder back to the player.

Card titleWhat it meansWhat to do
NO CABLE FOUNDThe XZ does not see the loopback cable.Connect the cable directly to either top port. Music goes in the other port and is optional for startup. Press RESCAN to check at once.
LOOKING FOR THE CABLE...A check runs now. The button reads SCANNING.Wait a moment.
STARTING DECKS 3 AND 4The cable is found and the audio input is starting.Wait a few seconds. The card's sentence says which step is running.
STOP DECKS 1 AND 2Decks 3 and 4 or a newly connected music hub wait for decks 1 and 2 to stop.Stop or pause decks 1 and 2. The card changes by itself.
COULD NOT START DECKS 3 AND 4The start failed. The picture marks the type of connection that needs attention: top USB, cable, rear socket or CH3/CH4 switches. The drawn port is an example.Read the sentence, fix that part, then press TRY AGAIN. It tries the start again, and restarts the four-deck helper if it had stopped.
DECKS 3 AND 4 DISCONNECTEDThe cable was unplugged or lost power while decks 3 and 4 ran.Plug the cable back into either top port. Press RESCAN to check at once.
FOUR DECKS ARE NOT AVAILABLEThe software players are not running in this build. Decks 1 and 2 play as usual.Press TWO DECKS.
DECKS 3 AND 4 ARE READYThe route came up. The card turns green, then wipes away.Press SHIFT twice on a side to play deck 3 or 4.

When the route comes up, a banner says DECKS 3 AND 4 ARE READY for a few seconds. If the play screen shows two decks at that moment, the banner says DECKS 3 AND 4 ARE READY. TAP DECKS AT THE TOP FOR FOUR DECKS. The view does not change by itself.

The E-8307 hub warning experimental

The player sees the loopback cable as a USB hub. When you plug it in, the player raises its own warning E-8307: HUBS ARE NOT SUPPORTED and would keep it up while the cable stays in. That is not an error. XZ Mods removes the warning window as soon as the player draws it, so it does not stay on screen in MODERN, MODS or CLASSIC, whether four decks are on or not.

A music hub the player refuses raises the same warning, and XZ Mods removes it too. If the sticks on a music hub do not appear, stop or pause decks 1 and 2 with the loopback cable connected and let the music hub finish connecting. A hub in the loopback port, a second hub behind the first, or a hub that does not support high-speed USB 2.0 is not supported. Remove that hub or connect the music stick directly.

DECK VIEW

DECK VIEW chooses what the play screen shows. It changes neither the sound, the mixer channels, nor which deck a side controls.

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    3. Tap DECKS
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    5. Tap DECKS
    6. Press BACK
DECK VIEWWaveform lanes, top to bottomBottom channels
2 DECKS (the default)The two decks the sides controlThe same two decks
4 DECKS, number order 1 2 3 41, 2, 3, 43, 1, 2, 4
4 DECKS, mixer order 3 1 2 43, 1, 2, 43, 1, 2, 4

The bottom channels always follow the mixer, left to right: CH3, CH1, CH2, CH4. Mixer order puts the lanes in the same order, top to bottom. Each lane and each channel carries its deck's number in a badge, so you can always tell which deck is which. Decks 1 and 2 have a white number on grey. Decks 3 and 4 have a black number on white, as on the jog displays.

DECK VIEW is saved to the USB with your other settings. You can change it in five places, and they all change the same setting:

  • the DECKS button at the top of the play screen;
  • TWO DECKS on the card;
  • MODS > SCREEN > DECK VIEW;
  • MODS > 4 DECKS > DECK VIEW;
  • the button above LINK, when you set it to DECK VIEW in MODS > PLAY > BUTTON ABOVE LINK. Each press then steps 2 DECKS, 4 DECKS in number order, 4 DECKS in mixer order.

The DECKS button and its picker

The DECKS button is always at the top of the play screen in both interfaces. It names the decks on screen: DECKS 1 2, DECKS 1234, DECKS 3124, or the pair the sides control in 2 DECKS, such as DECKS 3 2. In MODERN it sits left of the INFO button. In CLASSIC it sits in the black space between VJ.TOOLS and the METRICS readout.

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it

A tap outside the picker, BACK, or six seconds without input closes it. The encoder also turns and pushes inside the open picker.

Switch a side between decks experimental

The left controls play DECK 1 or DECK 3. The right controls play DECK 2 or DECK 4. Decks 3 and 4 must be ready.

    1. Press SHIFT on the left deck twice quickly
    1. Press SHIFT on the right deck twice quickly
  • Press SHIFT twice quickly on a side to switch it. The left SHIFT switches between decks 1 and 3, the right SHIFT between decks 2 and 4. These are the presses the XDJ-XZ uses for DJ software.
  • Or press SHORTCUT and tap the deck under DECK SELECT modern.

After a switch the tempo fader does not jump. The deck you switched to keeps its tempo until you move the fader across that deck's value. The same holds when you switch back.

In 2 DECKS the screen follows the sides. A side on deck 3 or 4 shows that deck's waveform, tag and channel, and the screen says where the side went for two seconds, for example LEFT: DECK 3. In a four-deck view the lanes stay where they are, and a pale blue tag marks the decks the sides control.

If decks 3 and 4 are not running, SHIFT pressed twice does not switch. The screen says DECK 3 AND 4 NEED THE CH3/CH4 ROUTE. If the route is lost while a side plays deck 3 or 4, both sides go back to decks 1 and 2 and the screen says DECK 3/4 ROUTE LOST.

The MODERN four-deck screen modern

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    3. Tap LANE 3
    4. Tap the screen
    5. Tap LANE 3
    6. Tap STEMS HEADER
    7. Tap STEMS HEADER

Tap a lane of deck 3 or 4 to open its detail panel. It shows the full pad bank, the deck's modes, what SYNC is doing and a whole-track overview you can touch to search. Tap the lane again, or CLOSE, to close it.

Stem buttons show in a half row under a deck's waveform, only for decks 1 and 2 and only while the deck's track has prepared stems. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems. A deck without stems shows no stem buttons and its waveform keeps the whole lane.

STEMS in the top bar shows or hides the stem buttons on all four lanes: one tap hides them, the next shows them. The screen says STEM BUTTONS HIDDEN or STEM BUTTONS SHOWN, and STEMS is lit while they show. Your 2 DECKS stem layout does not apply here and does not change. See Stems.

The CLASSIC four-deck screen classic

CLASSIC keeps the player's own look and adds what four decks need.

    1. Tap the screen
    2. Tap the screen
    3. Tap the screen
    4. Tap the screen
    5. Tap the screen
  • Waveforms. The waveform area holds four narrower lanes, one per deck, in the order DECK VIEW chooses. Decks 3 and 4 draw the same 3-band waveform with beat ticks, hot cue flags A to H, the cue point, loops and the playhead.
  • Side column. The left column has one tag per lane. The tag of a deck a side controls is pale blue with LEFT or RIGHT. Decks 1 and 2 show the analysed key, the playing key and its cents. Decks 3 and 4 show their playing key and its cents the same way, TRACK KEY until they report it, or NOT CONNECTED and SEE THE CARD while they are not running.
  • Bottom panel. Four channels in mixer order 3 1 2 4. Each shows the deck's title, time, QUANTIZE, tempo and range, AUTO CUE and MT, what SYNC follows, what the pads do, the BPM (orange with MASTER for the master deck) and the whole-track overview. A deck that is not connected shows a dim band with NOT CONNECTED and DECK n WAITS FOR THE LOOPBACK CABLE.
  • Stem rows are not drawn while four decks show, because there is no room, and STEMS stays dark. Your stem layout comes back when you return to two decks. Pressing STEMS meanwhile changes nothing and says STEM BUTTONS SHOW IN 2 DECKS VIEW.
  • 2 DECKS shows the decks the sides control. A side on deck 3 or 4 gets a whole half in the player's own style: its waveform, its side tag and its bottom panel.

Tap a lane, side tag or channel title of deck 3 or 4 to open its detail panel. Touch the overview in the bottom channel to search the track. NEEDLE LOCK refuses a search while the deck plays.

Load tracks onto decks 3 and 4 experimental

LOAD on a side loads the highlighted track into the deck that side controls, deck 3 or deck 4 included. In CLASSIC this goes through the player's own browser. In MODERN, tap a track to see a LOAD chip with one cell per deck, then tap the deck number. See Browsing and loading for the rest.

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    3. Press BROWSE
    4. Push ROTARY SELECTOR
    5. Tap TRACK ROW
    6. Tap LOAD DECK 3

Decks 3 and 4 cannot load a track at a memory point from the CUE/LOOP LIST. The screen says DECK 3 AND 4 CANNOT LOAD AT A MEMORY POINT.

INFO, SOURCE and UTILITY with four decks modern

INFO has a tab for each deck. SOURCE shows which decks use each stick. UTILITY and the other full screens keep a compact strip of all four decks at the bottom.

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    3. Press INFO
    4. Tap the screen
    5. Tap the screen
    6. Press BACK
    7. Open SOURCE (BACK at the top of a list)
    8. Press BACK
    9. Hold MENU for a second
    10. Press BACK

What decks 3 and 4 can do experimental

Decks 3 and 4 are software players. They follow the player's own controls on the side that controls them. MODS > 4 DECKS shows the current answer for each feature.

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    3. Press PLAY/PAUSE on the left deck
    4. Press CUE on the left deck
    5. Press PLAY/PAUSE on the left deck
    6. Press SYNC on the left deck
    7. Press DECK QUANTIZE on the left deck
    8. Press SYNC on the left deck
    9. Press MASTER on the left deck
    10. Press SYNC on the left deck
    11. Press PLAY/PAUSE on the left deck
    12. Press IN/CUE on the left deck
    13. Press OUT on the left deck
    14. Press RELOOP/EXIT on the left deck
FeatureDecks 1 and 2Decks 3 and 4
Beat jump pads with your own sizesYesYes, the same sizes and both pages
Gate cue and smart cueYesYes
Waveform colours, key notation, titlesYesYes
Playing keyYesYes
Key sync and key shiftYesYes. Both can shift together; new shifts check measured audio headroom.
StemsYes, with USB stems set upNo. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems.
RAM tracksYesYes, while the loopback cable is connected. See RAM tracks.

On a side that controls deck 3 or 4, these controls work on that deck experimental:

ControlWhat it does on deck 3 or 4
PLAY/PAUSE, CUEPlay and pause, back cue and cue audition. With VINYL on, pause brakes to a stop at the VINYL SPEED ADJUST rate.
HOT CUE, BEAT LOOP, SLIP LOOP, BEAT JUMPSet the pad mode of the software deck. The native deck keeps its own mode.
PadsHot cues, beat loops, slip loops and beat jumps, as on decks 1 and 2.
IN/CUE, OUT, RELOOP/EXITManual loops, loop adjustment with the jog, reloop and exit.
SLIP, DIRECTION REV, VINYLSlip, reverse and vinyl mode.
TEMPO RANGE, TEMPO RESET, MASTER TEMPOTempo range up to WIDE, original speed, and key lock while the tempo moves.
SYNC, MASTERFollow the master deck's tempo, and with QUANTIZE its beat. Make this deck the master. See SYNC on decks 3 and 4.
SHIFT + SYNC, MASTER TEMPOKEY SYNC to the master deck, and back to the deck's own key. See Keys and KEY SYNC.
DECK QUANTIZECue, loop and hot cue points land on the beat. DECK QUANTIZE switches every deck. SHIFT + DECK QUANTIZE switches only this side's deck.
MEMORY, DELETE, CUE/LOOP CALLStore, delete and call memory points.
TRACK SEARCH, SEARCHPrevious and next track, and fine search. With AUTO CUE on, the new track waits at its cue. Previous and next follow the list the track was loaded from in MODERN. After a CLASSIC load the deck shows NO SAVED TRACK ORDER, and TRACK SEARCH back returns to the cue.

On decks 3 and 4, TRACK SEARCH respects AUTO CUE. With AUTO CUE on, a newly loaded track waits at its cue point. With AUTO CUE off, a deck that was playing continues with the new track; a paused deck stays paused.

Hot cues and memory points you set on decks 3 and 4 are saved on the music stick for those decks only. Decks 1 and 2 and your DJ software do not see them, and the exported library stays unchanged.

SYNC on decks 3 and 4 experimental

Press SYNC and the deck takes the master deck's BPM at once. The SYNC button stays lit for as long as SYNC is on. With QUANTIZE on and a beat grid on both tracks, the deck also locks to the master's beat. Press SYNC again to turn it off.

  1. Master Deck 1 is the tempo master. Deck 3 plays at its own tempo, with SYNC off.
  2. SYNC Press SYNC on deck 3. It takes the master's BPM at once and reads SYNC 1. With QUANTIZE on and a beat grid on both tracks, it also locks to the master's beat.
  3. Tempo only With QUANTIZE off, only the tempo follows, and deck 3 reads BPM 1.

If the beats drift apart, press SYNC off and on again. With QUANTIZE on, every engage snaps to the nearest position at the selected beat value, even for a small drift. The beat value can be 1, 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 beat. With QUANTIZE off, only the tempo follows.

  • The tempo follows even when the master or the synced deck is paused. If the beat position is available, the paused deck aligns once. If it is unavailable, alignment happens as soon as it can be read. Continuous beat lock resumes when both decks play.
  • A pause, a jump, a loop or a new master never turns SYNC off. The deck follows again on its own, with no second press.
  • Nudge the jog from the side to move the deck a little off the master's beat. SYNC stays on and the tempo stays matched. The deck keeps the new alignment, also when the master's tempo changes, and the SYNC button flashes.
  • Nudge the master's jog from the side to move only the master. It stays master, and the synced decks keep their tempo and the new alignment.
  • To line the beats up again, press SYNC off and on. The deck snaps to the nearest beat and the button lights steadily.
  • Scratching on the platter top takes control of the deck. When you let go, QUANTIZE snaps it back to the beat.
  • Press SYNC off and the deck keeps its position and the synced tempo. The tempo fader takes over once you move it to that tempo.
  • The tempo fader does not move the deck while SYNC is on.

The bottom channel, the lane and the detail panel say what SYNC is doing:

ShownWhat it means
SYNC 1 to SYNC 4SYNC is on and follows that deck.
BPM 1 to BPM 4Only the tempo can follow that deck: QUANTIZE is off, a track has no beat grid, a loop is running, or the master's beat position is not available.
MASTERThis deck is the tempo master.
3/4 MASTERThis deck is the master for decks 3 and 4 only.
LIMITThe master's tempo is out of this deck's reach. The deck keeps its last tempo.
EXT MASTERThe master is another player on the LINK network, which decks 3 and 4 cannot follow.
NO BPMThe track has no BPM to sync with. Analyse it in your DJ software.

The detail panel adds a line about the reason, for example:

Detail panelWhat it means
SYNC ON / FOLLOWING DECK 1The deck follows deck 1.
SYNC ON / TEMPO MATCHED, PAUSED / TEMPO MATCHEDThe tempo matches. The beat locks once both decks play.
BPM SYNC / MASTER PAUSED, BPM SYNC / DECK PAUSEDOne of the two decks is paused. The tempo follows, and the beat locks once both play.
BPM SYNC / NO BEAT GRIDA track has no beat grid, so only the tempo follows.
BPM SYNC / LOOP ACTIVEA loop is running, so only the tempo follows until it ends.
BPM SYNC / BEAT POSITION UNAVAILABLEThe master's beat position cannot be read, so only the tempo follows.
BPM SYNC / QUANTIZE OFFQUANTIZE is off, so only the tempo follows.
SYNC ON / JOG CONTROLYou are nudging or scratching. SYNC picks up again when you let go. After a side nudge it keeps the new alignment.
NO MASTER / TEMPO UNCHANGEDNo deck is master. The deck keeps its tempo and follows as soon as there is one.
MASTER CLOCK UNAVAILABLE / LAST TEMPO RETAINEDThe master's tempo cannot be read right now. The deck keeps the last tempo.
SYNC TEMPO LIMIT / LAST TEMPO RETAINEDThe master's tempo is out of reach.
EXTERNAL MASTER / SYNC SOURCE UNAVAILABLEA LINK player is master.
TRACK BPM UNAVAILABLE / SYNC ONThe track has no BPM.

Limits

  • Decks 1 and 2 must be stopped or paused while decks 3 and 4 start.
  • Keep the music stick connected while you play. Decks 3 and 4 read from it all the time.
  • Decks 3 and 4 play WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3 and Ogg Vorbis files. AAC and M4A files do not play on decks 3 and 4.
  • A deck 3 or 4 master reads MASTER when decks 1 and 2 can follow it too, and 3/4 MASTER when it drives decks 3 and 4 only.
  • Press MASTER on a playing deck 3 or 4 and it is master at once. The MASTER buttons show the change.
  • When you pause the master, MASTER passes at once to the next playing deck. A deck with SYNC on comes first. Otherwise after deck 3 comes deck 4, then decks 1 and 2. After deck 4 come decks 1 and 2, then deck 3. In VINYL mode MASTER passes when you press pause, while the deck slows down.
  • When you pause a deck 1 or 2 master, a playing deck 3 or 4 takes MASTER at once. If the other of decks 1 and 2 is playing, MASTER goes to that deck instead, as with two decks.
  • In VINYL mode, hold the master's platter top and MASTER passes to the other synced, playing deck after a moment.
  • Load a new track on the master and MASTER passes to the other playing deck. The loading deck keeps SYNC on and plays its new track at the tempo the decks shared.
  • A handover never changes the tempo.
  • A master set by another player over LINK is never taken.
  • Some lamps on the player do not yet light as they do for decks 1 and 2. The beat loop and slip loop pad colours are provisional.
  • Four decks, the handover of MASTER between native and software decks, and scratching on decks 3 and 4 are experimental in this version.

If something goes wrong, the card or the 4 DECKS page names the state. Messages and troubleshooting lists every notice.

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.html:
XZ Mods is software for the XDJ-XZ that starts from a USB stick. It adds a MODS menu, stems you can mute live, custom beat jump, four decks over a loopback cable, DJ profiles, themes and games. It can also replace the whole play screen with its own MODERN interface.

What changes and what stays stock

XZ Mods runs in the player's memory. It never writes to the player's firmware, so the XDJ-XZ itself stays stock.

    1. Hold MENU for a second
    2. Push ROTARY SELECTOR
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    5. Press BACK
  • The player picks up the XZ Mods loader (autoexec.bin) from the USB at start and runs XZ Mods from there.
  • Your music, the library your DJ software exported and your playlists stay as they are. XZ Mods adds its own folders beside them.
  • The player's own settings are still there. Hold MENU to open UTILITY, exactly as on a stock XDJ-XZ.
  • Settings you change in MODS are saved on the USB, so they travel with it to another XZ running XZ Mods.

Go back to stock

  1. Switch the player off.
  2. Start it without the XZ Mods USB, or with a USB that has no autoexec.bin on it.

The player starts stock. Plug the XZ Mods USB back in and start again to load XZ Mods. If you play from a separate music stick, that stick works on the stock player as before.

What you need

ItemWhat you need
PlayerXDJ-XZ on firmware 1.26. No other firmware version is supported
Computer64-bit Windows with WebView2, or a Mac with macOS 14 or later, to prepare the USB
StemsMade on a Windows computer or an Apple silicon Mac. An Intel Mac can import stems made elsewhere
USBA USB stick for the loader. It can be your music USB, or a separate loader stick
Four decksA USB-B to USB-A cable. See Four decks experimental

The app downloads the official firmware it needs from the manufacturer and checks it. No firmware or boot files come with the XZ Mods download.

Caution

XZ Mods is a preview. Test every new USB at home before you use it in a set.

Prepare a USB

You prepare the USB in the XZ Mods app on your computer. It does not format the drive or touch your music.

  1. Install the XZ Mods app and open it.
  2. Plug in your USB. The app finds it and opens it. With several USBs plugged in, choose yours from the list.
  3. Choose Install XZ Mods.
  4. Follow the short guide: your DJ profile, the screen the XZ starts with, then a checklist of what it will write. Back returns to the step before.
  5. Choose Write to USB, then Eject USB.

Every step of the app is in The XZ Mods app. To add stems to your tracks, see Stems.

First start

    1. Press BROWSE
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise
    3. Press LOAD 1
    4. Press BACK
    5. Press MENU
    6. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to SCREEN and push it
    7. Tap CLASSIC
    8. Tap MODERN
    9. Press MENU
  1. Plug the USB into USB 1 or USB 2 on the top of the XDJ-XZ.
  2. Switch the player on.
  3. Wait for XZ Mods to start. Load a track as usual and check it plays.
  4. Press MENU on the play screen, or touch MODS at the top right, to open the MODS menu. HOME is the first page.

If you use a separate loader stick, keep it in until XZ Mods has started. Keep the USB with your music and stems in while you play.

MODERN on first start modern

MODERN draws the whole play screen. The player's controls work as before, and the top bar adds a few buttons.

The rest of the play screen is in The play screen.

CLASSIC on first start classic

CLASSIC keeps the player's own play screen and adds MODS to it. Touch MODS at the top right, or press MENU, to open the menu. A classic theme can restyle the screen. See Screen, interfaces and themes.

    1. Press the button above LINK
    2. Press the button above LINK

Choose MODERN or CLASSIC

The XZ starts in the interface saved on the USB. You choose it in the app before the first start, and you can change it on the player at any time. Nothing else changes when you switch. Your settings, stems and decks stay as they are.

InterfaceWhat you see
MODERNXZ Mods draws the whole screen: bigger waveforms, a browse sidebar and a stems row with mute buttons. Marked Beta in the app
CLASSICThe player's own play screen, with MODS added. Classic themes can restyle it

A new USB starts in MODERN unless you choose the standard interface in the app.

Switch on the player

There are two ways to switch.

  • Press the button above LINK. Out of the box it switches between MODERN and CLASSIC, and the screen says which one you are in. You can give it another job in PLAY › BUTTON ABOVE LINK.
  • Open MODS, go to SCREEN and choose CLASSIC or MODERN under INTERFACE.
    1. Press the button above LINK
    2. Press the button above LINK
    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Tap CLASSIC
    4. Tap MODERN
Tip

You can always reach MODS with the hardware alone. In CLASSIC, the button above LINK takes you to MODERN, where MENU opens MODS, and the encoder and BACK drive it.

Updating

There are two things to update, and they update separately.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap CONNECT
    3. Tap UPDATES
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise
WhatHow
The app on your computerOn Windows the app checks at launch and offers the update. On a Mac, download the new version from the release page. See App updates
XZ Mods on your USBOpen the USB in the app. When it says Update available, choose Update USB. The app backs up the old loader first
XZ Mods over the networkSend the update from the app and download it on the player. See Updates over the network experimental
Caution

Updating the app does not change the USB. After an app update, open the USB page and choose Update USB.

Music, your exported library and your saved settings stay in place through an update. A USB built with Keep this version on the USB stays on its build and ignores network updates. See XZ Mods version.

If something does not work after an update, see Messages and troubleshooting.

hardware.title: Controls on the player
hardware.html:
XZ Mods leaves every control on the XDJ-XZ doing its stock job unless this page says otherwise. This page covers only the controls whose behaviour XZ Mods changes or adds, and the ones you use to drive MODS. For everything else, the XDJ-XZ operating instructions still apply.

The top panel

The picture shows the XDJ-XZ from straight above, rendered from a true-scale model of the player.

Browse section keys

    1. Open SOURCE (BACK at the top of a list)
    2. Press MENU
    3. Press MENU
    4. Press INFO
    5. Press MENU
    6. Press BACK
    7. Press MENU
    8. Press SHORTCUT
    9. Press MENU
    10. Press MENU
    11. Hold MENU for a second
    12. Press BACK
KeyAction with XZ Mods
MENU pressOpens MODS on the play screen, the SOURCE screen, the INFO screen and the SHORTCUT screen experimental. Everywhere else it keeps its stock job. In MODS it closes MODS.
MENU holdOpens the player's own UTILITY, in both interfaces.
BACKGoes up one level. In MODS it steps from an open item to its page, then to the section rail.
TURN Rotary selector, turnMoves the highlight to the next card, row or button in MODS. On a beat jump pair, after a push, it steps the jump size.
PUSH Rotary selector, pushOpens or changes the highlighted item in MODS.
BUTTON ABOVE LINKDoes what you chose in MODS > PLAY > BUTTON ABOVE LINK. The default is INTERFACE.
SHIFT + BUTTON ABOVE LINKHold SHIFT on either deck and press it. Does the second choice on the same page. The default is ITS OWN JOB.
LINKIts stock job. With the screen switch key set to LINK it also switches the VJ.Tools view on and off.
SHORTCUTOpens the SHORTCUT screen. In MODERN this is MODERN's own SHORTCUT screen.
LOADLoads the highlighted track into the deck that side controls: deck 1 or 3, deck 2 or 4.
TIME MODE, DECK QUANTIZEStock on decks 1 and 2. For decks 3 and 4, see Quantize and Four decks.

A short press of MENU keeps the job the player's own firmware gives it wherever there is one. What a short press does in each place:

Where you areShort press of MENU
The MODS menu is openCloses MODS
A game is on screenThe game's own key
The VJ.Tools view is on screenAs before
A menu, popup or dialog is openWorks or closes the open menu
A track list (browse, playlist, search, history)The sort menu or the track menu
TAG LISTLIST MENU
The play screen in GRID ADJUSTThe beat grid menu
The play screenOpens MODS experimental
The SOURCE screenOpens MODS experimental
The track INFO screenOpens MODS experimental
The SHORTCUT screenOpens MODS experimental
The player's own UTILITYCloses UTILITY
Any other screenThe screen's own job

The button above LINK

The XDJ-XZ has a media button directly above LINK. On a stock player it opens the library of a computer or phone connected to the player. XZ Mods gives it two slots: a plain press, and a press while SHIFT is held on either deck. Set them in MODS > PLAY > BUTTON ABOVE LINK.

    1. Press the button above LINK
    2. Press the button above LINK
ChoiceWhat the button does
MODS MENUOpens and closes MODS. MODS then works with the rotary selector and BACK.
ITS OWN JOBThe stock job: the screen for playing a computer's or phone's library. In MODERN the player's own screen for it takes over until you are back on the play screen.
INTERFACESwitches between MODERN and CLASSIC, with the same notice as MODS > SCREEN.
VJ.TOOLS SCREENSwitches the VJ.Tools screen on and off. Without an enabled, connected VJ.Tools link it says so instead.
STEMSDoes what the STEMS button on the screen does: steps the stem buttons through their places in 2 DECKS, and shows or hides them in MODERN's 4 DECKS.
DECK VIEWSteps DECK VIEW: 2 DECKS, 4 DECKS in number order 1 2 3 4, 4 DECKS in mixer order 3 1 2 4, then 2 DECKS again. It saves the choice and shows the new view in a short notice.
NOTHINGThe button does nothing.
Tip

With the default INTERFACE on a plain press, you can always get back to MODS without touching the screen: press MENU on the play screen, or switch interface with the button above LINK and press MENU there.

LINK and the VJ.Tools view

When VJ.Tools on a computer is connected, the player's screen can show the VJ.Tools view instead of the play screen. MODS > CONNECT > VJ.TOOLS has a SCREEN SWITCH KEY with two choices:

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap CONNECT
    3. Tap VJ.TOOLS
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise
ChoiceWhat switches the VJ.Tools view
LINK (default)Pressing LINK. LINK also keeps its stock job.
ONSCREENA VJ.Tools button on the screen, in the corner opposite MODS.

To switch the view with the button above LINK instead, set that button to VJ.TOOLS SCREEN. See Connect and DJ profiles for the connection itself.

Deck keys

The picture shows the left deck from above. The right deck has the same controls in the same places.

    1. Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press SYNC on the left deck
    2. Press MASTER TEMPO on the left deck
    1. Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press SYNC on the left deck
    1. Press SHIFT on the left deck twice quickly
KeyAction with XZ Mods
SHIFT twiceSwitches the left side between deck 1 and deck 3, or the right side between deck 2 and deck 4. Press it twice within about half a second, without touching anything else. Decks 3 and 4 need the loopback cable; without it the screen says DECK 3 AND 4 NEED THE CH3/CH4 ROUTE.
SHIFT + SYNCKEY SYNC: shifts the key of the deck this side controls to match the master deck, and turns on MASTER TEMPO. Press it again to end KEY SYNC. Works on all four decks. SYNC alone keeps its stock job on decks 1 and 2.
MASTER TEMPOWhile KEY SYNC holds on that deck, a press ends KEY SYNC and returns the deck to its own key. Otherwise stock. SHIFT + MASTER TEMPO keeps its stock job.
HOT CUE, BEAT LOOP, SLIP LOOPChoose the pad mode as on a stock player. The mode set in MODS > STEMS > STEM PADS turns four pads into stem pads.
SHIFT + HOT CUEMutes or unmutes the first stem in your STEM ORDER (vocals by default) on that deck.
SHIFT + BEAT LOOPMutes or unmutes the second stem (harmonics by default).
SHIFT + SLIP LOOPMutes or unmutes the third stem (drums by default).
BEAT JUMPBeat jump mode with page 1 of your jump sizes.
SHIFT + BEAT JUMPBeat jump mode with page 2 of your jump sizes. Let go of SHIFT before you press a pad.
TEMPO sliderAfter a deck switch, the deck that takes over keeps its tempo until the slider crosses its value. Then the slider moves it again. This works both ways.
LOADLoads into the deck the side controls now.
Jog wheelStock on decks 1 and 2. On decks 3 and 4 it bends, scratches in VINYL mode and moves loop edges. The jog games use it too.

The three SHIFT + pad mode combinations work while the USB loader has the stem engine. They also turn stem audio on if it was off. With them, the stock SHIFT + HOT CUE (CALL) is not available on decks 1 and 2.

Every other deck key keeps its stock job on decks 1 and 2. While a side drives deck 3 or 4, the transport, loop, cue and tempo keys play that software deck instead. Four decks lists what each one does there.

Performance pads

The eight pads keep their stock job in every pad mode, with two exceptions: the stem pads, and the BEAT JUMP pads.

    1. Press HOT CUE on the left deck
    2. Press BEAT LOOP on the left deck
    3. Press SLIP LOOP on the left deck
    4. Press BEAT JUMP on the left deck
    5. Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press HOT CUE on the left deck, then BEAT LOOP on the left deck, then SLIP LOOP on the left deck
Pad modePads with XZ Mods
HOT CUEStock hot cues. Gate cue and smart cue change what a hot cue does when you turn them on; see Gate cue and smart cue.
BEAT LOOPStock beat loops.
SLIP LOOPStock slip loops.
BEAT JUMPYour jump sizes. A/B, C/D, E/F and G/H are pairs: the first pad jumps back, the second forward. With a loop on, the loop moves instead. SHIFT + pad keeps its stock job on decks 1 and 2. See Beat jump.
The stem modeFour pads (A to D, or E to H) mute stems instead. The other four keep their job in that mode.

Stem pads

In the pad mode you choose for stems, four pads switch stems on that deck. A, B and C mute the three stems in your STEM ORDER. D is BYPASS: it plays the original track instead of the stems. On a 4-stem track, D mutes bass instead. With the E-H bank, E to H do the same.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap STEMS
    3. Tap STEM PADS
    4. Tap HOT CUE
    5. Tap BEAT LOOP
    6. Tap SLIP LOOP
    7. Tap BEAT JUMP
    8. Tap PADS A-D
    9. Tap PADS E-H
    10. Tap ORDER
    11. Tap STEM COLOURS
    12. Tap OFF
    1. Press HOT CUE on the left deck
    2. Press pad A on the left deck
    3. Press pad B on the left deck
    4. Press pad C on the left deck
    5. Press pad D on the left deck
    6. Press pad A on the left deck
Setting on this pageChoicesDefault
Pad modeHOT CUE, BEAT LOOP, SLIP LOOP, BEAT JUMPHOT CUE
STEMS ONPADS A-D, PADS E-HPADS A-D
STEM PAD LIGHTSSTEM COLOURS, OFFSTEM COLOURS

If you choose BEAT JUMP for stems, beat jumps win its pads. Page 2 always jumps. Page 1 jumps while it uses MY SIZES, and gives stem pads only while page 1 is set to STOCK. Stems explains the stem audio itself, the order and the stem buttons on the screen.

Pad lights

What you seeMeaning
Stem pads in stem colours, muted stems dimSTEM PAD LIGHTS is STEM COLOURS, on decks 1 and 2.
Warm red and amber pads in BEAT JUMP modeBeat jump page 2 is selected on that deck.
Stock pad coloursEvery other mode, and page 1 of BEAT JUMP.

Decks 3 and 4 from the deck controls

Each side of the XZ drives one of two decks: the left side deck 1 or deck 3, the right side deck 2 or deck 4. Press SHIFT twice to switch. LOAD on that side then loads into the deck it controls.

    1. Press SHIFT on the right deck twice quickly
  1. Connect the loopback cable and wait until MODS > 4 DECKS says the route is ready.
  2. Press SHIFT twice quickly on the left side. The left side now drives deck 3.
  3. Move the TEMPO slider until it reaches deck 3's tempo. Until then the slider does not change deck 3.
  4. Press SHIFT twice again to go back to deck 1.

If the loopback route goes down, both sides go back to decks 1 and 2. Four decks covers setup, the deck view and every status.

When a control does not respond

What happensWhy, and what to do
MENU opens a stock menu instead of MODSThat screen has its own MENU job. Press BACK to the play screen, then press MENU.
MENU opens UTILITYYou held it. A short press opens MODS.
The button above LINK does nothingIt is set to NOTHING. Change it in MODS > PLAY > BUTTON ABOVE LINK.
SHIFT twice shows DECK 3 AND 4 NEED THE CH3/CH4 ROUTEDecks 3 and 4 are not connected. Open MODS > 4 DECKS.
The TEMPO slider does not change the deckPickup after a deck switch. Move the slider through the deck's tempo.
A key sync press shows a message on the deck's keySee Keys and KEY SYNC.
A BEAT JUMP pad shows JUMP UNAVAILABLESee When a jump is refused.

mods-menu.title: The MODS menu
mods-menu.html:
MODS is the menu XZ Mods adds to the player. Everything the mod can change lives here, sorted by what you want to do rather than by how the firmware is built. Both interfaces open the same menu, so what you learn here works in MODERN and CLASSIC. MODERN draws it in the FLAGSHIP look. CLASSIC draws it in the theme you chose.

Open and close MODS

Press MENU on the play screen. A short press opens MODS wherever the player's own firmware has no job for MENU, and leaves the stock job alone everywhere else. Hold MENU to open the player's own UTILITY, exactly as on a stock XDJ-XZ.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Press MENU
    3. Press MENU
    4. Tap CLOSE
Where you areShort press of MENU
The MODS menu is openCloses MODS
A game is on screenThe game's own key
The VJ.Tools view is on screenAs before
A menu, popup or dialog is openWorks or closes the open menu
A track list (browse, playlist, search, history)The sort menu or the track menu
TAG LISTLIST MENU
The play screen in GRID ADJUSTThe beat grid menu
The play screenOpens MODS experimental
The SOURCE screenOpens MODS experimental
The track INFO screenOpens MODS experimental
The SHORTCUT screenOpens MODS experimental
The player's own UTILITYCloses UTILITY
Any other screenThe screen's own job
Note

Rows marked experimental follow the XDJ-XZ operating instructions but have not been checked on every firmware version yet. If a press does something different on your player, report it github.com/OpticMystic/XZ-Mods/issues.

To leave MODS, press MENU again, tap CLOSE in the top right corner, or press BACK until you are back on the play screen.

You can also open MODS from the MODS button at the top of the MODERN play screen, or from the button above LINK when you set it to MODS MENU in PLAY.

Move around

You can drive the whole menu with the rotary encoder, with touch, or with both.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Push ROTARY SELECTOR to choose PLAY
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to GATE CUE and push it
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to SMART CUE and push it
    5. Press BACK
ControlWhat it does in MODS
Turn the encoderMoves the highlight to the next card, row or button
Push the encoderOpens or changes the highlighted item
BACKGoes up one level: from an open item to its page, then from a page to the section rail
TapOpens or changes whatever you tap

The hints in the bottom right corner (TURN MOVE · PUSH SELECT · BACK UP) always show what the encoder and BACK will do next.

Every page has the same frame. The section rail on the left lists HOME, PLAY, STEMS, SCREEN, 4 DECKS, CONNECT and EXTRAS. The dock along the bottom explains whatever is highlighted. On the right of the dock, WORKS ON shows which decks the highlighted feature works on, in mixer order 3 1 2 4. A dimmed number means the feature does not work on that deck, and a short amber line says why.

HOME

HOME is the first page. It shows one card for each section, with a one-line summary of what the section does and the current state of its most important setting, so you can see at a glance whether stems are ready or four decks are connected.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap HOME
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise
    4. Press BACK
CardIts status line shows
PLAYYour beat jump sizes, page 1 then page 2
STEMSNot set up, Off, or On with the state of deck 1 and deck 2
SCREENThe interface, the waveform colours and the key notation
4 DECKSNot connected, Looking for the cable, Starting decks 3 and 4, Ready with the deck view, Could not start, Disconnected, or Not available on this player
CONNECTYour DJ profile and its USB, and whether VJ.Tools is connected
EXTRASThe games and how many USB apps are on the stick

Two setup buttons can appear on HOME. SET UP USB STEMS opens the USB stems guide when the stem engine is not ready. SET UP FOUR DECKS opens 4 DECKS when no cable is found, a start failed, the cable was lost, or the USB loader has no four-deck engine.

PLAY

PLAY changes what the pads and buttons do while you perform.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise
    4. Press BACK

Beat jump and performance features explains every item on this page.

STEMS

STEMS mutes vocals, harmonics and drums from the pads or the screen.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap STEMS
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise
    4. Press BACK

STEMS IN DJ SOFTWARE sets up stems for a computer playing through the player. MODERN adds a BYPASS BUTTON switch beside STEM COLOURS. Stems explains every item on this page.

SCREEN

SCREEN sets how the play screen looks.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise
    4. Press BACK

Screen, interfaces and themes explains every item on this page. DECK VIEW is explained in Four decks.

4 DECKS

4 DECKS plays decks 3 and 4 over the loopback cable experimental.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap 4 DECKS
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise
    4. Press BACK

Four decks explains the cable, every state and what decks 3 and 4 can do.

CONNECT

CONNECT links the player to you and to computers.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap CONNECT
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise
    4. Press BACK

Connect and DJ profiles explains every page here.

EXTRAS

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap EXTRAS
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise
    4. Press BACK

Extras explains every page here.

UTILITY, the player's own settings

MENU held opens the player's own UTILITY: quantize, auto cue, play mode, the display and the other stock settings.

    1. Hold MENU for a second
    2. Push ROTARY SELECTOR
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    5. Press BACK
  • In CLASSIC you see the player's own UTILITY screen, unchanged.
  • In MODERN, XZ Mods draws UTILITY in the MODERN look. It is the same list of stock settings, in the stock order.
  • In MODERN, MODS also has a UTILITY cell at the bottom of the section rail. It closes MODS and opens UTILITY. Until MODERN has read the player's settings, it reads NOT READY.

MODERN UTILITY modern

    1. Press SHORTCUT
    2. Tap the screen
    3. Tap the screen

Turn the encoder to move through the settings. On a writable row, push to open its choices, turn to pick one and push to set it. A locked row stays in the list and shows a read-only value and explanation. BACK goes back to the list. MENU or X closes UTILITY.

A lock next to a setting comes with one of these notes:

NoteWhat it means
PLAYER CONTROLLEDThe player sets this itself. XZ Mods only shows it.
FIRMWARE LIMITXZ Mods cannot read or set it on this firmware version.
READ-ONLY BUILDA RAM trial shows settings but changes none. Start from the USB loader to change them.
READ ONLY HEREXZ Mods shows this setting but cannot change it here.

Pushing a locked setting does nothing.

MY SETTINGS modern

MY SETTINGS shows the player settings saved on a USB stick, and the DJ profiles on it. In MODERN, open the stick in browse, highlight the category rail on the left, and press MENU.

    1. Press BROWSE
    2. Press MENU
    3. Tap the screen
    4. Tap the screen
    5. Tap the screen
    6. Tap the screen

Further down, WAVEFORM sets COLOR, POSITION, ZOOM, USB COLORS and the stem row layout. SAVED ON USB 1 lists the settings stored on the stick, which you can change there.

Saving to the USB

There is no save button in MODS. Every change saves on its own to the settings USB, the stick you browse. The settings live in the VJ.Tools folder on that stick, so they travel with you to another XZ running XZ Mods. When you browse a stick, the player takes that stick's settings. A stick with no settings, or with damaged ones, leaves the current settings as they are.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Tap CLASSIC
    4. Tap MODERN
    5. Press MENU

The XZ also remembers the last settings it applied. If you start it with no stick, it uses them.

The save state at the right of the dock says what happened to your last change:

Save stateWhat it means
SAVING...The change is being written.
SAVED TO USB 1 (or USB 2)The change is on the stick.
SAVED ON THIS XZ / NO USBNo stick is in. The change is kept on this XZ.
SAVED ON THIS XZ / USB CHANGEDThe settings stick changed. The change is kept on this XZ.
SAVED ON THIS XZ / USB PROFILE KEPTThe stick is locked. The change is kept on this XZ and the stick is left as it was.
USB REMOVED: SETTINGS KEPTYou pulled the settings stick. Nothing resets.
NOT SAVED TO USB 1: CHECK USBWriting failed. Check that the stick is in and not locked.
NOT SAVED: USB PROFILE KEPTThe stick is locked and the XZ could not keep the change either.
NO SETTINGS USB: CHANGES LAST UNTIL POWER OFF.Nothing can be saved. Your change works until you switch the player off.
NOT SAVED: CHANGES LAST UNTIL POWER OFF.This build does not save settings. Changes work until you switch the player off.

Lines that say NOT SAVED or NO SETTINGS USB show in amber. DJ profiles are not settings. They stay on the DJ's stick and never on the XZ. See Connect and DJ profiles.

Older pages

Earlier versions had GENERAL, CONTROLS, THEMES and SETTINGS pages in MODS. They are gone. Anything that pointed at them now opens the page that replaced them:

Old pageOpens
GENERALHOME
CONTROLSSTEM PADS, in STEMS
THEMESSCREEN
SETTINGSPLAY

performance.title: Beat jump and performance features
performance.html:
XZ Mods adds performance features to the pads and deck keys: two pages of beat jump sizes you choose, gate cue, smart cue, key shift and KEY SYNC, and RAM tracks. Their settings live on one MODS page, PLAY. Every change saves to your USB as you make it.

The PLAY page

Open MODS and choose PLAY in the section rail.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 3 clicks clockwise
    4. Press BACK

If the cue engine has not reported on this USB loader, GATE CUE and SMART CUE show as SET UP GATE CUE and SET UP SMART CUE instead of switches. See Feature setup.

Beat jump

In BEAT JUMP mode the eight pads form four pairs: A/B, C/D, E/F and G/H. The first pad of a pair jumps back, the second jumps forward, by the same number of beats. With a loop on, the loop moves by that amount instead.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Tap BEAT JUMP PADS
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise
    1. Press BEAT JUMP on the left deck
    2. Press pad A on the left deck
    3. Press pad B on the left deck
    4. Press pad C on the left deck
    5. Press pad D on the left deck
    6. Press pad E on the left deck
    7. Press pad F on the left deck
    8. Press pad G on the left deck
    9. Press pad H on the left deck
    10. Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press BEAT JUMP on the left deck
    11. Press pad A on the left deck
    12. Press pad B on the left deck
    13. Press pad C on the left deck
    14. Press pad D on the left deck
    15. Press pad E on the left deck
    16. Press pad F on the left deck
    17. Press pad G on the left deck
    18. Press pad H on the left deck

You get two pages of sizes:

PageHow you select itDefault sizes A/B, C/D, E/F, G/H
Page 1Press BEAT JUMP1, 2, 4, 8 beats
Page 2Hold SHIFT, press BEAT JUMP, let go of SHIFT16, 32, 64, 128 beats (4, 8, 16, 32 bars)
  1. Page 1 Press BEAT JUMP. With the default sizes the pairs A/B, C/D, E/F and G/H jump 1, 2, 4 and 8 beats. The first pad of a pair jumps back, the second forward.
  2. Page 2 Hold SHIFT, press BEAT JUMP, let go of SHIFT. The pairs jump 16, 32, 64 and 128 beats, and the pads light warm red and amber.
  3. With a loop on With a loop on, the loop moves by the jump instead.
  1. Press BEAT JUMP for page 1, or SHIFT + BEAT JUMP for page 2.
  2. Let go of SHIFT.
  3. Press a pad. The first pad of a pair jumps back, the second forward.

Each deck remembers its own page. Choosing another pad mode and coming back with BEAT JUMP gives page 1 again. On page 2 the pads light warm red and amber, so you can see which page you are on. SHIFT + pad keeps its stock job on decks 1 and 2.

Change the jump sizes

Open MODS > PLAY > BEAT JUMP PADS. The editor shows the pads as they sit on the deck: A to D on top, E to H below.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Tap BEAT JUMP PADS
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to PAGE 2 and push it
    5. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to PAGE 1 and push it
    6. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to PAGE 1: MY SIZES and push it
    7. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to PAGE 2 and push it
  1. Choose PAGE 1 or PAGE 2.
  2. For page 1, choose PAGE 1: MY SIZES. With STOCK, page 1 keeps the player's own sizes.
  3. Tap a pad in the pair you want to change.
  4. Tap a size in the row along the bottom.

Without the touch screen, turn the rotary selector to a pair, push it, then turn to step the size. It stops at the smallest and largest size. Push or press BACK when you are done.

Sizes you can choose
Beats1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256
Bars1/4, 1/2, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64

The sizes apply to every deck. UTILITY's own beat jump setting is separate and does not change them.

SettingChoicesDefault
PAGE 1STOCK, MY SIZESMY SIZES
Page 1 A/B, C/D, E/F, G/H1 to 256 beats1, 2, 4, 8 beats
Page 2 A/B, C/D, E/F, G/H1 to 256 beats16, 32, 64, 128 beats

Decks 3 and 4

Decks 3 and 4 use the same sizes and both pages. They jump along the track's beat grid, or by its BPM when there is no grid. A track with neither jumps at 120 BPM, as on decks 1 and 2. With a loop on, the loop moves.

When a jump is refused

A jump the deck cannot make does nothing else. XZ Mods never silently shortens the selected distance. The screen shows why:

    1. Press BEAT JUMP on the left deck
    2. Press pad A on the left deck
NoticeDeckWhat it means
JUMP UNAVAILABLE: TRACK EDGE, BUFFER OR DECK STATE1 or 2The player refused the jump. It would pass the start or end of the track, or the deck cannot jump right now.
JUMP UNAVAILABLE: BEFORE TRACK START3 or 4The jump would land before the start of the track.
JUMP UNAVAILABLE: AFTER TRACK END3 or 4The jump would land after the end of the track.
JUMP UNAVAILABLE: LOOP MOVE OUT OF TRACK3 or 4Moving the loop would push it past the start or end.
JUMP UNAVAILABLE: NO BEAT GRID OR BPM3 or 4The track's beat grid is damaged, so beats can't be counted. Analyse it again in your DJ software.

Gate cue and smart cue

Both change what a hot cue pad does in HOT CUE mode. Turn them on in MODS > PLAY. Both are off by default, and each works on its own.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Tap GATE CUE
    4. Tap SMART CUE
    5. Tap CLOSE
    6. Press HOT CUE on the left deck
    7. Press pad A on the left deck
FeatureWhat a hot cue pad does
GATE CUEThe track plays from the hot cue only while you hold the pad. Let go and it jumps back to the hot cue and pauses. Use it to stab hot cues like samples. Press PLAY/PAUSE while you hold the pad to keep playing after you let go.
SMART CUECalling a hot cue also moves the CUE point there, so CUE takes you back to the last hot cue you used. Recording a new hot cue does not move it.

Gate cue and smart cue work on all four decks. On decks 1 and 2 they need the cue engine; see below.

Feature setup

When the cue engine has not reported on a deck, MODS shows a short setup instead of the switch. It checks the feature on a loaded USB track in four steps: detect, choose deck, enable and test.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Tap SET UP GATE CUE
    4. Tap DETECT FEATURE
    5. Tap DETECT FEATURE
    6. Tap USE SELECTED DECK
    7. Tap ENABLE FEATURE
    8. Tap I TESTED IT / DONE
  1. Load a track from USB on deck 1 or deck 2.
  2. Press DETECT FEATURE.
  3. Choose the deck, then enable the feature.
  4. Close MODS and test it: hold and release a hot cue for gate cue, or call a hot cue and check that the cue point follows for smart cue.
  5. Reopen the setup and confirm.

If the status still asks you to load a USB track while one is loaded, prepare the USB again with the current XZ Mods app.

Keys and KEY SYNC

XZ Mods can move the key of any deck a semitone at a time, and match a deck's key to the master deck with KEY SYNC. The master can be any deck, 1 to 4. The key display then shows the key the track plays in now.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Tap KEYS
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise
    1. Hold SHIFT on the left deck and press SYNC on the left deck

From the deck

  1. Load tracks with analysed keys, and make the deck you want to match to the tempo master.
  2. Hold SHIFT and press SYNC on the deck you want to move. On a side that drives deck 3 or 4, this moves that deck.
  3. The deck shifts to a key that fits the master deck and MASTER TEMPO turns on. A notice shows the new key and the master deck, with RELATIVE KEY when it matches the relative major or minor.

To end KEY SYNC, press SHIFT + SYNC again, or press MASTER TEMPO. Both return the deck to its own key and put MASTER TEMPO back the way it was. After that, MASTER TEMPO works as on a stock player.

KEY SYNC changes the key only. The tempo, SYNC and the master deck stay as they were.

All four decks can hold key shifts and KEY SYNC together. Before starting a new shift on deck 3 or 4, the player checks its measured audio workload. If there is too little headroom, it shows KEY SHIFT REFUSED: AUDIO LOAD TOO HIGH and leaves the current keys unchanged. Shifts already in use keep running. SYSTEM READOUT shows render times and the number of active key shifters.

If KEY SYNC cannot work, a notice or the deck's key display shows why for a few seconds:

MessageWhat to do
KEY ENGINE OFF: SET UP KEYSThis USB loader has no key engine. Open MODS > PLAY > KEYS and press SET UP KEYS, or prepare the USB again with the current XZ Mods app.
DECK 1 TRACK HAS NO KEY (or another deck)The track on this deck has no analysed key. Analyse it in your DJ software.
LOAD AN ANALYZED TRACK / SET UP KEYSThe deck has no track with an analysed key. Load one.
LOAD A KEYED TRACK ON DECK 2 (or another deck)The master deck has no track with an analysed key.
THIS DECK IS MASTER, MAKE DECK 2 MASTER FIRSTThe deck you pressed is the master, so there is nothing to match. Make another deck the master. On the KEYS page the master deck has no KEY SYNC button and says it is the master.
SELECT ONE LOCAL MASTER / SET UP KEYSNo deck on this player is the tempo master. Press MASTER on the deck to match to.
VERIFY MASTER PLAYING KEY / SET UP KEYSThe master deck's playing key is not known yet. Let it play a moment, then try again.
MASTER CHANGED / RETRY KEY SYNC, TRACK CHANGED / RETRY KEY CONTROLThe master or the track changed before the key moved. Press again.
KEY SHIFT REFUSED: AUDIO LOAD TOO HIGHMeasured audio work leaves too little headroom for a new shift. Existing shifts keep running. Check SYSTEM READOUT and retry when the load falls.
SHIFT OUT OF RANGE, KEY RANGE IS -12 TO +12 SEMITONESThe key that fits is further away than the deck can shift.
EMERGENCY LOOP / LOAD NEXT TRACKThe deck lost its track and loops. Load another track first.

The KEYS page

MODS > PLAY > KEYS does the same from the screen, and adds key shift by semitones. On the play screen, tapping a deck's key opens the same controls for that deck.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Tap KEYS
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY UP and push it
    5. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY DOWN and push it
    6. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to RESET and push it
    7. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY SYNC and push it

With MASTER TEMPO on, the key holds while the tempo moves. Without it, the tempo changes the key too, and the key display shows that.

When the key engine has not reported, the buttons show an amber dot, the dock says NOT READY and SET UP KEYS appears. It opens a short setup that checks the key engine and the chosen deck's track, and ends with a live test:

The key on the MODERN play screen modern

In MODERN each deck's panel beside its waveform shows its key. With PLAYING KEY on, the big key is the key the track plays in now, after tempo and key shift.

Part of the key panelMeaning
KEY SYNCKEY SYNC holds on this deck.
The big keyThe key the deck plays in now. Green or amber compares it with the master deck's key; see Key and KEY SYNC.
+12¢Cents between the playing key and the nearest semitone.
ORIGINALThe track's own key, shown when the playing key differs.
▲1The key shift in semitones, on older USB loaders that do not report the analysed key.

The key on the CLASSIC play screen classic

In CLASSIC, XZ Mods draws the playing key where the player shows its beat countdown, under the key:

What you seeMeaning
KEY and a keyThe track plays in its own key.
TRACK KEYDeck 3 or 4 shows the track's own key until it reports the key it plays in.
Own key ▸ playing keyThe tempo or a key shift moved the key.
SYNCKEY SYNC holds on this deck. The tile turns green while the key matches the master.
MASTERThis deck is the master that KEY SYNC matches to.
+12c in amberCents between the playing key and the nearest semitone.
Green or amber keyThe playing key compared with the master deck's key, as KEY MATCH COLOURS sets it.
A message in redKEY SYNC could not work; see the table above.

PLAYING KEY

PLAYING KEY is on by default. Turn it off in MODS > SCREEN to show the track's own key instead. In CLASSIC, off brings the beat countdown back. Key notation (AS ON THE USB, MUSICAL or WHEEL) is set on the same page; see Screen, interfaces and themes.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Tap PLAYING KEY
    4. Tap PLAYING KEY
    5. Tap KEY MATCH COLOURS
    6. Tap KEY BEFORE TITLE
    7. Tap CLOSE

Decks 3 and 4 show their playing key too, after tempo and key shift. Until a software deck reports it, the deck shows the track's own key.

RAM tracks experimental

RAM TRACKS copies the track on a deck into the player's memory. The deck then plays from memory, so it keeps playing if the music USB goes out. It works on all four decks. Decks 3 and 4 need the loopback cable connected to start a copy.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Tap RAM TRACKS
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to LOAD TRACK INTO RAM and push it
  1. Load a track from USB on the deck.
  2. Open MODS > PLAY > RAM TRACKS and choose that deck.
  3. Press LOAD TRACK INTO RAM. Keep the USB connected while it copies.
  4. Wait for ORIGINAL AUDIO IN RAM.

A track that plays is also copied on its own when there is room. CANCEL COPY or RELEASE RAM COPY stops that for the loaded track.

StateButtonWhat it means
RAM ENGINE NOT DETECTEDSET UP RAM TRACKSThis USB loader has no RAM engine, or it has not reported yet. The setup checks the engine. If it stays, prepare the USB again with the current XZ Mods app.
LOOPBACK CABLE NOT CONNECTEDSET UP FOUR DECKSDeck 3 or 4 is chosen and decks 3 and 4 are not running. The button opens 4 DECKS.
NOT IN RAMLOAD TRACK INTO RAMThe deck plays from USB.
COPYING TO RAMCANCEL COPYThe copy is running. Cancel leaves the track playing from USB.
ORIGINAL AUDIO IN RAMRELEASE RAM COPYThe deck plays from memory. Release frees the memory and needs the USB still connected.
COPY FAILEDRETRY LOAD INTO RAMThe track keeps playing from USB. Retry; if it fails again, load the track again from USB.
USB OUT / RAM COPY ONLYBACK TO PLAYThe USB is out and the deck plays from memory. The play screen says so in the deck's lane; see below. Load another track to release the copy.

When a copy does not fit, the page says why and offers the next step:

MessageWhat to do
This file exceeds the 64 MiB RAM limit.Press CHOOSE ANOTHER TRACK.
Other RAM tracks leave too little space for this file.Press MANAGE RAM TRACKS, choose a deck with a copy and release it.
Free RAM cannot keep the 64 MiB safety reserve.Release another copy the same way.
  • One track per deck. Each file can be up to 64 MiB, and all four decks together up to 128 MiB. The player always keeps 64 MiB of its memory free.
  • RAM TRACKS copies the original audio. On decks 1 and 2, the line under the action button says what else is held; see the table below.
  • On decks 3 and 4 the waveform, beat grid and cues already loaded stay with the copy when the USB goes out. Cues you change then are kept for the session and not written to a USB.
  • If the loopback cable goes out, decks 3 and 4 keep their copies and pause, as they do without RAM. They do not start again on their own when the cable returns.
  • Loading another track on the deck drops its RAM copy.

When the music USB goes out experimental

    1. Press BROWSE
    2. Push ROTARY SELECTOR
    3. Press LOAD 1
  1. NOT IN RAM The deck plays from USB.
  2. COPYING TO RAM Press LOAD TRACK INTO RAM. Keep the USB connected while it copies.
  3. ORIGINAL AUDIO IN RAM The deck plays from memory.
  4. USB OUT / RAM COPY ONLY The music USB goes out and the deck plays on from memory. A teal card, WHOLE TRACK IN RAM · PLAYABLE, takes the waveform's place and says how to get it back.

A deck with its whole track in RAM keeps playing when the music USB goes out. The waveform was read from the USB, so the deck's lane cannot draw it any more. A teal card takes its place: WHOLE TRACK IN RAM · PLAYABLE, and under it how to get the waveform back.

Everything else about the deck stays on screen: title and artist, time and remain, BPM, tempo, key, the lamps, the hot cues and the playhead.

To get the waveform back, reinsert the same USB or insert another, then load a track from it. The card goes as soon as the deck has a waveform to draw again. Loading a track also ends the deck's RAM copy, as it always does.

On decks 3 and 4 the waveform loaded before the USB went out stays, so the card shows there only if the waveform had not loaded yet.

Line under the button, decks 1 and 2What it means
COPIES AUDIO / STEMS STAY ON USBNo copy yet. RAM TRACKS copies the audio, not the stems.
AUDIO IN RAM / STEMS NEED USBThe audio is in RAM. The stems still read the USB.
AUDIO + STEMS IN RAM / WAVES KEPTThe deck's prepared stems are held in RAM as well, and the loaded waveforms stay.
Experimental

Playing on from RAM after the USB goes out has not been confirmed on a player yet. Keep the USB in during a set.

Quantize

On decks 1 and 2, quantize is the player's own: DECK QUANTIZE and UTILITY work as on a stock player. In MODERN each deck shows its QUANTIZE lamp and beat value above its time. You can hide them in MODS > SCREEN > LAMPS AND TITLES.

    1. Press DECK QUANTIZE
    2. Press DECK QUANTIZE

While a side drives deck 3 or 4:

KeyAction
DECK QUANTIZESwitches quantize for every deck. Decks 1 and 2 switch through the player as before.
SHIFT + DECK QUANTIZESwitches quantize only for the deck of that side.

With quantize on, decks 3 and 4 put cue points, loop in and out, hot cues and beat and slip loops on the beat grid, at a one-beat value. SYNC then also locks the deck to the master's beat. Four decks has the rest of what decks 3 and 4 do.

play-screen.title: The play screen
play-screen.html:
The play screen is where you spend the set. XZ Mods gives you two ways to draw it. MODERN replaces the whole screen with its own layout. CLASSIC keeps the player's own screen and adds a row of buttons, the playing key and the stem rows to it. You choose between them in MODS under SCREEN (see Screen, interfaces and themes).

The MODERN play screen modern

MODERN draws every deck the same way: a top bar across the screen, one waveform lane per deck with a narrow info column on its left, a row of hot-cue lamps, and a deck strip at the bottom. Two decks share the screen in halves. For four decks, see Four decks.

    1. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 6 clicks clockwise
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 6 clicks anticlockwise
    3. Tap TIME 1
    4. Tap TIME 1
    5. Tap INFO HEADER
    6. Press BACK

Top bar modern

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    3. Tap STEMS HEADER
    4. Tap STEMS HEADER

A lamp label in grey shows a mode the player does not let XZ Mods change from the screen. Change it in the player's own UTILITY instead (hold MENU). You can hide the three lamps in MODS under SCREEN, LAMPS AND TITLES. The BEAT FX readout then takes their room.

Deck column and waveform lanes modern

Turn the rotary encoder on the play screen to zoom both lanes together. There are seven zoom steps. The zoom is kept when you leave the screen, and saved to the USB with your other settings.

Deck strip modern

In the last 30 seconds of a track the overview's playing address flashes slowly, and in the last 15 seconds it flashes fast, in either time mode.

Key and KEY SYNC modern

The large key in each deck's column is the key the deck plays right now. Tempo with MASTER TEMPO off, a key shift and KEY SYNC all move it. Its colour compares it with the master deck's key. Green means it mixes with the master's key: the same key, its relative major or minor, or one step away on the key wheel, tuned within 25 cents of the master. Amber means it would mix, but it is detuned by more than 25 cents. White means neither, and the master deck itself is always white. Turn KEY MATCH COLOURS off in SCREEN and every key is white. The cents beside it show how far it sits off the semitone, so you can match by ear. Once the playing key leaves the track's analysed key, ORIGINAL shows the analysed key below it.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap PLAY
    3. Tap KEYS
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY UP and push it
    5. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY DOWN and push it
    6. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to RESET and push it
    7. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR to KEY SYNC and push it

While KEY SYNC holds a deck's key, the KEY caption becomes a blue KEY SYNC chip and the deck's MT lamp blinks, half a second lit and half a second dark.

You choose how keys are written (as on the USB, musical or wheel numbers) and whether the playing key shows at all in MODS under SCREEN. See Screen, interfaces and themes.

Waveform colours modern

MODS under SCREEN offers four waveform colours for MODERN. They change the lanes and the overviews together. Your choice is saved to the USB. 3-BAND COLOURS, beside LAMPS AND TITLES, changes the colour of each band; see 3-band colours.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Tap STOCK
    4. Tap RGB
    5. Tap 3-BAND
    6. Tap STEMS
    7. Tap LAMPS AND TITLES
    8. Tap MODE LAMPS
    9. Tap QUANTIZE LAMP
    10. Tap TITLES IN WAVEFORMS
    11. Tap DECK + WAVE
    12. Tap DECK ONLY
    13. Tap OFF
    14. Tap CLOSE
ChoiceWhat you see
STOCKOne blue waveform with white peaks
RGBLows red, mids green, highs blue
3-BANDLows blue, mids amber, highs white, or the colours you chose in 3-BAND COLOURS
STEMSDrums, harmonics and vocals in their stem colours. A track without stems shows 3-BAND

USB COLORS (MODS, SCREEN, LAMPS AND TITLES) lets each deck take the colours saved on the USB stick its track came from.

Notices modern

When something you asked for does not happen, a notice appears in the middle of the screen for two and a half seconds. It says what went wrong in one line, for example DECK 1 DID NOT LOAD THE TRACK. A long notice wraps. Messages and troubleshooting explains each one.

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    3. Tap CHOOSE TRACK
    4. Push ROTARY SELECTOR
    5. Tap TRACK ROW
    6. Tap LOAD DECK 3

If a deck cannot go on, its lane turns red and names the problem, for example EMERGENCY LOOP (the deck loops until you load a track) or CANNOT READ THE TRACK with the player's error code. Tap CHOOSE TRACK on the red band to make that deck active and open BROWSE.

A deck that plays its whole track from RAM after the music USB went out is not in trouble, so its lane says so in teal instead: WHOLE TRACK IN RAM · PLAYABLE, in the waveform's place. See RAM tracks.

SHORTCUT modern

Press SHORTCUT on the play screen to see the settings you change most during a set on one page. It has the same four groups as the player's own SHORTCUT screen: PLAYER SETTINGS, DECK STATUS, DEVICE SETTINGS and MY SETTINGS. Press BACK or tap the arrow in the top left corner to return to the play screen.

    1. Press SHORTCUT
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    3. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    4. Press BACK

Which rows you can change depends on what the player lets XZ Mods write. A locked row shows its value and the reason it is read-only. A short MENU on SHORTCUT opens MODS.

NEEDLE LOCK appears in PLAYER SETTINGS when the player reports it. LOCK prevents a waveform touch from searching a playing deck. Pause the deck to search, or choose UNLOCK when that setting is writable.

With four decks, SHORTCUT also shows DECK SELECT. See Four decks.

The CLASSIC play screen classic

CLASSIC keeps the player's own play screen, so every stock element stays where the XDJ-XZ operating instructions put it. XZ Mods restyles it in the classic theme you chose and adds a row of buttons across the top, the playing key under each deck's key, and stem rows under the waveforms.

    1. Tap the screen
    2. Tap the screen
    3. Tap the screen

This picture is the stock screen of a real player with the XZ Mods buttons and stem rows added. Everything else on it is the player's own: the deck tabs, source, key, BEAT FX, ZOOM, the deck strips with A.HOTCUE, A.CUE, QUANTIZE, TEMPO and the BPM box. The XDJ-XZ operating instructions explain those.

The key line replaces the player's beat countdown under the key. You choose the key notation and whether the playing key shows in MODS under SCREEN.

Scrolling waveform classic

In CLASSIC, SCREEN offers three scrolling waveforms. The setting is wave_mode on the USB.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Tap CLASSIC
    4. Tap 2 DECKS
    5. Tap 4 DECKS
    6. Tap 4 DECKS
    7. Tap STOCK
    8. Tap 3-BAND
    9. Tap STEMS
    10. Tap AS ON THE USB
    11. Tap MUSICAL
    12. Tap WHEEL
    13. Tap PLAYING KEY
    14. Tap KEY MATCH COLOURS
    15. Tap KEY BEFORE TITLE
    16. Tap CLOSE
ChoiceWhat you see
STOCKThe player's own scrolling waveform
3-BANDLayered lows, mids and highs (the default). 3-BAND COLOURS chooses their colours; see 3-band colours
STEMSDrums, harmonics and vocals layered in their stem colours. A track without prepared stems shows 3-BAND

The overview in each deck strip stays the player's own in every choice.

When a deck plays its whole track from RAM after the music USB went out, a teal card in its lane says WHOLE TRACK IN RAM · PLAYABLE where the waveform was. See RAM tracks.

If something looks wrong

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Tap PLAYING KEY
    4. Tap PLAYING KEY
    5. Tap KEY MATCH COLOURS
    6. Tap KEY BEFORE TITLE
    7. Tap CLOSE
You seeWhyWhat to do
Dashes instead of numbersThe value has not been read yet, or the deck has no trackWait a moment, or load a track
A grey mode lamp that does not reactThe player does not let XZ Mods change that modeChange it in UTILITY (hold MENU)
NO STEM WAVE YET · 3BAND in a laneSTEMS waveform chosen, but this track's stems are not loaded yetWait, or prepare the track's stems. See Stems
The key stays white on every deckNo master deck, or KEY MATCH COLOURS is offSet a tempo master, or turn KEY MATCH COLOURS on in SCREEN

screen-and-themes.title: Screen, interfaces and themes
screen-and-themes.html:
SCREEN is the MODS section for how the player looks. Here you choose between the MODERN and CLASSIC interfaces, pick a theme, set the waveform colours and the 3-band colours, and decide how keys are written. Nothing on this page changes how a track sounds.

Open MODS with MENU, then choose SCREEN in the section rail.

The SCREEN page

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Tap 2 DECKS
    4. Tap 4 DECKS
    5. Tap 4 DECKS
    6. Tap STOCK
    7. Tap RGB
    8. Tap 3-BAND
    9. Tap STEMS
    10. Tap AS ON THE USB
    11. Tap MUSICAL
    12. Tap WHEEL
    13. Tap PLAYING KEY
    14. Tap KEY MATCH COLOURS
    15. Tap KEY BEFORE TITLE
ControlChoicesWhat it changes
INTERFACECLASSIC, MODERNWho draws the play screen. See MODERN and CLASSIC
DECK VIEW2 DECKS, 4 DECKS in number order, 4 DECKS in mixer orderWhich decks the play screen shows. Sound and controls do not change. Hidden on a player that cannot run decks 3 and 4
THEME (CLASSIC)24 classic themesThe look of the player's own screen and of MODS
LAMPS AND TITLES (MODERN)A page of switchesWhich parts of the MODERN play screen you see
3-BAND COLOURSA page of coloursThe colours of the lows, mids and highs in every 3-BAND waveform. See 3-band colours
WAVEFORM COLOURSSTOCK, 3-BAND, STEMS (MODERN adds RGB)The colours of the scrolling waveforms
KEY NOTATIONAS ON THE USB, MUSICAL, WHEELHow keys are written
PLAYING KEYON, OFFThe key a track plays in now, or its original key
KEY MATCH COLOURSON, OFFGreen or amber keys on the play screen and in the track list
KEY BEFORE TITLEON, OFFThe key in front of each title in the track list
TRACK LIST COLUMNSInformation onlyTap a column title in the track list, or press MENU there, to choose its columns and sort
SYSTEM READOUTOpens its setupCPU, RAM and temperature on the top bar. It has the last row of the page to itself

The HOME card for SCREEN sums the page up in one line, for example Classic | 3-band | Am keys.

MODERN and CLASSIC

XZ Mods gives the player two interfaces. You choose one with INTERFACE on the SCREEN page, or when you prepare the USB in the XZ Mods app. MODERN is the default.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Tap CLASSIC
    4. Tap MODERN
    1. Press the button above LINK
    2. Press the button above LINK
  • MODERN is a full-screen layout drawn by XZ Mods, with bigger waveforms and a browse sidebar.
  • CLASSIC keeps the player's own play screen and adds MODS to it. The classic themes restyle that screen.
MODERNCLASSIC
Play screenDrawn by XZ Mods, full screenThe XDJ-XZ's own layout, restyled
ThemesOne look, STANDARD. MODS is drawn in FLAGSHIP24 themes. MODS is drawn in the theme you pick
Waveform coloursSTOCK, RGB, 3-BAND, STEMSSTOCK, 3-BAND, STEMS
Lamps and titlesEach part can be shown or hiddenNot available
Playing keyShown as the big key in each deck's columnShown where the beat countdown sits
Stem buttonsSix places, including small buttons beside the hot cuesFive places
BrowseThe XZ Mods browser with a sidebar. See Browsing and loadingThe player's own browser

Each interface keeps its own theme. If you switch from CLASSIC to MODERN and back, your classic theme comes back with you.

To switch without opening MODS, press the button above LINK. Out of the box it switches between MODERN and CLASSIC. You can give it another job in PLAY › BUTTON ABOVE LINK. See Controls on the player.

Classic themes classic

A classic theme restyles the player's own play screen and the MODS menu: artwork, text, waveforms, cue marks and dialogs. Track positions, numbers and touch areas stay where the player puts them, so a theme never moves a control under your finger.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap SCREEN
    3. Tap CLASSIC
    4. Tap THEME
    5. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise, then push it

  • Stem colours are separate. Set them in STEMS › STEM COLOURS.

Keys

Key notation

ChoiceExampleWhen to use it

Playing key

With PLAYING KEY on, each deck shows the key the track plays in now, after tempo changes and key shifts. The original key and the offset in cents sit beside it.

  • In MODERN the playing key is the big key in each deck's column. Off shows the track's original key there.
  • In CLASSIC the playing key sits where the beat countdown is. Off brings the countdown back.
  • Decks 3 and 4 show their playing key too. Until a software deck reports it, the deck shows the track's own key, marked TRACK KEY in CLASSIC.

The key readout and Key Sync are explained in The play screen and Beat jump and performance features.

Key match colours and key before title

KEY MATCH COLOURS colours keys green or amber by how well they mix with the master deck, in the track list and on the play screen. Green means the key mixes with the master's key and sits within 25 cents of it. Amber means it would mix, but it is detuned by more than 25 cents. KEY BEFORE TITLE puts the key in front of each title in the track list. See Browsing and loading.

Deck colours

When a screen names a deck, it draws the deck number in a small badge. The badge tells you the deck by its digit and the pair by its colours.

No deck owns a colour. Blue and pale blue mark the deck a side of the player controls. Amber, red, green, the waveform bands and USB colours keep their own meanings. The WORKS ON row in the MODS dock uses the same badges, in mixer order 3 1 2 4. See Four decks for the deck view.

System readout

SYSTEM READOUT puts CPU load, memory and temperature beside STEMS and MODS on the top bar. Open it to see deck 3 and 4 audio render times and active key shifters across all four decks. P99 is the time at or below which 99% of the last 256 rendered blocks finished; MAX is the longest. Short blocks are scaled to a full block. D3+D4 MAX adds both maxima and compares them with the 5,805 microseconds available per block. New shifts use a stricter 3,483 microsecond budget, leaving time for other work. These render numbers include decoding, time stretch and key shift; they do not measure the complete output path. Use them when you suspect the player is working hard, for example with stems on both decks and four decks running.
