settings.title: Settings reference
settings.html:
XZ Mods keeps its settings on your USB, so they travel with you from player to player. This page explains where they are kept and what happens when the USB changes, then lists every setting with its values, its default and the chapter that explains it.

Where settings are kept

Your settings live in one file on the USB: VJ.Tools/XZ-Mods.cfg. You change them in MODS, or on your computer with the XZ Mods app. There is no save button. Every change saves on its own to the USB you are browsing, and the bottom of the MODS page says what happened for a few seconds.

MessageMeaning
SAVED TO USB 1 (or USB 2)The change is on that USB.
NOT SAVED TO USB 1: CHECK USBThe USB could not be written. Check that it is not full or locked, then change the setting again.
SAVED ON THIS XZ / NO USBNo USB is in. The change is kept on this player only.
USB REMOVED: SETTINGS KEPTYou pulled the USB. The player keeps your settings for the rest of the set.
USB 1 HAS NO SETTINGS: KEPT CURRENTThe USB you browsed has no settings file. The player keeps the settings it has.
USB 1 SETTINGS INVALID: KEPT CURRENTThe settings file on that USB could not be read. The player keeps the settings it has.
NOT SAVED: CHANGES LAST UNTIL POWER OFF.This start of XZ Mods cannot save. Your changes work until you switch the player off.

When the USB changes

The player follows the same rules as its own MY SETTINGS:

  • Browsing a USB in USB 1 or USB 2 loads that USB's settings. Browsing a computer or a LINK source never changes them.
  • A USB without settings, or with settings the player cannot read, leaves your current settings as they are. Nothing resets to defaults in the middle of a set.
  • The player remembers the last settings it used. Started without a USB, it uses those. A USB with its own settings takes over again once you browse it.

The player's own MY SETTINGS, which your DJ software writes to the USB, are a separate set. XZ Mods settings never change them, and loading MY SETTINGS does not change XZ Mods settings.

MODERN's own display choices are settings too: its waveform colour, waveform position and zoom, how it writes keys, the TRACK COLOURS choice, the LAMPS AND TITLES and BYPASS BUTTON switches, and the columns of its track list. So are the 3-band colours. They are saved to the USB with everything else and come back after the player restarts.

Things you do during a set, such as muting a stem, BYPASS, a key shift, KEY SYNC or a RAM copy, are not settings. They start fresh every time the player starts.

Going back to the defaults

There is no single button that resets every setting. Set each one back in MODS, using the Default column below. Some pages have their own way back: PAGE 1: STOCK for beat jump page 1, RESET STEM COLORS for the stem colours, and RESET 3-BAND COLOURS for the 3-band colours.

Note

Deleting the settings file from the USB does not reset anything. The player keeps the settings it has, and saves them to the USB again with your next change.

stems.title: Stems
stems.html:
Stems split a track into its parts so you can mute them live. XZ Mods plays three stems per track: VOCALS, HARMONICS (everything melodic that is not a voice) and DRUMS. You mute them from the pads or from buttons on the screen, change their levels by sliding, and switch back to the whole track with BYPASS. Stems work on decks 1 and 2. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems.

Note

MODERN labels the harmonics stem INST and the vocals stem VOCAL on its stem buttons. They are the same stems.

Prepare stems

The player cannot split a track itself. You prepare stems on your computer, once per track, and they travel on the USB beside your music.

  1. Prepare the stems in the XZ Mods app on your computer, or in OverCue Desktop. See The XZ Mods app.
  2. Keep the stems on the same USB as the music. Your original files and the library your DJ software exported stay unchanged.
  3. On the player, load the original track through the normal browser and wait a moment for its stems to load.

A track without prepared stems plays as normal. Its stem buttons say why, and the button at their end tells you what to do (see Stem readiness).

Turn stems on

Open MODS, choose STEMS on the section rail, and turn USB STEMS on. It is on by default. With it off, every pad keeps its normal job and the stem buttons say STEMS ARE OFF or STEMS OFF.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap STEMS
    3. Tap USB STEMS
    4. Tap USB STEMS
    5. Tap CLOSE

Stem buttons on the play screen

Each deck gets three stem buttons and BYPASS. Tap a stem button to mute that stem, and tap it again to bring it back. A muted stem goes dark and keeps its level in its label.

    1. Tap STEMS HEADER
    2. Tap STEMS HEADER
    3. Tap STEMS HEADER
    4. Tap STEMS HEADER
    5. Tap STEMS HEADER
    6. Tap STEMS HEADER

MODERN stem buttons modern

    1. Tap DRUMS
    2. Tap BYPASS
    3. Tap BYPASS

On full-height rows each stem button is also a fader. Put a finger on it and slide right to raise the level or left to lower it. One button's width covers the whole range. A tap without a slide toggles the mute. Half-height rows and the small buttons beside the hot cues mute only.

In 2 DECKS, STEMS in the top bar steps through six layouts in this order: beside the hot cues, below each deck at full height, below at half height, at the outer edges at full height, at the outer edges at half height, and hidden. You can also pick one in MODS under STEMS. MODERN keeps its own layout (modern_stems), so switching to CLASSIC and back does not change it. The default is the small buttons beside the hot cues.

The marks under STEMS follow the same order, so the lit mark tells you the layout without looking at the decks.

BYPASS BUTTON in MODS under STEMS shows or hides the BYPASS button. Hidden, the stem buttons take its room and the pads still bypass.

If stems are off when you tap STEMS, the layout still changes, and a notice says STEM ROWS SHOW ONCE STEMS ARE ON IN MODS.

Stem buttons in 4 DECKS modern

In a 4 DECKS view the lanes are too short for the layouts, so STEMS is a switch there. One tap hides the stem buttons on every deck, and the screen says STEM BUTTONS HIDDEN. The next tap brings them back and says STEM BUTTONS SHOWN. STEMS is lit while they show and has no layout marks. Your 2 DECKS layout does not change, and XZ Mods saves the 4 DECKS choice on the USB separately.

    1. Tap DECKS
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise, then push it
    3. Tap STEMS HEADER
    4. Tap STEMS HEADER

A deck whose track has no prepared stems shows no stem buttons in 4 DECKS, and its waveform keeps the whole lane. The buttons appear when you load a track with stems. Decks 3 and 4 have no stems, so they never show stem buttons. Four decks has pictures.

CLASSIC stem rows classic

In CLASSIC the stem rows sit inside the player's own waveform area, one row per deck.

    1. Tap the screen
    2. Tap the screen
    3. Tap the screen

In 2 DECKS, the STEMS button in the top right corner of the play screen steps the rows through five layouts: BELOW / FULL, BELOW / HALF, OUTER / FULL, OUTER / HALF and HIDDEN, then back to BELOW / FULL. Its five marks show the current one. Half rows give each waveform more height. HIDDEN gives the player's waveforms their full size back while the stems keep playing. CLASSIC keeps its own layout (stems_overlay).

While four decks show in CLASSIC, no stem rows are drawn, and STEMS stays dark. A tap changes nothing and says STEM BUTTONS SHOW IN 2 DECKS VIEW. The layout comes back when you return to two decks.

Stem pads

The pads mute stems too, without looking at the screen. Open STEM PADS on the STEMS page.

    1. Press HOT CUE on the left deck
    2. Press pad A on the left deck
    3. Press pad B on the left deck
    4. Press pad C on the left deck
    5. Press pad D on the left deck
    6. Press pad A on the left deck

Mute and bypass are performance state. They are not saved, and every track starts with all stems playing.

Stem order

The order puts the stems where your fingers expect them. It changes the pads and the stem buttons on the screen together. There are six orders.

    2. Tap STEMS
    3. Tap USB STEMS
    4. Tap BY THE CUES

The layered STEMS waveform and the stem row for DJ software keep their own order.

Stem colours

Each stem has a colour on the pads, the stem buttons and the STEMS waveform. In the ORIGINAL theme drums are blue, harmonics red and vocals green. Every theme has its own shades.

The choices are THEME, BLUE, RED, GREEN, AMBER, PURPLE, CYAN, PINK and WHITE. A fixed colour stays when you change theme.

Stem readiness

Each deck's stem buttons tell you whether its stems can play. When they cannot, the stem buttons go dark and the last button names the reason. Where you can fix it from the player, that button does it.

In MODERN the stem buttons on a deck that cannot play stems read STEMS ARE OFF or NO STEMS ON THIS TRACK, and only the hot-cue lamps stay in the pad row. In 4 DECKS such a deck shows no stem buttons, and its waveform keeps the whole lane.

USB STEMS setup

Tap SET UP or HOW TO FIX on a stem row, or SET UP USB STEMS in MODS, to open USB STEMS setup. It checks one deck at a time and walks you through the three steps: check the engine, turn stems on, load a prepared track.

Stems in DJ software experimental

When the XZ plays from DJ software on a computer over USB, the stem buttons can switch the software's stems instead. Open STEMS IN DJ SOFTWARE on the STEMS page and follow its four steps for each deck: DETECT, MAP STEMS, LIVE TEST and CONFIRM.

troubleshooting.title: Messages and troubleshooting
troubleshooting.html:
This chapter lists every message XZ Mods can show you, what it means and the one thing to do about it. Find the words you see on the screen in the tables below. Messages in capitals come from the player. Messages in normal case come from the XZ Mods app on your computer.

If the player will not start with the USB

XZ Mods never changes the player's firmware, so the player always starts stock without the USB.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap CONNECT
    3. Tap UPDATES
    4. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 2 clicks clockwise
  1. Switch the player off.
  2. Remove the XZ Mods USB and switch the player on. It starts stock. Play from a stick without XZ Mods if you are in a set.
  3. On your computer, open the USB in the XZ Mods app. If it says Update available, choose Update USB. If it says Up to date, open Updates › XZ Mods version › Restore or update a loader by hand and update the loader again. The app keeps a backup of the old loader each time.
  4. Try the USB again. If it still does not start, report the problem.

Check these first:

CheckWhy
The player runs firmware 1.26XZ Mods supports no other firmware version
autoexec.bin is at the top of the USBA loader prepared into a folder has to be copied to the USB yourself
You updated the USB after updating the appAn app update does not change the USB

If XZ Mods started after a network update and stopped working, open CONNECT › UPDATES and push PREVIOUS VERSION, then switch the player off and on. See Updates over the network.

If the sound goes wrong while you test, stop playback and switch the player off and on. Load the same track again and check the original mix before you go on.

Tip

MODS is always reachable with the hardware alone. In CLASSIC, the button above LINK switches to MODERN, where MENU opens MODS. Turn the encoder to move, push it to choose and press BACK to go back.

Stems on the USB

When a deck cannot play stems, its stem row says why and its last button offers the next step. In CLASSIC the row sits under the deck's waveform. Open the button to see the deck's setup page in MODS.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap STEMS
    3. Tap SET UP USB STEMS
    4. Tap CHECK STEM ENGINE
    5. Tap CHECK THIS DECK AGAIN
    6. Tap CHECK THIS DECK AGAIN
    7. Tap STEMS READY / BACK TO PLAY
    8. Press MENU

Every state on both interfaces, with pictures, is in Stems.

Notices on the play screen modern

A notice is a short message in the middle of the lanes. It clears on its own after a few seconds, and the deck keeps playing.

    1. Press BROWSE
    2. Turn ROTARY SELECTOR 1 click clockwise
    3. Press LOAD 1

The player's own warnings

The player sometimes raises its own warning window, for example about a USB or a device. A warning never takes the screen or the controls away from XZ Mods.

  • MODERN. The play screen says the warning once, in the player's own words, for example E-8307: USB ACCESS ERROR. Browse, the decks and every control keep working.
  • MODS, in either interface. MODS stays open on the same page. The strip at the top of the dock turns red with the warning's code and text, and REPORT THIS. The strip goes when the warning does.
  • CLASSIC with MODS closed. The player's window shows as on a stock XDJ-XZ. Touches, keys and the encoder go to the player until it closes the window.

E-8307: HUBS ARE NOT SUPPORTED

The player sees the loopback cable for four decks as a hub. It raises E-8307: HUBS ARE NOT SUPPORTED or E-8307: UNSUPPORTED DEVICE and would keep it up while the cable is in. It is not an error. XZ Mods removes the window as soon as the player draws it, in MODERN, MODS and CLASSIC. See Four decks.

The diary on your USB sticks

XZ Mods keeps a short diagnostic diary in VJ.Tools/XZ-Mods-diary/ on each mounted USB stick, including music sticks. If a problem happens during a set, keep those sticks so you can include their diaries in a later report.

The diary records the XZ Mods version, settings fingerprint, USB slots, interface, deck view, state changes and fixed notice codes. It also records available CPU, memory, audio, SYNC, key-processing and USB-read measurements. It never records track titles, music paths, serial numbers or network identities. A missing measurement stays unknown.

Each stick holds at most 4 MiB of diary files. Older segments are replaced first, and the previous session's latest segment is kept when a new session starts. Writing pauses during track loads, RAM copies and heavy USB reads. No diary is created on a read-only stick or when less than 64 MiB of free space plus a small write reserve remains. Read-only test sessions save nothing. Normal USB-loader sessions write diary entries when these conditions allow it. Long busy periods and removal can leave gaps.

The diary stays on the sticks. Nothing is sent until you choose to include it in a report.

Report a problem

When something goes wrong, send a report. It helps fix the problem for everyone.

    1. Press MENU
    2. Tap REPORT THIS
    3. Tap SKIP, I'LL ADD IT ON MY COMPUTER
    4. Tap SEND REPORT
  • On the player. Open MODS › EXTRAS › REPORT AN ISSUE, or push REPORT THIS beside an error in the dock. Choose a topic, add words if you like, and send. Offline, the report waits on the stick for your computer. See Report an issue.
  • On your computer. In the XZ Mods app, open Feedback at the top right and choose Report a problem. Only one box is required, and My reports in Feedback shows where your report is afterwards. See Report a problem or share an idea.
  • On GitHub. Open an issue at https://github.com/OpticMystic/XZ-Mods/issues.

Say what you did, what you expected and what happened. The app adds the cleaned-up details itself, and you can see and untick each one. Nothing is sent until you press Send privately, and the app posts nothing publicly. From the player, the public GitHub issue is a separate step you submit yourself.
